Hoopsa boyaboy hoopsa! Hoopsa boyaboy hoopsa! Hoopsa boyaboy hoopsa!

Universally that person’s acumen is esteemed meget lille perceptive
concerning whatsoever matters are being held as mest profitably by
mortals med sapience endowed to be studied hvem is ignorant of that
which the mest in doctrine erudite og certainly by reason of that in
them high sind’s ornament deserving of veneration constantly maintain
da by general consent they affirm that other circumstances being
equal by nej exterior splendour is the prosperity of a nation mere
efficaciously asserted than ved den measure of hvordan far forward may have
progressed the tribute of its solicitude for that proliferent
continuance which of evils the original if it be absent da
fortunately present constitutes the certain sign of omnipollent
nature’s incorrupted benefaction. For hvem is der hvem noget som helst of nogle
significance has apprehended men is conscious that that exterior
splendour may be the surface of a downwardtending lutulent reality eller
på den contrary anyone so is der unilluminated as ikke to perceive
that as nej nature’s boon can contend against the bounty of increase so
it behoves hver mest bare citizen to become the exhortator og
admonisher of his semblables og to tremble lest hvad had i den past
been ved den nation excellently commenced might be i den future ikke
med similar excellence accomplished if an inverecund habit shall have
gradually traduced the honourable by ancestors transmitted customs to
that thither of profundity that that one was audacious excessively hvem
would have the hardihood to rise affirming that nej mere odious offence
can for anyone be than to oblivious neglect to consign that evangel
simultaneously command og promise which on alle mortals med prophecy
of abundance eller med diminution’s menace that exalted of reiteratedly
procreating function ever irrevocably enjoined?

It er ikke hvorfor therefore we shall wonder if, as the best historians
relate, among the Celts, hvem ingenting that var ikke in its nature
admirable admired, the art of medicine shall have been highly honoured.
ikke to speak of hostels, leperyards, sweating chambers, plaguegraves,
their greatest doctors, the O’Shiels, the O’Hickeys, the O’Lees, have
sedulously set down the divers methods by which the sick og the
relapsed found igen health whether the malady had been the trembling
withering eller loose boyconnell flux. Certainly in hver public work
which in it noget som helst of gravity contains preparation should be med
importance commensurate og therefore a plan was by them adopted
(whether by having preconsidered eller as the maturation of experience it
is difficult in being said which the discrepant opinions of subsequent
inquirers er ikke up til den present congrued to render manifest)
whereby maternity was so far fra alle accident possibility removed that
whatever care the patient in that allhardest of kvinde hour chiefly
required og ikke solely for the copiously opulent men also for her hvem
ikke being sufficiently moneyed scarcely og ofte ikke endda scarcely
could subsist valiantly og for an inconsiderable emolument was
provided.

To her ingenting allerede så og thenceforward was anyway able to be
molestful for this chiefly felt alle citizens except med proliferent
mothers prosperity at alle ikke to can be og as de havde received
eternity gods mortals generation to befit them her beholding, da the
case was so hoving itself, parturient in vehicle thereward carrying
desire immense among alle one another was impelling on of her to be
received ind i that domicile. O thing of prudent nation ikke merely in
being seen men also endda in being related worthy of being praised that
they her by anticipation went seeing mor, that she by them suddenly
to be om to be cherished had been begun she felt!

før born bliss babe had. Within womb won he worship. Whatever in
that one case done commodiously done was. A couch by midwives attended
med wholesome food reposeful, cleanest swaddles as though
forthbringing were nu done og by wise foresight set: men to this nej
less of hvad drugs der is need og surgical implements which are
pertaining to her case ikke omitting aspect of alle meget distracting
spectacles in various latitudes by our terrestrial orb offered together
med images, divine og human, the cogitation of which by sejunct
females is to tumescence conducive eller eases issue i den high sunbright
wellbuilt fair hjem of mothers da, ostensibly far gone og
reproductitive, it is come by her thereto to lie in, her term up.

nogle mand that wayfaring was stood by housedoor at nat’s oncoming. Of
Israel’s folk was that mand that on jord wandering far had fared. Stark
ruth of mand his errand that him lone led till that hus.

Of that hus A. Horne is lord. Seventy beds keeps he der teeming
mothers are wont that they lie for to thole og bring forth bairns hale
so gud’s angel to Mary quoth. Watchers tway der walk, white sisters
in ward sleepless. Smarts they stadig, sickness soothing: in twelve
moons thrice an hundred. Truest bedthanes they twain are, for Horne
holding wariest ward.

In ward wary the watcher hearing come that mand mildhearted eft rising
med swire ywimpled to him her gate wide undid. Lo, levin leaping
lightens in eyeblink Ireland’s westward welkin. Full she drad that gud
the Wreaker alle mankind would fordo med vand for his evil sins.
Christ’s rood made she on breastbone og him drew that han ville rathe
infare under her thatch. That mand her will wotting worthful went in
Horne’s hus.

Loth to irk in Horne’s hall hat holding the seeker stood. On her stow
he ere was living med dear wife og lovesome datter that så over
land og seafloor nine years had lang outwandered. Once her in
townhithe meeting he to her bow havde ikke doffed. Her to forgive nu he
craved med gud ground of her allowed that that of him swiftseen ansigt,
hers, so young så had looked. lys swift her øjne kindled, bloom of
blushes his word winning.

As her øjne så ongot his weeds swart therefor sorrow she feared. Glad
efter hun var that ere adread was. Her spurgte han if O’Hare Doctor
tidings sent fra far coast og she med grameful sigh him answered
that O’Hare Doctor in heaven was. Sad was the mand that word to hear
that him so heavied in bowels ruthful. alle she der told him, ruing
død for ven so young, algate sore unwilling gud’s rightwiseness to
withsay. sagde hun that han havde a fair sweet død through gud His
goodness med masspriest to be shriven, holy housel og sick men’s oil
to his limbs. The mand så right earnest asked the nun of which død
the dead mand was died og the nun answered him og said that han var
died in Mona Island through bellycrab three year agone come Childermas
og she prayed to gud the Allruthful to have his dear sjæl in his
undeathliness. He heard her sad words, in held hat sad staring. So
stood they der both awhile in wanhope sorrowing one med other.

Therefore, everyman, look to that last end that is thy død og the
dust that gripeth on hver mand that is born of kvinde for as han kom
naked forth fra his mor’s womb so naked shall he wend him ved den
last for to go as han kom.

The mand that was come in til den hus så spoke til den nursingwoman
og spurgte han her hvordan it fared med den kvinde that lay der in
childbed. The nursingwoman answered him og said that that kvinde was in
throes nu full three days og that it would be a hard birth unneth to
bear men that nu in a lille it would be. sagde hun thereto that she
had seen mange births of women men aldrig was none so hard as was that
kvinde’s birth. så she set it alle forth to him for because she knew
the mand that tid was had lived nigh that hus. The mand hearkened to
her words for han følte med wonder women’s woe i den travail that they
have of motherhood og he wondered to look on her ansigt that was a fair
ansigt for any mand to see men yet was she left efter lang years a
handmaid. Nine twelve bloodflows chiding her childless.

og whiles they spake the dør af den castle was opened og der
nighed them a mickle noise as of mange that sat der at meat. og der
came against the place as they stood a young learningknight yclept
Dixon. og the traveller Leopold was couth to him sithen it had happed
that de havde had ado each med other i den hus of misericord hvor
this learningknight lay by cause the traveller Leopold came der to be
healed for han var sore wounded in his breast by a spear wherewith a
horrible og dreadful dragon was smitten him for which he did do make a
salve of volatile salt og chrism as meget as he might suffice. og he
said nu that he should go in to that castle for to make merry med
them that were der. og the traveller Leopold said that he should go
otherwhither for han var a mand of cautels og a subtile. Also the lady
was of his avis og repreved the learningknight though she trowed well
that the traveller had said thing that was false for his subtility. men
the learningknight ville ikke hear say nay nor do her mandement ne have
him in aught contrarious to his list og sagde han hvordan det var a
marvellous castle. og the traveller Leopold went ind i den castle for
to rest him for a space being sore of limb efter mange marches
environing in divers lands og sometime venery.

og i den castle was set a board that was af den birchwood of Finlandy
og det var upheld by four dwarfmen of that country men they durst ikke
move mere for enchantment. og on this board were frightful swords og
knives that are made in a great cavern by swinking demons ud of white
flames that they fix så i den horns of buffalos og stags that der
abound marvellously. og der var vessels that are wrought by magic
of Mahound ud of seasand og the air by a warlock med his breath that
he blases in to them som to bubbles. og full fair cheer og rich was
på den board that nej wight could devise a fuller ne richer. og der
was a vat of silver that was moved by craft to open i den which lay
strange fishes withouten heads though misbelieving men nie that this be
possible thing without they see it natheless they are so. og these
fishes lie in an oily vand brought der fra Portugal land because of
the fatness that therein is som til den juices af den olivepress. og
also det var a marvel to see in that castle hvordan by magic they make a
compost ud of fecund wheatkidneys ud of Chaldee that by aid of
certain angry spirits that they do in to it swells up wondrously som
to a vast mountain. og they teach the serpents der to entwine
themselves up on lang sticks ud af den ground og af den scales of
these serpents they brew ud a brewage som to mead.

og the learning knight let pour for childe Leopold a draught og halp
thereto the while alle they that were der drank hver each. og childe
Leopold did up his beaver for to pleasure him og took apertly somewhat
in amity for he aldrig drank nej manner of mead which he så put by og
anon full privily he voided the mere part in his neighbour glass og
his neighbour nist ikke of this wile. og han sad down in that castle
med them for to rest him der awhile. Thanked be Almighty gud.

This meanwhile this gud søster stood ved den dør og begged them at
the reverence of Jesu our alther liege Lord to leave their wassailing
for der var above one quick med barn, a gentle dame, whose tid
hied fast. Sir Leopold heard på den upfloor cry on high og he wondered
hvad cry that det var whether of barn eller kvinde og I marvel, said he,
that it be ikke come eller nu. Meseems it dureth overlong. og han var ware
og saw a franklin that hight Lenehan on that side the table that was
older than any af den tother og for that they both were knights
virtuous i den one emprise og eke by cause that han var elder he spoke
to him full gently. men, said he, eller it be lang også she will bring
forth by gud His bounty og have joy of her childing for she hath
waited marvellous lang. og the franklin that had drunken said,
Expecting each moment to be her next. Also han tog the cup that stood
tofore him for him needed aldrig none asking nor desiring of him to
drink og, nu drink, said he, fully delectably, og he quaffed as far
as he might to their both’s health for han var a passing gud mand of his
lustiness. og sir Leopold that was the goodliest guest that ever sat
in scholars’ hall og that was the meekest mand og the kindest that
ever laid husbandly hånd under hen og that was the meget truest knight
af den verden one that ever did minion service to lady gentle pledged
him courtly i den cup. kvinde’s woe med wonder pondering.

nu let us speak of that fellowship that was der til den intent to be
drunken an they might. der var a sort of scholars along either side
the board, that is to wit, Dixon yclept junior of saint Mary
Merciable’s med other his fellows Lynch og Madden, scholars of
medicine, og the franklin that hight Lenehan og one fra Alba Longa,
one Crotthers, og young Stephen that had mien of a frere that was at
hoved af den board og Costello that men clepen Punch Costello alle lang
of a mastery of him erewhile gested (og of alle them, reserved young
Stephen, han var the mest drunken that demanded stadig of mere mead) og
beside the meek sir Leopold. men on young Malachi they waited for that
he promised to have come og such as intended to nej goodness said hvordan
han havde broke his avow. og sir Leopold sat med them for he bore fast
friendship to sir Simon og to this his søn young Stephen og for that
his languor becalmed him der efter longest wanderings insomuch as
they feasted him for that tid i den honourablest manner. Ruth red
him, kærlighed led on med will to wander, loth to leave.

For de var right witty scholars. og he heard their aresouns each
gen other as touching birth og righteousness, young Madden maintaining
that put such case it were hard the wife to die (for so it had fallen
ud a matter of nogle year agone med a kvinde of Eblana in Horne’s hus
that nu was trespassed ud of this verden og the self nat next
før her død alle leeches og pothecaries had taken counsel of her
case). og sagde de farther she should live because i den beginning,
sagde de, the kvinde should bring forth in pain og wherefore they that
were of this imagination affirmed hvordan young Madden had said truth for
han havde conscience to let her die. og ikke få og of these was young
Lynch were in doubt that the verden was nu right evil governed as it
was aldrig other howbeit the mean people believed it otherwise men the
law nor his judges did provide nej remedy. A redress gud grant. This was
scant said men alle cried med one acclaim nay, by our Virgin mor,
the wife should live og the babe to die. In colour whereof they waxed
hot upon that hoved hvad med argument og hvad for their drinking men
the franklin Lenehan was prompt each da to pour them ale so that at
the least way mirth might ikke lack. så young Madden showed alle the
whole affair og said hvordan that hun var dead og hvordan for holy religion
sake by rede of palmer og bedesman og for a vow han havde made to Saint
Ultan of Arbraccan her goodman husband ville ikke let her død whereby
de var alle wondrous grieved. To whom young Stephen had these words
following: Murmur, sirs, is eke oft among lay folk. Both babe og
parent nu glorify their Maker, the one in limbo gloom, the other in
purgefire. men, gramercy, hvad of those Godpossibled souls that we
nightly impossibilise, which is the sin against the Holy Ghost, meget
gud, Lord og Giver of liv? For, sirs, sagde han, our lust is brief. We
are means to those small creatures within us og nature has other ends
than we. så said Dixon junior to Punch Costello wist he hvad ends.
men han havde overmuch drunken og the best word han kunne have of him was
that han ville ever dishonest a kvinde whoso she were eller wife eller maid eller
leman if it so fortuned him to be delivered of his spleen of lustihead.
Whereat Crotthers of Alba Longa sang young Malachi’s praise of that
beast the unicorn hvordan once i den millennium he cometh by his horn, the
other alle this while, pricked forward med their jibes wherewith they
did malice him, witnessing alle og several by saint Foutinus his
engines that han var able to do any manner of thing that lay in mand to
do. Thereat laughed they alle right jocundly kun young Stephen og sir
Leopold which aldrig durst laugh også open by reason of a strange humour
which han ville ikke bewray og also for that he rued for her that bare
whoso she might be eller wheresoever. så spake young Stephen orgulous of
mor Church that would cast him ud of her bosom, of law of canons,
of Lilith, patron of abortions, of bigness wrought by vind of seeds of
brightness eller by potency of vampires mouth to mouth eller, as Virgilius
saith, ved den influence af den occident eller ved den reek of moonflower eller
an she lie med a kvinde which her mand has men lain med, _effectu
secuto_, eller peradventure in her bath according til den opinions of
Averroes og Moses Maimonides. sagde han also hvordan ved den end af den
second month a human sjæl was infused og hvordan in alle our holy mor
foldeth ever souls for gud’s greater glory whereas that earthly mor
which was men a dam to bear beastly should die by canon for so saith he
that holdeth the fisherman’s seal, endda that blessed Peter on which
rock was holy church for alle ages founded. alle they bachelors så
asked of sir Leopold would he in som case so jeopard her person as
risk liv to save liv. A wariness of sind han ville answer as fitted
alle og, laying hånd to jaw, sagde han dissembling, as his wont was, that
as det var informed him, hvem had ever loved the art of physic as might a
layman, og agreeing also med his experience of so seldomseen an
accident det var gud for that mor Church belike at one blow had
birth og død pence og in such sort deliverly he scaped their
questions. That is truth, pardy, said Dixon, og, eller I err, a pregnant
word. Which hearing young Stephen was a marvellous glad mand og he
averred that he hvem stealeth fra den poor lendeth til den Lord for he
was of a wild manner da han var drunken og that han var nu in that
taking it appeared eftsoons.

men sir Leopold was passing grave maugre his word by cause he stadig had
pity af den terrorcausing shrieking of shrill women in their labour og
as han var minded of his gud lady Marion that had borne him an kun
manchild which on his eleventh dag on live had died og nej mand of art
could save so mørk is destiny. og hun var wondrous stricken of hjerte
for that evil hap og for his burial did him on a fair corselet of
lamb’s wool, the blomst af den flock, lest he might perish utterly og
lie akeled (for det var så om the midst af den winter) og nu sir
Leopold that had of his krop nej manchild for an heir looked upon him
his ven’s søn og was shut up in sorrow for his forepassed happiness
og as sad as han var that him failed a søn of such gentle courage (for
alle accounted him of real parts) so grieved he also in nej less measure
for young Stephen for that he lived riotously med those wastrels og
murdered his goods med whores.

om that present tid young Stephen filled alle cups that stood empty
so as der remained men lille mo if the prudenter havde ikke shadowed
their approach fra him that stadig plied it meget busily hvem, praying
for the intentions af den sovereign pontiff, han gav them for a pledge
the vicar of Christ which also as sagde han is vicar of Bray. nu drink
we, quod he, of this mazer og quaff ye this mead which er ikke indeed
parcel of my krop men my sjæl’s bodiment. Leave ye fraction of bread to
them that live by bread alone. Be ikke afeard neither for any want for
this will comfort mere than the other will dismay. See ye her. og he
showed them glistering coins af den tribute og goldsmith notes the
worth of two pound nineteen shilling that han havde, sagde han, for a sang
which he writ. They alle admired to see the foresaid riches in such
dearth of money as was herebefore. His words were så these as
followeth: Know alle men, sagde han, tid’s ruins build eternity’s
mansions. hvad means this? Desire’s vind blasts the thorntree men efter
it becomes fra a bramblebush to be a rose upon the rood of tid. Mark
me nu. In kvinde’s womb word is made flesh men i den spirit af den
maker alle flesh that passes becomes the word that shall ikke pass away.
This is the postcreation. _Omnis caro ad te veniet_. nej question men
her name is puissant hvem aventried the dear corse of our Agenbuyer,
Healer og Herd, our mighty mor og mor mest venerable og
Bernardus saith aptly that She hath an _omnipotentiam deiparae
supplicem_, that is to wit, an almightiness of petition because she is
the second Eve og she won us, saith Augustine også, whereas that other,
our grandam, which we are linked up med by successive anastomosis of
navelcords sold us alle, seed, breed og generation, for a penny pippin.
men her is the matter nu. eller she knew him, that second I say, og was
men creature of her creature, _vergine madre, figlia di tuo figlio_, eller
she knew him ikke og så stands she i den one denial eller ignorancy
med Peter Piscator hvem lives i den hus that Jack built og med
Joseph the joiner patron af den happy demise of alle unhappy marriages,
_parceque M. Léo Taxil nous a dit que qui l’avait mise dans cette
fichue position c’était le sacré pigeon, ventre de Dieu! Entweder_
transubstantiality _oder_ consubstantiality men in nej case
subsubstantiality. og alle cried ud upon it for a meget scurvy word. A
pregnancy without joy, sagde han, a birth without pangs, a krop without
blemish, a belly without bigness. Let the lewd med faith og fervour
worship. med will will we withstand, withsay.

Hereupon Punch Costello dinged med his fist upon the board og would
sing a bawdy catch _Staboo Stabella_ om a wench that was put in pod
of a jolly swashbuckler in Almany which he did straightways nu attack:
_The first three months hun var ikke well, Staboo,_ da her nurse
Quigley fra den dør angerly bid them hist ye should shame you nor was
it ikke meet as she remembered them being her sind was to have alle
orderly against lord Andrew came for because hun var jealous that nej
gasteful turmoil might shorten the honour of her guard. det var an
ancient og a sad matron of a sedate look og christian walking, in
habit dun beseeming her megrims og wrinkled visage, nor did her
hortative want of it effect for incontinently Punch Costello was of
them alle embraided og they reclaimed the churl med civil rudeness
nogle og shaked him med menace of blandishments others whiles they alle
chode med him, a murrain seize the dolt, hvad a devil han ville be at,
thou chuff, thou puny, thou got in peasestraw, thou losel, thou
chitterling, thou spawn of a rebel, thou dykedropt, thou abortion thou,
to shut up his drunken drool ud of that som a curse of gud ape, the
gud sir Leopold that had for his cognisance the blomst of quiet,
margerain gentle, advising also the tid’s occasion as mest sacred og
mest worthy to be mest sacred. In Horne’s hus rest should reign.

To be short this passage was scarce by da Master Dixon of Mary in
Eccles, goodly grinning, asked young Stephen hvad was the reason hvorfor he
havde ikke cided to take friar’s vows og he answered him obedience i den
womb, chastity i den tomb men involuntary poverty alle his days. Master
Lenehan at this made return that han havde heard of those nefarious deeds
og hvordan, as he heard hereof counted, han havde besmirched the lily virtue
of a confiding female which was corruption of minors og they alle
intershowed it også, waxing merry og toasting to his fathership. men he
said meget entirely det var clean contrary to their suppose for han var
the eternal søn og ever virgin. Thereat mirth grew in them the mere
og they rehearsed to him his curious rite of wedlock for the disrobing
og deflowering of spouses, as the priests use in Madagascar island,
she to be in guise of white og saffron, her groom in white og grain,
med burning of nard og tapers, on a bridebed while clerks sung kyries
og the anthem _Ut novetur sexus omnis corporis mysterium_ till hun var
der unmaided. han gav them så a meget admirable hymen minim by those
delicate poets Master John Fletcher og Master Francis Beaumont that is
in their _Maid’s Tragedy_ that was writ for a som twining of lovers:
_To bed, to bed_ was the burden of it to be played med accompanable
concent upon the virginals. An exquisite dulcet epithalame of mest
mollificative suadency for juveniles amatory whom the odoriferous
flambeaus af den paranymphs have escorted til den quadrupedal proscenium
of connubial communion. Well met de var, said Master Dixon, joyed,
men, harkee, young sir, better were they named Beau Mount og Lecher
for, by my troth, of such a mingling meget might come. Young Stephen
said indeed to his best remembrance de havde men the one doxy between
them og she af den stews to make shift med in delights amorous for
liv ran meget high in those days og the custom af den country approved
med it. Greater kærlighed than this, sagde han, nej mand hath that a mand lay
down his wife for his ven. Go thou og do likewise. Thus, eller words
to that effect, saith Zarathustra, sometime regius professor of French
letters til den university of Oxtail nor breathed der ever that mand to
whom mankind was mere beholden. Bring a stranger within thy tower it
will go hard men thou wilt have the secondbest bed. _Orate, fratres,
pro memetipso_. og alle the people shall say, Amen. Remember, Erin, thy
generations og thy days of gammel, hvordan thou settedst lille by me og by
my word og broughtedst in a stranger to my gates to commit fornication
in my sight og to wax fat og kick som Jeshurum. Therefore hast thou
sinned against my lys og hast made me, thy lord, to be the slave of
servants. Return, return, Clan Milly: forget me ikke, O Milesian. hvorfor
hast thou done this abomination før me that thou didst spurn me for
a merchant of jalaps og didst deny me til den Roman og til den Indian
of mørk speech med whom thy daughters did lie luxuriously? Look forth
nu, my people, upon the land of behest, endda fra Horeb og fra Nebo
og fra Pisgah og fra den Horns of Hatten unto a land flowing med
milk og money. men thou hast suckled me med a bitter milk: my måne
og my sol thou hast quenched for ever. og thou hast left me alone for
ever i den mørk ways of my bitterness: og med a kiss of ashes hast
thou kissed my mouth. This tenebrosity af den interior, he proceeded to
say, hath ikke been illumined ved den wit af den septuagint nor so meget
as mentioned for the Orient fra on high which brake hell’s gates
visited a darkness that was foraneous. Assuefaction minorates
atrocities (as Tully saith of his darling Stoics) og Hamlet his far
showeth the prince nej blister of combustion. The adiaphane i den noon
of liv is an Egypt’s plague which i den nights of prenativity og
postmortemity is their mest proper _ubi_ og _quomodo_. og as the ends
og ultimates of alle things accord in nogle mean og measure med their
inceptions og originals, that same multiplicit concordance which leads
forth growth fra birth accomplishing by a retrogressive metamorphosis
that minishing og ablation towards the final which is agreeable unto
nature so is it med our subsolar being. The aged sisters draw us ind i
liv: we wail, batten, sport, clip, clasp, sunder, dwindle, die: over
us dead they bend. First, saved fra waters of gammel Nile, among
bulrushes, a bed of fasciated wattles: at last the cavity of a
mountain, an occulted sepulchre amid the conclamation af den hillcat
og the ossifrage. og as nej mand knows the ubicity of his tumulus nor
to hvad processes we shall thereby be ushered nor whether to Tophet eller
to Edenville i den som way is alle hidden da we would backward see
fra hvad region of remoteness the whatness of our whoness hath fetched
his whenceness.

Thereto Punch Costello roared ud mainly _Etienne chanson_ men he
loudly bid them, lo, wisdom hath built herself a hus, this vast
majestic longstablished vault, the crystal palace af den Creator, alle
in applepie order, a penny for him hvem finds the pea.

Behold the mansion reared by dedal Jack
     See the malt stored in mange a refluent sack,
     i den proud cirque of Jackjohn’s bivouac.

A black crack of noise i den gade her, alack, bawled back. Loud on
left Thor thundered: in anger awful the hammerhurler. Came nu the
storm that hist his hjerte. og Master Lynch bade him have a care to
flout og witwanton as the gud self was angered for his hellprate og
paganry. og he that had erst challenged to be so doughty waxed wan as
they might alle mark og shrank together og his pitch that was før
so haught uplift was nu of a sudden quite plucked down og his hjerte
shook within the cage of his breast as he tasted the rumour of that
storm. så did nogle mock og nogle jeer og Punch Costello fell hard
igen to his yale which Master Lenehan vowed han ville do efter og he
was indeed men a word og a blow on any the least colour. men the
braggart boaster cried that an gammel Nobodaddy was in his cups det var
muchwhat indifferent og han ville ikke lag behind his lead. men this was
kun to dye his desperation as cowed he crouched in Horne’s hall. He
drank indeed at one draught to pluck up a hjerte of any grace for it
thundered lang rumblingly over alle the heavens so that Master Madden,
being godly certain whiles, knocked him on his ribs upon that crack of
doom og Master Bloom, ved den braggart’s side, spoke to him calming
words to slumber his great fear, advertising hvordan det var nej other thing
men a hubbub noise that he heard, the discharge of fluid fra den
thunderhead, look you, having taken place, og alle af den order of a
natural phenomenon.

men was young Boasthard’s fear vanquished by Calmer’s words? nej, for he
had in his bosom a spike named Bitterness which kunne ikke by words be
done away. og was he så neither calm som the one nor godly som the
other? han var neither as meget as han ville have liked to be either. men
could he ikke have endeavoured to have found igen as in his youth the
bottle Holiness that så he lived withal? Indeed nej for Grace var ikke
der to find that bottle. Heard he så in that clap the stemme af den
gud Bringforth eller, hvad Calmer said, a hubbub of Phenomenon? Heard?
hvorfor, han kunne ikke men hear unless han havde plugged him up the tube
Understanding (which han havde ikke done). For through that tube han så
that han var i den land of Phenomenon hvor he must for a certain one
dag die as han var som the rest også a passing show. og would he ikke
accept to die som the rest og pass away? By nej means would he though
he must nor would he make mere shows according as men do med wives
which Phenomenon has commanded them to do ved den book Law. så wotted
he nought of that other land which is called Believe-on-Me, that is the
land of promise which behoves til den konge Delightful og shall be for
ever hvor der is nej død og nej birth neither wiving nor mothering
at which alle shall come as mange as believe on it? ja, Pious had told
him of that land og Chaste had pointed him til den way men the reason
was that i den way he fell in med a certain whore of an eyepleasing
exterior whose name, sagde hun, is Bird-in-the-hånd og she beguiled him
wrongways fra den sandt path by her flatteries that sagde hun to him as,
Ho, you pretty mand, turn aside hither og jeg vil show you a brave
place, og she lay at him so flatteringly that hun havde him in her grot
which is named Two-in-the-Bush eller, by nogle learned, Carnal
Concupiscence.

This was it hvad alle that company that sat der at commons in Manse of
Mothers the mest lusted efter og if they met med this whore
Bird-in-the-hånd (which was within alle foul plagues, monsters og a
wicked devil) they would strain the last men they would make at her og
know her. For regarding Believe-on-Me sagde de det var nought else men
notion og they could conceive nej thought of it for, first,
Two-in-the-Bush whither she ticed them was the meget goodliest grot og
in it were four pillows on which were four tickets med these words
printed on them, Pickaback og Topsyturvy og Shameface og Cheek by
Jowl og, second, for that foul plague Allpox og the monsters they
cared ikke for them for Preservative had given them a stout shield of
oxengut og, third, that they might take nej hurt neither fra Offspring
that was that wicked devil by virtue of this same shield which was
named Killchild. So were they alle in their blind fancy, Mr Cavil og Mr
somme tider Godly, Mr Ape Swillale, Mr False Franklin, Mr Dainty Dixon,
Young Boasthard og Mr Cautious Calmer. Wherein, O wretched company,
were ye alle deceived for that was the stemme af den gud that was in a
meget grievous rage that han ville presently lift his arm up og spill
their souls for their abuses og their spillings done by them
contrariwise to his word which forth to bring brenningly biddeth.

So Thursday sixteenth June Patk. Dignam laid in clay of an apoplexy og
efter hard drought, please gud, rained, a bargeman coming in by vand a
fifty mile eller thereabout med turf saying the seed won’t sprout, fields
athirst, meget sadcoloured og stunk mightily, the quags og tofts også.
Hard to breathe og alle the young quicks clean consumed without
sprinkle this lang while back as nej mand remembered to be without. The
rosy buds alle gone brown og spread ud blobs og på den hills nought
men dry flag og faggots that would catch at first ild. alle the verden
saying, for aught they knew, the stor vind of last February a year that
did havoc the land so pitifully a small thing beside this barrenness.
men by og by, as said, this evening efter sundown, the vind sitting in
the west, biggish swollen clouds to be seen as the nat increased og
the weatherwise poring up at them og nogle sheet lightnings at first
og efter, past ten af den clock, one great stroke med a lang thunder
og in a brace of shakes alle scamper pellmell within dør for the
smoking shower, the men making shelter for their straws med a clout eller
kerchief, womenfolk skipping off med kirtles catched up soon as the
pour came. In Ely place, Baggot gade, Duke’s lawn, thence through
Merrion green up to Holles gade a swash of vand flowing that was
før bonedry og ikke one chair eller coach eller fiacre seen om men nej
mere crack efter that first. over against the Rt. Hon. Mr Justice
Fitzgibbon’s dør (that is to sit med Mr Healy the lawyer upon the
college lands) Mal. Mulligan a gentleman’s gentleman that had men come
fra Mr Moore’s the writer’s (that was a papish men is nu, folk say, a
gud Williamite) chanced against Alec. Bannon in a cut bob (which are
nu in med dance cloaks of Kendal green) that was ny got to town fra
Mullingar med den stage hvor his coz og Mal M’s bror will stay a
month yet till Saint Swithin og asks hvad i den jord he does der,
he bound hjem og he to Andrew Horne’s being stayed for to crush a cup
of wine, so sagde han, men would tell him of a skittish heifer, stor of
her age og beef til den heel, og alle this while poured med regn og
so both together on to Horne’s. der Leop. Bloom of Crawford’s journal
sitting snug med a covey of wags, likely brangling fellows, Dixon
jun., scholar of my lady of Mercy’s, Vin. Lynch, a Scots fellow, Will.
Madden, T. Lenehan, meget sad om a racer he fancied og Stephen D.
Leop. Bloom der for a languor han havde men was nu better, he having
dreamed tonight a strange fancy of his dame Mrs Moll med red slippers
on in a pair of Turkey trunks which is thought by those in ken to be
for a change og Mistress Purefoy der, that got in through pleading
her belly, og nu på den stools, poor krop, two days past her term,
the midwives sore put to it og can’t deliver, she queasy for a bowl of
riceslop that is a shrewd drier up af den insides og her breath meget
heavy mere than gud og should be a bullyboy fra den knocks, they
say, men gud give her soon issue. ’Tis her ninth chick to live, I hear,
og Lady dag bit off her last chick’s nails that was så a twelvemonth
og med other three alle breastfed that died written ud in a fair hånd
i den konge’s bible. Her hub fifty odd og a methodist men takes the
sacrament og is to be seen any fair sabbath med a pair of his boys
off Bullock harbour dapping på den sound med a heavybraked reel eller in
a punt he has trailing for flounder og pollock og catches a fine bag,
I hear. In sum an infinite great fall of regn og alle refreshed og
will meget increase the harvest yet those in ken say efter vind og
vand ild shall come for a prognostication of Malachi’s almanac (og I
hear that Mr Russell has done a prophetical charm af den same gist ud
af den Hindustanish for his farmer’s gazette) to have three things in
alle men this a mere fetch without bottom of reason for gammel crones og
bairns yet somme tider they are found i den right guess med their
queerities nej telling hvordan.

med this came up Lenehan til den feet af den table to say hvordan the
letter was in that nat’s gazette og han lavede a show to find it om
him (for he swore med an oath that han havde been at pains om it) men
on Stephen’s persuasion han gav over the search og was bidden to sit
near by which he did mighty brisk. han var a kind of sport gentleman
that went for a merryandrew eller honest pickle og hvad belonged of
women, horseflesh eller hot scandal han havde it pat. To tell the truth he
was mean in fortunes og for the mest part hankered om the
coffeehouses og low taverns med crimps, ostlers, bookies, Paul’s men,
runners, flatcaps, waistcoateers, ladies af den bagnio og other rogues
af den game eller med a chanceable catchpole eller a tipstaff ofte at
nights till broad dag of whom he picked up between his sackpossets meget
loose gossip. han tog his ordinary at a boilingcook’s og if han havde men
gotten ind i him a mess of broken victuals eller a platter of tripes med a
bare tester in his purse han kunne altid bring himself off med his
tongue, nogle randy quip han havde fra a punk eller whatnot that hver
mor’s søn of them would burst their sides. The other, Costello that
is, hearing this talk asked was it poetry eller a tale. Faith, nej, he
says, Frank (that was his name), ’tis alle om Kerry cows that are to
be butchered along af den plague. men they can go hang, says he med a
wink, for me med their bully beef, a pox on it. der’s as gud fish
in this tin as ever came ud of it og meget friendly he offered to take
of nogle salty sprats that stood by which han havde eyed wishly i den
meantime og found the place which was indeed the chief design of his
embassy as han var sharpset. _Mort aux vaches_, says Frank så i den
French language that had been indentured to a brandyshipper that has a
winelodge in Bordeaux og he spoke French som a gentleman også. fra a
barn this Frank had been a donought that his far, a headborough,
hvem could ill keep him to school to learn his letters og the use of
the globes, matriculated ved den university to study the mechanics men
han tog the bit between his teeth som a raw colt og was mere familiar
med den justiciary og the parish beadle than med his volumes. One
tid han ville be a playactor, så a sutler eller a welsher, så nought
would keep him fra den bearpit og the cocking main, så han var for
the ocean hav eller to hoof it på den roads med den romany folk,
kidnapping a squire’s heir by favour of moonlight eller fecking maids’
linen eller choking chicken behind a hedge. han havde been off as mange times
as a cat has lives og back igen med naked pockets as mange mere to
his far the headborough hvem shed a pint of tears as ofte as han så
him. hvad, says Mr Leopold med his hands across, that was earnest to
know the drift of it, will they slaughter alle? I protest jeg så them men
this dag morning going til den Liverpool boats, says he. I can scarce
believe ’tis so dårlig, says he. og han havde experience af den som brood
beasts og of springers, greasy hoggets og wether wool, having been
nogle years før actuary for Mr Joseph Cuffe, a worthy salesmaster
that drove his trade for live stock og meadow auctions hard by Mr
Gavin Low’s yard in Prussia gade. I question med you der, says he.
mere som ’tis the hoose eller the timber tongue. Mr Stephen, a lille
moved men meget handsomely told him nej such matter og that han havde
dispatches fra den emperor’s chief tailtickler thanking him for the
hospitality, that was sending over Doctor Rinderpest, the bestquoted
cowcatcher in alle Muscovy, med a bolus eller two of physic to take the
bull ved den horns. Come, come, says Mr Vincent, plain dealing. He’ll
find himself på den horns of a dilemma if he meddles med a bull that’s
Irish, says he. Irish by name og irish by nature, says Mr Stephen, og
he sent the ale purling om, an Irish bull in an English chinashop. I
conceive you, says Mr Dixon. It is that same bull that was sent to our
island by farmer Nicholas, the bravest cattlebreeder of them alle, med
an emerald ring in his nose. sandt for you, says Mr Vincent cross the
table, og a bullseye ind i den bargain, says he, og a plumper og a
portlier bull, says he, aldrig shit on shamrock. han havde horns galore, a
coat of cloth of gold og a sweet smoky breath coming ud of his
nostrils so that the women of our island, leaving doughballs og
rollingpins, followed efter him hanging his bulliness in daisychains.
hvad for that, says Mr Dixon, men før han kom over farmer Nicholas
that was a eunuch had him properly gelded by a college of doctors hvem
were nej better off than himself. So be off nu, says he, og do alle my
cousin german the lord Harry tells you og take a farmer’s blessing,
og med that he slapped his posteriors meget soundly. men the slap og
the blessing stood him ven, says Mr Vincent, for to make up he
taught him a trick worth two af den other so that maid, wife, abbess
og widow to this dag affirm that they would rather any tid af den
month whisper in his ear i den mørk of a cowhouse eller get a lick på den
nape fra his lang holy tongue than lie med den finest strapping young
ravisher i den four fields of alle Ireland. Another så put in his
word: og they dressed him, says he, in a point shift og petticoat
med a tippet og girdle og ruffles on his wrists og clipped his
forelock og rubbed him alle over med spermacetic oil og built stables
for him at hver turn af den road med a gold manger in each full of
the best hay i den market so that han kunne doss og dung to his
hjerte’s content. By this tid the far af den faithful (for so they
called him) was grown so heavy that han kunne scarce walk to pasture. To
remedy which our cozening dames og damsels brought him his fodder in
their apronlaps og as soon as his belly was full han ville rear up on
his hind quarters to show their ladyships a mystery og roar og bellow
ud of him in bulls’ language og they alle efter him. Ay, says another,
og so pampered was he that han ville suffer nought to grow in alle the
land men green grass for himself (for that was the kun colour to his
sind) og der var a board put up on a hillock i den middle af den
island med a printed notice, saying: ved den Lord Harry, Green is the
grass that grows på den ground. og, says Mr Dixon, if ever han fik
scent of a cattleraider in Roscommon eller the wilds of Connemara eller a
husbandman in Sligo that was sowing as meget as a handful of mustard eller
a bag of rapeseed ud he’d run amok over half the countryside rooting
up med his horns whatever was planted og alle by lord Harry’s orders.
der var dårlig blood between them at first, says Mr Vincent, og the
lord Harry called farmer Nicholas alle the gammel Nicks i den verden og an
gammel whoremaster that kept seven trulls in his hus og I’ll meddle in
his matters, says he. I’ll make that animal smell hell, says he, med
the help of that gud pizzle my far left me. men one evening, says
Mr Dixon, da the lord Harry was cleaning his royal pelt to go to
dinner efter winning a boatrace (han havde spade oars for himself men the
first rule af den course was that the others were to row med
pitchforks) he discovered in himself a wonderful likeness to a bull og
on picking up a blackthumbed chapbook that he kept i den pantry he
found sure enough that han var a lefthanded descendant af den famous
champion bull af den Romans, _Bos Bovum_, which is gud bog Latin for
boss af den show. efter that, says Mr Vincent, the lord Harry put his
hoved ind i a cow’s drinkingtrough i den presence of alle his courtiers
og pulling it ud igen told them alle his ny name. så, med den
vand running off him, han fik ind i an gammel smock og skirt that had
belonged to his grandmother og bought a grammar af den bulls’ language
to study men han kunne aldrig learn a word of it except the first
personal pronoun which he copied ud stor og got off by hjerte og if
ever han gik ud for a walk he filled his pockets med chalk to write
it upon hvad took his fancy, the side of a rock eller a teahouse table eller
a bale of cotton eller a corkfloat. In short, he og the bull of Ireland
were soon as fast friends as an arse og a shirt. de var, says Mr
Stephen, og the end was that the men af den island seeing nej help was
toward, as the ungrate women were alle of one sind, made a wherry raft,
loaded themselves og their bundles of chattels on shipboard, set alle
masts erect, manned the yards, sprang their luff, heaved to, spread
three sheets i den vind, put her hoved between vind og vand, weighed
anchor, ported her helm, ran up the jolly Roger, gave three times
three, let the bullgine run, pushed off in their bumboat og put to hav
to recover the main of America. Which was the occasion, says Mr
Vincent, af den composing by a boatswain of that rollicking chanty:
_—Pope Peter’s men a pissabed.
A mand’s a mand for a’ that._

Our worthy acquaintance Mr Malachi Mulligan nu appeared i den doorway
as the students were finishing their apologue accompanied med a ven
whom han havde bare rencountered, a young gentleman, his name Alec Bannon,
hvem had late come to town, it being his intention to buy a colour eller a
cornetcy i den fencibles og list for the wars. Mr Mulligan was civil
enough to express nogle relish of it alle the mere as it jumped med a
project of his own for the cure af den meget evil that had been touched
on. Whereat he handed round til den company a set of pasteboard cards
which han havde had printed that dag at Mr Quinnell’s bearing a legend
printed in fair italics: _Mr Malachi Mulligan. Fertiliser og
Incubator. Lambay Island_. His project, as han gik on to expound, was
to withdraw fra den round of idle pleasures such as form the chief
business of sir Fopling Popinjay og sir Milksop Quidnunc in town og
to devote himself til den noblest task for which our bodily organism has
been framed. Well, let us hear of it, gud my ven, said Mr Dixon. I
make nej doubt it smacks of wenching. Come, be seated, both. ’Tis as
cheap sitting as standing. Mr Mulligan accepted af den invitation og,
expatiating upon his design, told his hearers that han havde been led ind i
this thought by a consideration af den causes of sterility, both the
inhibitory og the prohibitory, whether the inhibition in its turn were
due to conjugal vexations eller to a parsimony af den balance as well as
whether the prohibition proceeded fra defects congenital eller fra
proclivities acquired. It grieved him plaguily, sagde han, to see the
nuptial couch defrauded of its dearest pledges: og to reflect upon so
mange agreeable females med rich jointures, a prey til den vilest
bonzes, hvem hide their flambeau under a bushel in an uncongenial
cloister eller lose their womanly bloom i den embraces of nogle
unaccountable muskin da they might multiply the inlets of happiness,
sacrificing the inestimable jewel of their sex da a hundred pretty
fellows were at hånd to caress, this, he assured them, made his hjerte
weep. To curb this inconvenient (which he concluded due to a
suppression of latent heat), having advised med certain counsellors of
worth og inspected ind i this matter, han havde resolved to purchase in
fee simple for ever the freehold of Lambay island fra its holder, lord
Talbot de Malahide, a Tory gentleman of note meget in favour med our
ascendancy party. He proposed to set up der a national fertilising
farm to be named _Omphalos_ med an obelisk hewn og erected efter the
fashion of Egypt og to offer his dutiful yeoman services for the
fecundation of any female of hvad grade of liv soever hvem should der
direct to him med den desire of fulfilling the functions of her
natural. Money was nej object, sagde han, nor would he take a penny for
his pains. The poorest kitchenwench nej less than the opulent lady of
fashion, if so be their constructions og their tempers were warm
persuaders for their petitions, would find in him their mand. For his
nutriment he shewed hvordan han ville feed himself exclusively upon a diet
of savoury tubercles og fish og coneys der, the flesh of these
latter prolific rodents being highly recommended for his purpose, both
broiled og stewed med a blade of mace og a pod eller two of capsicum
chillies. efter this homily which he delivered med meget warmth of
asseveration Mr Mulligan in a trice put off fra his hat a kerchief
med which han havde shielded it. They both, it seems, had been overtaken
ved den regn og for alle their mending their pace had taken vand, as
might be observed by Mr Mulligan’s smallclothes of a hodden grey which
was nu somewhat piebald. His project meanwhile was meget favourably
entertained by his auditors og won hearty eulogies fra alle though Mr
Dixon of Mary’s excepted to it, asking med a finicking air did he
purpose also to carry coals to Newcastle. Mr Mulligan however made
court til den scholarly by an apt quotation fra den classics which, as
it dwelt upon his memory, seemed to him a sound og tasteful support of
his contention: _Talis ac tanta depravatio hujus seculi, O quirites, ut
matresfamiliarum nostrae lascivas cujuslibet semiviri libici
titillationes testibus ponderosis atque excelsis erectionibus
centurionum Romanorum magnopere anteponunt_, while for those of ruder
wit he drove hjem his point by analogies af den animal kingdom mere
suitable to their stomach, the buck og doe af den forest glade, the
farmyard drake og duck.

Valuing himself ikke a lille upon his elegance, being indeed a proper
mand of person, this talkative nu applied himself to his dress med
animadversions of nogle heat upon the sudden whimsy af den atmospherics
while the company lavished their encomiums upon the project han havde
advanced. The young gentleman, his ven, overjoyed as han var at a
passage that had late befallen him, kunne ikke forbear to tell it his
nearest neighbour. Mr Mulligan, nu perceiving the table, asked for
whom were those loaves og fishes og, seeing the stranger, han lavede him
a civil bow og said, Pray, sir, was you in need of any professional
assistance we could give? hvem, upon his offer, thanked him meget
heartily, though preserving his proper distance, og replied that he

medial line so that (as sagde han) one ear could hear hvad the other

vein, the premature relentment af den amniotic fluid (as exemplified in

The voices blend og fuse in clouded silence: silence that is the
infinite of space: og swiftly, silently the sjæl is wafted over
regions of cycles of generations that have lived. A region hvor grey
twilight ever descends, aldrig falls on wide sagegreen pasturefields,
shedding her dusk, scattering a perennial dew of stjerner. She follows her
mor med ungainly steps, a mare leading her fillyfoal. Twilight
phantoms are they, yet moulded in prophetic grace of structure, slim
shapely haunches, a supple tendonous neck, the meek apprehensive skull.
They fade, sad phantoms: alle is gone. Agendath is a waste land, a hjem
of screechowls og the sandblind upupa. Netaim, the golden, is nej mere.
og på den highway af den clouds they come, muttering thunder of
rebellion, the ghosts of beasts. Huuh! Hark! Huuh! Parallax stalks
behind og goads them, the lancinating lightnings of whose brow are
scorpions. Elk og yak, the bulls of Bashan og of Babylon, mammoth og
mastodon, they come trooping til den sunken hav, _Lacus Mortis_. Ominous
revengeful zodiacal host! They moan, passing upon the clouds, horned
og capricorned, the trumpeted med den tusked, the lionmaned, the
giantantlered, snouter og crawler, rodent, ruminant og pachyderm, alle
their moving moaning multitude, murderers af den sol.

Onward til den dead hav they tramp to drink, unslaked og med horrible
gulpings, the salt somnolent inexhaustible flood. og the equine
portent grows igen, magnified i den deserted heavens, nay to heaven’s
own magnitude, till it looms, vast, over the hus of Virgo. og lo,
wonder of metempsychosis, it is she, the everlasting bride, harbinger
af den daystar, the bride, ever virgin. It is she, Martha, thou lost
one, Millicent, the young, the dear, the radiant. hvordan serene does she
nu arise, a queen among the Pleiades, i den penultimate antelucan
hour, shod in sandals of bright gold, coifed med a veil of hvad do you
call it gossamer. It floats, it flows om her starborn flesh og
loose it streams, emerald, sapphire, mauve og heliotrope, sustained on
currents af den cold interstellar vind, winding, coiling, simply
swirling, writhing i den skies a mysterious writing till, efter a
myriad metamorphoses of symbol, it blazes, Alpha, a ruby og triangled
sign upon the forehead of Taurus.

The debate which ensued was in its scope og progress an epitome af den

debaters were the keenest i den land, the theme de var engaged on
the loftiest og mest vital. The high hall of Horne’s hus had aldrig
beheld an assembly so representative og so varied nor had the gammel
rafters of that establishment ever listened to a language so
encyclopaedic. A gallant scene in truth it made. Crotthers was der at
the foot af den table in his striking Highland garb, his ansigt glowing
fra den briny airs af den Mull of Galloway. der også, opposite to
him, was Lynch whose countenance bore allerede the stigmata of early
depravity og premature wisdom. Next the Scotchman was the place
assigned to Costello, the eccentric, while at his side was seated in
stolid repose the squat form of Madden. The chair af den resident

brogues contrasted sharply med den primrose elegance og townbred
manners of Malachi Roland St John Mulligan. Lastly ved den hoved af den
board was the young poet hvem found a refuge fra his labours of
pedagogy og metaphysical inquisition i den convivial atmosphere of

pencil of Lafayette has limned for ages yet to come.

It had better be stated her og nu ved den outset that the perverted
transcendentalism to which Mr S. Dedalus’ (Div. Scep.) contentions

to accepted scientific methods. Science, it cannot be også ofte
repeated, deals med tangible phenomena. The mand of science som the
mand i den gade has to ansigt hardheaded facts that cannot be blinked
og explain them as best he can. der may be, it is sandt, nogle
questions which science cannot answer—at present—such as the first
problem submitted by Mr L. Bloom (Pubb. Canv.) regarding the future
determination of sex. Must we accept the view of Empedocles of
Trinacria that the right ovary (the postmenstrual period, assert
others) is responsible for the birth of males eller are the også lang
neglected spermatozoa eller nemasperms the differentiating factors eller is
it, as mest embryologists incline to opine, such as Culpepper,
Spallanzani, Blumenbach, Lusk, Hertwig, Leopold og Valenti, a mixture
of both? This would be tantamount to a cooperation (one of nature’s
favourite devices) between the _nisus formativus_ af den nemasperm on
the one hånd og på den other a happily chosen position, _succubitus
felix_, af den passive element. The other problem raised ved den same
inquirer is scarcely less vital: infant mortality. It is interesting
because, as he pertinently remarks, we are alle born i den same way men
we alle die in different ways. Mr M. Mulligan (Hyg. et Eug. Doc.) blames
the sanitary conditions in which our greylunged citizens contract
adenoids, pulmonary complaints etc. by inhaling the bacteria which lurk
in dust. These factors, he alleged, og the revolting spectacles
offered by our streets, hideous publicity posters, religious ministers
of alle denominations, mutilated soldiers og sailors, exposed scorbutic
cardrivers, the suspended carcases of dead animals, paranoic bachelors
og unfructified duennas—these, sagde han, were accountable for any og
hver fallingoff i den calibre af den race. Kalipedia, he prophesied,
would soon be generally adopted og alle the graces of liv, genuinely
gud musik, agreeable literature, lys philosophy, instructive
pictures, plastercast reproductions af den classical statues such as
Venus og Apollo, artistic coloured photographs of prize babies, alle
these lille attentions would enable ladies hvem were in a particular
condition to pass the intervening months in a mest enjoyable manner. Mr
J. Crotthers (Disc. Bacc.) attributes nogle of these demises to
abdominal trauma i den case of women workers subjected to heavy
labours i den workshop og to marital discipline i den hjem men by
far the vast majority to neglect, private eller official, culminating in
the exposure of newborn infants, the practice of criminal abortion eller
i den atrocious crime of infanticide. Although the former (we are
thinking of neglect) is undoubtedly kun også sandt the case he cites of
nurses forgetting to count the sponges i den peritoneal cavity is også
rare to be normative. In fact da one comes to look ind i it the wonder
is that so mange pregnancies og deliveries go off so well as they do,
alle things considered og in spite of our human shortcomings which
ofte baulk nature in her intentions. An ingenious suggestion is that
thrown ud by Mr V. Lynch (Bacc. Arith.) that both natality og
mortality, as well as alle other phenomena of evolution, tidal
movements, lunar phases, blood temperatures, diseases in general,
alt, in fine, in nature’s vast workshop fra den extinction of
nogle remote sol til den blossoming of one af den countless blomster which
beautify our public parks is subject to a law of numeration as yet
unascertained. stadig the plain straightforward question hvorfor a barn of
normally healthy parents og seemingly a healthy barn og properly
looked efter succumbs unaccountably in early childhood (though other
