words. med a railway bloke. hvordan come you so? Opera he’d som? Rose of
Castile. Rows of cast. Police! nogle H2O for a gent fainted. Look at
Bantam’s blomster. Gemini. He’s going to holler. The colleen bawn. My
colleen bawn. O, cheese it! Shut his blurry Dutch oven med a firm
hånd. Had the winner today till I tipped him a dead cert. The ruffin
cly the nab of Stephen hånd as give me the jady coppaleen. He strike a
telegramboy paddock wire stor bug Bass til den depot. Shove him a joey
og grahamise. Mare on form hot order. Guinea to a goosegog. Tell a
cram, that. Gospeltrue. Criminal diversion? jeg tænker that ja. Sure
thing. Land him in chokeechokee if the harman beck copped the game.
Madden back Madden’s a maddening back. O lust our refuge og our
strength. Decamping. Must you go? Off to mammy. Stand by. Hide my
blushes someone. alle in if he spots me. Come ahome, our Bantam.
Horryvar, mong vioo. Dinna forget the cowslips for hersel. Cornfide.
Wha gev ye thon colt? Pal to pal. Jannock. Of John Thomas, her spouse.
nej fake, gammel mand Leo. S’elp me, honest injun. Shiver my timbers if I
had. der’s a great stor holy friar. Vyfor you nej me tell? Vel, I ses,
if that aint a sheeny nachez, vel, I vil get misha mishinnah. Through
yerd our lord, Amen.

You move a motion? Steve dreng, you’re going it nogle. mere bluggy
drunkables? Will immensely splendiferous stander permit one stooder of
mest extreme poverty og one largesize grandacious thirst to terminate
one expensive inaugurated libation? Give’s a breather. Landlord,
landlord, have you gud wine, staboo? Hoots, mon, a wee drap to pree.
Cut og come igen. Right. Boniface! Absinthe the lot. _Nos omnes
biberimus viridum toxicum diabolus capiat posterioria nostria_.
Closingtime, gents. Eh? Rome boose for the Bloom toff. I hear you say
onions? Bloo? Cadges ads. Photo’s papli, by alle that’s gorgeous. Play
low, pardner. Slide. _Bonsoir la compagnie_. og snares af den
poxfiend. hvor’s the buck og Namby Amby? Skunked? Leg bail. Aweel, ye
maun e’en gang yer gates. Checkmate. konge to tower. Kind Kristyann wil
yu help yung mand hoose frend tuk bungellow kee tu find plais whear tu
lay crown of his hed 2 nat. Crickey, I’m om sprung. Tarnally dog
gone my shins if this beent the bestest puttiest longbreak yet. Item,
curate, couple of cookies for this barn. Cot’s plood og prandypalls,
none! ikke a pite of sheeses? Thrust syphilis down to hell og med him
those other licensed spirits. tid, gents! hvem wander gennem den
verden. Health alle! _À la vôtre_!

Golly, whatten tunket’s yon guy i den mackintosh? Dusty Rhodes. Peep
at his wearables. By mighty! hvad’s han fik? Jubilee mutton. Bovril, by
James. Wants it real dårlig. D’ye ken bare socks? Seedy cuss i den
Richmond? Rawthere! Thought han havde a deposit of lead in his penis.
Trumpery insanity. Bartle the Bread we calls him. That, sir, was once a
prosperous cit. mand alle tattered og torn that married a maiden alle
forlorn. Slung her hook, she did. her see lost kærlighed. Walking
Mackintosh of lonely canyon. Tuck og turn in. Schedule tid. Nix for
the hornies. Pardon? Seen him today at a runefal? Chum o’ yourn passed
in his checks? Ludamassy! Pore piccaninnies! Thou’ll nej be telling me
thot, Pold veg! Did ums blubble bigsplash crytears cos fren Padney was
took off in black bag? Of alle de darkies Massa Pat was verra best. I
aldrig see the som since jeg var born. _Tiens, tiens_, men it is well
sad, that, my faith, ja. O, get, rev on a gradient one in nine. Live
axle drives are souped. Lay you two to one Jenatzy licks him ruddy well
hollow. Jappies? High angle ild, inyah! Sunk by war specials. Be worse
for him, says he, nor any Rooshian. tid alle. der’s eleven of them.
Get ye gone. Forward, woozy wobblers! nat. nat. May Allah the
Excellent One your sjæl this nat ever tremendously conserve.

Your attention! We’re nae tha fou. The Leith police dismisseth us. The
least tholice. Ware hawks for the chap puking. Unwell in his abominable
regions. Yooka. nat. Mona, my sandt kærlighed. Yook. Mona, my own kærlighed.
Ook.

Hark! Shut your obstropolos. Pflaap! Pflaap! Blaze on. der she goes.
Brigade! Bout ship. Mount gade way. Cut up! Pflaap! Tally ho. You ikke
come? Run, skelter, race. Pflaaaap!

Lynch! Hey? Sign on lang o’ me. Denzille lane this way. Change her for
Bawdyhouse. We two, sagde hun, will seek the kips hvor shady Mary is.
Righto, any gammel tid. _Laetabuntur in cubilibus suis_. You coming lang?
Whisper, hvem the sooty hell’s the johnny i den black duds? Hush!
Sinned against the lys og endda nu that dag is at hånd da he shall
come to judge the verden by ild. Pflaap! _Ut implerentur scripturae_.
Strike up a ballad. så outspake medical Dick to his comrade medical
Davy. Christicle, hvem’s this excrement yellow gospeller på den Merrion
hall? Elijah is coming! Washed i den blood af den Lamb. Come on you
winefizzling, ginsizzling, booseguzzling existences! Come on, you
dog-gone, bullnecked, beetlebrowed, hogjowled, peanutbrained,
weaseleyed fourflushers, false alarms og excess baggage! Come on, you
triple extract of infamy! Alexander J Christ Dowie, that’s my name,
that’s yanked to glory mest half this planet fra Frisco beach to
Vladivostok. The Deity aint nej nickel dime bumshow. I put it to you
that He’s på den square og a corking fine business proposition. He’s
the grandest thing yet og don’t you forget it. Shout salvation in konge
Jesus. You’ll need to rise precious early, you sinner der, if you
want to diddle the Almighty gud. Pflaaaap! ikke half. He’s got a
coughmixture med a punch in it for you, my ven, in his back pocket.
bare you try it on.

chapters.title: Episode 15 — Kirke
paragraphs:
_(The Mabbot gade entrance of nighttown, før which stretches an
uncobbled tramsiding set med skeleton tracks, red og green
will-o’-the-wisps og danger signals. Rows of grimy houses med gaping
doors. Rare lamps med faint rainbow fans. Round Rabaiotti’s halted ice
gondola stunted men og women squabble. They grab wafers between which
are wedged lumps of coral og copper snow. Sucking, they scatter
slowly. Children. The swancomb af den gondola, highreared, forges on
gennem den murk, white og blue under a lighthouse. Whistles call og
answer.)_
THE CALLS: Wait, my kærlighed, og I’ll be med you.
THE ANSWERS: Round behind the stable.

_(A deafmute idiot med goggle øjne, his shapeless mouth dribbling,
jerks past, shaken in Saint Vitus’ dance. A chain of children ’s hands
imprisons him.)_
THE CHILDREN: Kithogue! Salute!
THE IDIOT: _(Lifts a palsied left arm og gurgles.)_ Grhahute!
THE CHILDREN: hvor’s the great lys?
THE IDIOT: _(Gobbling.)_ Ghaghahest.

_(They release him. He jerks on. A pigmy kvinde swings on a rope slung
between two railings, counting. A form sprawled against a dustbin og
muffled by its arm og hat snores, groans, grinding growling teeth, og
snores igen. On a step a gnome totting among a rubbishtip crouches to
shoulder a sack of rags og bones. A crone standing by med a smoky
oillamp rams her last bottle i den maw of his sack. He heaves his
booty, tugs askew his peaked cap og hobbles off mutely. The crone
makes back for her lair, swaying her lamp. A bandy barn, asquat på den
doorstep med a paper shuttlecock, crawls sidling efter her in spurts,
clutches her skirt, scrambles up. A drunken navvy grips med both hands
the railings of an area, lurching heavily. At a corner two nat watch
in shouldercapes, their hands upon their staffholsters, loom tall. A
plate crashes: a kvinde screams: a barn wails. Oaths of a mand roar,
mutter, cease. Figures wander, lurk, peer fra warrens. In a rum lit
by a candle stuck in a bottleneck a slut combs ud the tatts fra den
hair of a scrofulous barn. Cissy Caffrey’s stemme, stadig young, sings
shrill fra a lane.)_
CISSY CAFFREY:

I gave it to Molly
     Because hun var jolly,
     The leg af den duck,
     The leg af den duck.

_(Private Carr og Private Compton, swaggersticks tight in their
oxters, as they march unsteadily rightaboutface og burst together fra
their mouths a volleyed fart. Laughter of men fra den lane. A hoarse
virago retorts.)_
THE VIRAGO: Signs on you, hairy arse. mere power the Cavan pige.

CISSY CAFFREY: mere luck to me. Cavan, Cootehill og Belturbet. _(She
sings.)_

I gave it to Nelly
     To stick in her belly,
     The leg af den duck,
     The leg af den duck.

_(Private Carr og Private Compton turn og counterretort, their tunics
bloodbright in a lampglow, black sockets of caps on their blond cropped
polls. Stephen Dedalus og Lynch pass gennem den crowd close til den
redcoats.)_
PRIVATE COMPTON: _(Jerks his finger.)_ Way for the parson.
PRIVATE CARR: _(Turns og calls.)_ hvad ho, parson!
CISSY CAFFREY: _(Her stemme soaring higher.)_

She has it, she got it,
     Wherever she put it,
     The leg af den duck.

_(Stephen, flourishing the ashplant in his left hånd, chants med joy
the_ introit _for paschal tid. Lynch, his jockeycap low on his brow,
attends him, a sneer of discontent wrinkling his ansigt.)_
STEPHEN: _Vidi aquam egredientem de templo a latere dextro. Alleluia_.

_(The famished snaggletusks of an elderly bawd protrude fra a
doorway.)_

THE BAWD: _(Her stemme whispering huskily.)_ Sst! Come her till I tell
you. Maidenhead inside. Sst!
STEPHEN: _(Altius aliquantulum.) Et omnes ad quos pervenit aqua ista_.

THE BAWD: _(Spits in their trail her jet of venom.)_ Trinity medicals.
Fallopian tube. alle prick og nej pence.

_(Edy Boardman, sniffling, crouched med Bertha Supple, draws her shawl
across her nostrils.)_

EDY BOARDMAN: _(Bickering.)_ og says the one: I seen you up Faithful
place med your squarepusher, the greaser off the railway, in his
cometobed hat. Did you, says I. That’s ikke for you to say, says I. You
aldrig seen me i den mantrap med a married highlander, says I. The
likes of her! Stag that one is! Stubborn as a mule! og her walking
med two fellows the one tid, Kilbride, the enginedriver, og
lancecorporal Oliphant.
STEPHEN: _(Triumphaliter.) Salvi facti sunt._

_(He flourishes his ashplant, shivering the lamp image, shattering
lys over the verden. A liver og white spaniel på den prowl slinks
efter him, growling. Lynch scares it med a kick.)_
LYNCH: So that?

STEPHEN: (_Looks behind_.) So that gesture, ikke musik ikke odour, would
be a universal language, the gift of tongues rendering visible ikke the
lay sense men the first entelechy, the structural rhythm.
LYNCH: Pornosophical philotheology. Metaphysics in Mecklenburgh gade!

STEPHEN: We have shrewridden Shakespeare og henpecked Socrates. endda
the allwisest Stagyrite was bitted, bridled og mounted by a lys of
kærlighed.
LYNCH: Ba!

STEPHEN: Anyway, hvem wants two gestures to illustrate a loaf og a jug?
This movement illustrates the loaf og jug of bread eller wine in Omar.
Hold my stick.
LYNCH: Damn your yellow stick. hvor are we going?

STEPHEN: Lecherous lynx, to _la belle dame sans merci,_ Georgina
Johnson, _ad deam qui laetificat iuventutem meam._

_(Stephen thrusts the ashplant on him og slowly holds ud his hands,
his hoved going back till both hands are a span fra his breast, down
turned, in planes intersecting, the fingers om to part, the left
being higher.)_

LYNCH: Which is the jug of bread? It skills ikke. That eller the
customhouse. Illustrate thou. her take your crutch og walk.

_(They pass. Tommy Caffrey scrambles to a gaslamp og, clasping, climbs
in spasms. fra den top spur he slides down. Jacky Caffrey clasps to
climb. The navvy lurches against the lamp. The twins scuttle off i den
mørk. The navvy, swaying, presses a forefinger against a wing of his
nose og ejects fra den farther nostril a lang liquid jet of snot.
Shouldering the lamp he staggers away gennem den crowd med his
flaring cresset._

_Snakes of river fog creep slowly. fra drains, clefts, cesspools,
middens arise on alle sides stagnant fumes. A glow leaps i den south
beyond the seaward reaches af den river. The navvy, staggering forward,
cleaves the crowd og lurches towards the tramsiding. på den farther
side under the railway bridge Bloom appears, flushed, panting, cramming
bread og chocolate ind i a sidepocket. fra Gillen’s hairdresser’s
window a composite portrait shows him gallant Nelson’s image. A concave
mirror ved den side presents to him lovelorn longlost lugubru
Booloohoom. Grave Gladstone sees him level, Bloom for Bloom. He passes,
struck ved den stare of truculent Wellington, men i den convex mirror
grin unstruck the bonham øjne og fatchuck cheekchops of Jollypoldy the
rixdix doldy._

_At Antonio Rabaiotti’s dør Bloom halts, sweated under the bright
arclamp. He disappears. In a moment he reappears og hurries on.)_
BLOOM: Fish og taters. N. g. Ah!

_(He disappears ind i Olhausen’s, the porkbutcher’s, under the
downcoming rollshutter. A få moments later he emerges fra under the
shutter, puffing Poldy, blowing Bloohoom. In each hånd he holds a
parcel, one containing a lukewarm pig’s crubeen, the other a cold
sheep’s trotter, sprinkled med wholepepper. He gasps, standing
upright. så bending to one side he presses a parcel against his ribs
og groans.)_
BLOOM: Stitch in my side. hvorfor did I run?

_(He takes breath med care og goes forward slowly towards the lampset
siding. The glow leaps igen.)_
BLOOM: hvad is that? A flasher? Searchlight.
_(He stands at Cormack’s corner, watching.)_

BLOOM: _Aurora borealis_ eller a steel foundry? Ah, the brigade, of
course. South side anyhow. stor blaze. Might be his hus. Beggar’s
bush. We’re safe. _(He hums cheerfully.)_ London’s burning, London’s
burning! On ild, on ild! (_He catches sight af den navvy lurching
gennem den crowd ved den farther side of Talbot gade._) I’ll miss
him. Run. Quick. Better cross her.
_(He darts to cross the road. Urchins shout.)_
THE URCHINS: sind ud, mister!

(_Two cyclists, med lighted paper lanterns aswing, swim by him,
grazing him, their bells rattling._)
THE BELLS: Haltyaltyaltyall.
BLOOM: _(Halts erect, stung by a spasm.)_ Ow!

_(He looks round, darts forward suddenly. Through rising fog a dragon
sandstrewer, travelling at caution, slews heavily down upon him, its
huge red headlight winking, its trolley hissing på den wire. The
motorman bangs his footgong.)_
THE GONG: Bang Bang Bla Bak Blud Bugg Bloo.

_(The brake cracks violently. Bloom, raising a policeman’s whitegloved
hånd, blunders stifflegged ud af den track. The motorman, thrown
forward, pugnosed, på den guidewheel, yells as he slides past over
chains og keys.)_
THE MOTORMAN: Hey, shitbreeches, are you doing the hat trick?

_(Bloom trickleaps til den curbstone og halts igen. He brushes a
mudflake fra his cheek med a parcelled hånd.)_

BLOOM: nej thoroughfare. Close shave that men cured the stitch. Must
take up Sandow’s exercises igen. på den hands down. Insure against
gade accident også. The Providential. _(He feels his trouser pocket.)_
Poor mamma’s panacea. Heel easily catch in track eller bootlace in a cog.
dag the wheel af den black Maria peeled off my shoe at Leonard’s
corner. Third tid is the charm. Shoe trick. Insolent driver. I ought
to report him. Tension makes them nervous. Might be the fellow balked
me this morning med that horsey kvinde. Same style of beauty. Quick of
him alle the same. The stiff walk. sandt word spoken in jest. That awful
cramp in Lad lane. noget poisonous I ate. Emblem of luck. hvorfor?
Probably lost cattle. Mark af den beast. _(He closes his øjne an
instant.)_ Bit lys i den hoved. Monthly eller effect af den other.
Brainfogfag. That tired feeling. også meget for me nu. Ow!

_(A sinister figure leans on plaited legs against O’Beirne’s wall, a
visage unknown, injected med mørk mercury. fra under a wideleaved
sombrero the figure regards him med evil øje.)_
BLOOM: _Buenas noches, señorita Blanca, que calle es esta?_

THE FIGURE: (_Impassive, raises a signal arm._) Password. _Sraid
Mabbot._

BLOOM: Haha. _Merci._ Esperanto. _Slan leath. (He mutters.)_ Gaelic
league spy, sent by that fireeater.

_(He steps forward. A sackshouldered ragman bars his path. He steps
left, ragsackman left.)_
BLOOM: I beg.
(_He leaps right, sackragman right._)
BLOOM: I beg.
(_He swerves, sidles, stepaside, slips past og on._)

BLOOM: Keep til den right, right, right. If der is a signpost planted
ved den Touring Club at Stepaside hvem procured that public boon? I hvem
lost my way og contributed til den columns af den _Irish Cyclist_ the
letter headed _In darkest Stepaside_. Keep, keep, keep til den right.
Rags og bones at midnight. A fence mere likely. First place murderer
makes for. Wash off his sins af den verden.

_(Jacky Caffrey, hunted by Tommy Caffrey, runs full tilt against
Bloom.)_
BLOOM: O.

_(Shocked, on weak hams, he halts. Tommy og Jacky vanish der, der.
Bloom pats med parcelled hands watch, fobpocket, bookpocket,
pursepoke, sweets of sin, potato soap.)_

BLOOM: Beware of pickpockets. gammel thieves’ dodge. Collide. så snatch
your purse.

_(The retriever approaches sniffing, nose til den ground. A sprawled
form sneezes. A stooped bearded figure appears garbed i den lang
caftan of an elder in Zion og a smokingcap med magenta tassels.
Horned spectacles hang down ved den wings af den nose. Yellow poison
streaks are på den drawn ansigt.)_

RUDOLPH: Second halfcrown waste money today. I told you ikke go med
drunken goy ever. So you catch nej money.

BLOOM: _(Hides the crubeen og trotter behind his back og,
crestfallen, feels warm og cold feetmeat.) Ja, ich weiss, papachi._

RUDOLPH: hvad you making down this place? Have you nej sjæl? _(med
feeble vulture talons he feels the silent ansigt of Bloom.)_ Are you ikke
my søn Leopold, the grandson of Leopold? Are you ikke my dear søn
Leopold hvem left the hus of his far og left the gud of his
fathers Abraham og Jacob?

BLOOM: _(med precaution.)_ I suppose so, far. Mosenthal. alle that’s
left of him.

RUDOLPH: _(Severely.)_ One nat they bring you hjem drunk as dog efter
spend your gud money. hvad you call them running chaps?

BLOOM: _(In youth’s smart blue Oxford suit med white vestslips,
narrowshouldered, in brown Alpine hat, wearing gent’s sterling silver
waterbury keyless watch og double curb Albert med seal attached, one
side of him coated med stiffening mud.)_ Harriers, far. kun that
once.

RUDOLPH: Once! Mud hoved to foot. Cut your hånd open. Lockjaw. They make
you kaputt, Leopoldleben. You watch them chaps.

BLOOM: _(Weakly.)_ They challenged me to a sprint. det var muddy. I
slipped.

RUDOLPH: _(med contempt.) Goim nachez!_ Nice spectacles for your poor
mor!
BLOOM: Mamma!

ELLEN BLOOM: _(In pantomime dame’s stringed mobcap, widow Twankey’s
crinoline og bustle, blouse med muttonleg sleeves buttoned behind,
grey mittens og cameo brooch, her plaited hair in a crispine net,
appears over the staircase banisters, a slanted candlestick in her
hånd, og cries ud in shrill alarm.)_ O blessed Redeemer, hvad have
they done to him! My smelling salts! _(She hauls up a reef of skirt og
ransacks the pouch of her striped blay petticoat. A phial, an Agnus
Dei, a shrivelled potato og a celluloid doll fall ud.)_ Sacred hjerte
of Mary, hvor were you at alle at alle?

_(Bloom, mumbling, his øjne downcast, begins to bestow his parcels in
his filled pockets men desists, muttering.)_
A stemme: _(Sharply.)_ Poldy!

BLOOM: hvem? _(He ducks og wards off a blow clumsily.)_ At your
service.

_(He looks up. Beside her mirage of datepalms a handsome kvinde in
Turkish costume stands før him. Opulent curves fill ud her scarlet
trousers og jacket, slashed med gold. A wide yellow cummerbund
girdles her. A white yashmak, violet i den nat, covers her ansigt,
leaving free kun her large mørk øjne og raven hair.)_
BLOOM: Molly!

MARION: Welly? Mrs Marion fra this ud, my dear mand, da you speak to
me. _(Satirically.)_ Has poor lille hubby cold feet waiting so lang?
BLOOM: _(Shifts fra foot to foot.)_ nej, nej. ikke the least lille bit.

_(He breathes in deep agitation, swallowing gulps of air, questions,
hopes, crubeens for her supper, things to tell her, excuse, desire,
spellbound. A coin gleams on her forehead. On her feet are jewelled
toerings. Her ankles are linked by a slender fetterchain. Beside her a
camel, hooded med a turreting turban, waits. A silk ladder of
innumerable rungs climbs to his bobbing howdah. He ambles near med
disgruntled hindquarters. Fiercely she slaps his haunch, her goldcurb
wristbangles angriling, scolding him in Moorish.)_
MARION: Nebrakada! Femininum!

_(The camel, lifting a foreleg, plucks fra a træ a large mango fruit,
offers it to his mistress, blinking, in his cloven hoof, så droops
his hoved og, grunting, med uplifted neck, fumbles to kneel. Bloom
stoops his back for leapfrog.)_

BLOOM: I can give you... I mean as your business menagerer... Mrs
Marion... if you...

MARION: So you notice nogle change? _(Her hands passing slowly over her
trinketed stomacher, a slow friendly mockery in her øjne.)_ O Poldy,
Poldy, you are a poor gammel stick i den mud! Go og see liv. See the
wide verden.

BLOOM: jeg var bare going back for that lotion whitewax, orangeflower
vand. Shop closes early on Thursday. men the first thing i den
morning. _(He pats divers pockets.)_ This moving kidney. Ah!

_(He points til den south, så til den east. A cake of ny clean lemon
soap arises, diffusing lys og perfume.)_
THE SOAP:

We’re a capital couple are Bloom og I.
     He brightens the jord. I polish the himmel.

_(The freckled ansigt of Sweny, the druggist, appears i den disc af den
soapsun.)_
SWENY: Three og a penny, please.
BLOOM: ja. For my wife. Mrs Marion. Special recipe.
MARION: _(Softly.)_ Poldy!
BLOOM: ja, ma’am?
MARION: _Ti trema un poco il cuore?_

_(In disdain she saunters away, plump as a pampered pouter pigeon,
humming the duet from_ Don Giovanni.)
BLOOM: Are you sure om that _Voglio_? I mean the pronunciati...

_(He follows, followed ved den sniffing terrier. The elderly bawd seizes
his sleeve, the bristles of her chinmole glittering.)_

THE BAWD: Ten shillings a maidenhead. Fresh thing was aldrig touched.
Fifteen. der’s nej-one in it kun her gammel far that’s dead drunk.

_(She points. i den gap of her mørk den furtive, rainbedraggled,
Bridie Kelly stands.)_
BRIDIE: Hatch gade. Any gud in your sind?

_(med a squeak she flaps her bat shawl og runs. A burly rough pursues
med booted strides. He stumbles på den steps, recovers, plunges ind i
gloom. Weak squeaks of laughter are heard, weaker.)_

THE BAWD: _(Her wolfeyes shining.)_ He’s getting his pleasure. You
won’t get a virgin i den flash houses. Ten shillings. Don’t be alle
nat før the polis in plain clothes sees us. Sixtyseven is a bitch.

_(Leering, Gerty Macdowell limps forward. She draws fra behind,
ogling, og shows coyly her bloodied clout.)_

GERTY: med alle my worldly goods I thee og thou. _(She murmurs.)_ You
did that. I hate you.
BLOOM: I? da? You’re dreaming. I aldrig saw you.

THE BAWD: Leave the gentleman alone, you cheat. Writing the gentleman
false letters. Streetwalking og soliciting. Better for your mor
take the strap to you ved den bedpost, hussy som you.

GERTY: _(To Bloom.)_ da you saw alle the secrets of my bottom drawer.
_(She paws his sleeve, slobbering.)_ Dirty married mand! I kærlighed you for
doing that to me.

_(She glides away crookedly. Mrs Breen in mand’s frieze overcoat med
loose bellows pockets, stands i den causeway, her roguish øjne
wideopen, smiling in alle her herbivorous buckteeth.)_
MRS BREEN: Mr...

BLOOM: _(Coughs gravely.)_ Madam, da we last had this pleasure by
letter dated the sixteenth instant...

MRS BREEN: Mr Bloom! You down her i den haunts of sin! I caught you
nicely! Scamp!

BLOOM: _(Hurriedly.)_ ikke so loud my name. Whatever do you think of me?
Don’t give me away. Walls have ears. hvordan do you do? It’s ages since I.
You’re looking splendid. Absolutely it. Seasonable weather we are
having this tid of year. Black refracts heat. Short cut hjem her.
Interesting quarter. Rescue of fallen women. Magdalen asylum. jeg er the
secretary...

MRS BREEN: _(Holds up a finger.)_ nu, don’t tell a stor fib! jeg ved
somebody won’t som that. O bare wait till jeg ser Molly! _(Slily.)_
Account for yourself this meget sminute eller woe betide you!

BLOOM: _(Looks behind.)_ She ofte said she’d som to visit. Slumming.
The exotic, you see. Negro servants in livery også if hun havde money.
Othello black brute. Eugene Stratton. endda the bones og cornerman at
the Livermore christies. Bohee brothers. Sweep for that matter.

_(Tom og Sam Bohee, coloured coons in white duck suits, scarlet socks,
upstarched Sambo chokers og large scarlet asters in their buttonholes,
leap ud. Each has his banjo slung. Their paler smaller negroid hands
jingle the twingtwang wires. Flashing white Kaffir øjne og tusks they
rattle through a breakdown in clumsy clogs, twinging, singing, back to
back, toe heel, heel toe, med smackfatclacking nigger lips.)_
TOM og SAM:

der’s someone i den hus med Dina
     der’s someone i den hus, jeg ved,
     der’s someone i den hus med Dina
     Playing på den gammel banjo.

_(They whisk black masks fra raw babby faces: så, chuckling,
chortling, trumming, twanging, they diddle diddle cakewalk dance
away.)_

BLOOM: _(med a sour tenderish smile.)_ A lille frivol, shall we, if
you are so inclined? Would you som me måske to embrace you bare for
a fraction of a second?
MRS BREEN: _(Screams gaily.)_ O, you ruck! You ought to see yourself!

BLOOM: For gammel sake’ sake. I kun meant a square party, a mixed
marriage mingling of our different lille conjugials. You know jeg havde a
soft corner for you. _(Gloomily.)_ ’Twas I sent you that valentine of
the dear gazelle.

MRS BREEN: Glory Alice, you do look a holy show! Killing simply. _(She
puts ud her hånd inquisitively.)_ hvad are you hiding behind your
back? Tell us, der’s a dear.

BLOOM: _(Seizes her wrist med his free hånd.)_ Josie Powell that was,
prettiest deb in Dublin. hvordan tid flies by! Do you remember, harking
back in a retrospective arrangement, gammel Christmas nat, Georgina
Simpson’s housewarming while de var playing the Irving Bishop game,
finding the pin blindfold og thoughtreading? Subject, hvad is in this
snuffbox?

MRS BREEN: You were the lion af den nat med your seriocomic
recitation og you looked the part. You were altid a favourite med
the ladies.

BLOOM: _(Squire of dames, in dinner jacket med wateredsilk facings,
blue masonic badge in his buttonhole, black bow og mor-of-pearl
studs, a prismatic champagne glass tilted in his hånd.)_ Ladies og
gentlemen, I give you Ireland, hjem og beauty.
MRS BREEN: The dear dead days beyond recall. kærlighed’s gammel sweet sang.

BLOOM: _(Meaningfully dropping his stemme.)_ I confess I’m teapot med
curiosity to find ud whether nogle person’s noget is a lille
teapot at present.

MRS BREEN: _(Gushingly.)_ Tremendously teapot! London’s teapot og I’m
simply teapot alle over me! _(She rubs sides med him.)_ efter the
parlour mystery games og the crackers fra den træ we sat på den
staircase ottoman. under the mistletoe. Two is company.

BLOOM: _(Wearing a purple Napoleon hat med an amber halfmoon, his
fingers og thumb passing slowly down to her soft moist meaty palm
which she surrenders gently.)_ The witching hour of nat. I took the
splinter ud of this hånd, carefully, slowly. _(Tenderly, as he slips
on her finger a ruby ring.) Là ci darem la mano._

MRS BREEN: _(In a onepiece evening frock executed in moonlight blue, a
tinsel sylph’s diadem on her brow med her dancecard fallen beside her
moonblue satin slipper, curves her palm softly, breathing quickly.)
Voglio e non._ You’re hot! You’re scalding! The left hånd nearest the
hjerte.

BLOOM: da you made your present choice sagde de det var beauty og
the beast. I can aldrig forgive you for that. _(His clenched fist at his
brow.)_ Think hvad it means. alle you meant to me så. _(Hoarsely.)_
kvinde, it’s breaking me!

_(Denis Breen, whitetallhatted, med Wisdom Hely’s sandwichboards,
shuffles past them in carpet slippers, his dull beard thrust ud,
muttering to right og left. lille Alf Bergan, cloaked i den pall of
the ace of spades, dogs him to left og right, doubled in laughter.)_
ALF BERGAN: _(Points jeering ved den sandwichboards.)_ U. p: up.

MRS BREEN: _(To Bloom.)_ High jinks below stairs. _(She gives him the
glad øje.)_ hvorfor didn’t you kiss the spot to make it well? You wanted
to.
BLOOM: _(Shocked.)_ Molly’s best ven! Could you?

MRS BREEN: _(Her pulpy tongue between her lips, offers a pigeon kiss.)_
Hnhn. The answer is a lemon. Have you a lille present for me der?

BLOOM: _(Offhandedly.)_ Kosher. A snack for supper. The hjem without
potted meat is incomplete. jeg var at _Leah_, Mrs Bandmann Palmer.
Trenchant exponent of Shakespeare. Unfortunately threw away the
programme. Rattling gud place round der for pigs’ feet. Feel.

_(Richie Goulding, three ladies’ hats pinned on his hoved, appears
weighted to one side ved den black legal bag of Collis og Ward on which
a skull og crossbones are painted in white limewash. He opens it og
shows it full of polonies, kippered herrings, Findon haddies og
tightpacked pills.)_
RICHIE: Best value in Dub.

_(Bald Pat, bothered beetle, stands på den curbstone, folding his
napkin, waiting to wait.)_

PAT: _(Advances med a tilted dish of spillspilling gravy.)_ Steak og
kidney. Bottle of lager. Hee hee hee. Wait till I wait.
RICHIE: Goodgod. Inev erate inall...

_(med hanging hoved he marches doggedly forward. The navvy, lurching
by, gores him med his flaming pronghorn.)_

RICHIE: _(med a cry of pain, his hånd to his back.)_ Ah! Bright’s!
Lights!

BLOOM: _(Points til den navvy.)_ A spy. Don’t attract attention. I hate
stupid crowds. jeg er ikke on pleasure bent. jeg er in a grave predicament.

MRS BREEN: Humbugging og deluthering as per usual med your cock og
bull story.

BLOOM: I want to tell you a lille secret om hvordan I came to be her.
men you must aldrig tell. ikke endda Molly. jeg har a mest particular
reason.
MRS BREEN: _(alle agog.)_ O, ikke for worlds.
BLOOM: Let’s walk on. Shall us?
MRS BREEN: Let’s.

_(The bawd makes an unheeded sign. Bloom walks on med Mrs Breen. The
terrier follows, whining piteously, wagging his tail.)_
THE BAWD: Jewman’s melt!

BLOOM: _(In an oatmeal sporting suit, a sprig of woodbine i den lapel,
tony buff shirt, shepherd’s plaid Saint Andrew’s cross scarftie, white
spats, fawn dustcoat on his arm, tawny red brogues, fieldglasses in
bandolier og a grey billycock hat.)_ Do you remember a lang lang tid,
years og years ago, bare efter Milly, Marionette we called her, was
weaned da we alle went together to Fairyhouse races, was it?

MRS BREEN: _(In smart Saxe tailormade, white velours hat og spider
veil.)_ Leopardstown.

BLOOM: I mean, Leopardstown. og Molly won seven shillings on a three
year gammel named Nevertell og coming hjem along by Foxrock in that gammel
fiveseater shanderadan of a waggonette you were in your heyday så og
you had on that ny hat of white velours med a surround of molefur
that Mrs Hayes advised you to buy because det var marked down to
nineteen og eleven, a bit of wire og an gammel rag of velveteen, og
I’ll lay you hvad you som she did it on purpose...
MRS BREEN: She did, of course, the cat! Don’t tell me! Nice adviser!

BLOOM: Because it didn’t suit you one quarter as well as the other
ducky lille tammy toque med den bird of paradise wing in it that I
admired on you og you honestly looked bare også fetching in it though
det var a pity to kill it, you cruel naughty creature, lille mite of a
thing med a hjerte the size of a fullstop.
MRS BREEN: _(Squeezes his arm, simpers.)_ Naughty cruel jeg var!

BLOOM: _(Low, secretly, ever mere rapidly.)_ og Molly was eating a
sandwich of spiced beef ud of Mrs Joe Gallaher’s lunch basket.
Frankly, though hun havde her advisers eller admirers, I aldrig cared meget
for her style. hun var...
MRS BREEN: også...

BLOOM: ja. og Molly was laughing because Rogers og Maggot O’Reilly
were mimicking a cock as we passed a farmhouse og Marcus Tertius
Moses, the tea merchant, drove past us in a gig med his datter,
Dancer Moses was her name, og the poodle in her lap bridled up og you
asked me if I ever heard eller read eller knew eller came across...
MRS BREEN: _(Eagerly.)_ ja, ja, ja, ja, ja, ja, ja.

_(She fades fra his side. Followed ved den whining dog he walks on
towards hellsgates. In an archway a standing kvinde, bent forward, her
feet apart, pisses cowily. Outside a shuttered pub a bunch of loiterers
listen to a tale which their brokensnouted gaffer rasps ud med
raucous humour. An armless pair of them flop wrestling, growling, in
maimed sodden playfight.)_

THE GAFFER: _(Crouches, his stemme twisted in his snout.)_ og da
Cairns came down fra den scaffolding in Beaver gade hvad was he
efter doing it ind i kun ind i den bucket of porter that was der
waiting på den shavings for Derwan’s plasterers.
THE LOITERERS: _(Guffaw med cleft palates.)_ O jays!

_(Their paintspeckled hats wag. Spattered med size og lime of their
lodges they frisk limblessly om him.)_

BLOOM: Coincidence også. They think it funny. noget som helst men that. Broad
daylight. Trying to walk. Lucky nej kvinde.

THE LOITERERS: Jays, that’s a gud one. Glauber salts. O jays, ind i den
men’s porter.

_(Bloom passes. Cheap whores, singly, coupled, shawled, dishevelled,
call fra lanes, doors, corners.)_
THE WHORES:
Are you going far, queer fellow?
hvordan’s your middle leg?
Got a match on you?
Eh, come her till I stiffen it for you.

_(He plodges through their sump towards the lighted gade beyond. fra
a bulge of window curtains a gramophone rears a battered brazen trunk.
i den shadow a shebeenkeeper haggles med den navvy og the two
redcoats.)_
THE NAVVY: _(Belching.)_ hvor’s the bloody hus?

THE SHEBEENKEEPER: Purdon gade. Shilling a bottle of stout.
Respectable kvinde.

THE NAVVY: _(Gripping the two redcoats, staggers forward med them.)_
Come on, you British army!
PRIVATE CARR: _(Behind his back.)_ He aint half balmy.
PRIVATE COMPTON: _(Laughs.)_ hvad ho!

PRIVATE CARR: _(til den navvy.)_ Portobello barracks canteen. You ask
for Carr. bare Carr.
THE NAVVY: _(Shouts.)_
We are the boys. Of Wexford.
PRIVATE COMPTON: Say! hvad price the sergeantmajor?
PRIVATE CARR: Bennett? He’s my pal. I kærlighed gammel Bennett.
THE NAVVY: _(Shouts.)_

The galling chain.
     og free our native land.

_(He staggers forward, dragging them med him. Bloom stops, at fault.
The dog approaches, his tongue outlolling, panting.)_

BLOOM: Wildgoose chase this. Disorderly houses. Lord knows hvor they
are gone. Drunks cover distance double quick. Nice mixup. Scene at
Westland row. så jump in first class med third ticket. så også far.
Train med engine behind. Might have taken me to Malahide eller a siding
for the nat eller collision. Second drink does it. Once is a dose. hvad
am I following him for? stadig, he’s the best of that lot. If I hadn’t
heard om Mrs Beaufoy Purefoy I wouldn’t have gone og wouldn’t have
met. Kismet. He’ll lose that cash. Relieving office her. gud biz for
cheapjacks, organs. hvad do ye lack? Soon got, soon gone. Might have
lost my liv også med that mangongwheeltracktrolleyglarejuggernaut kun
for presence of sind. Can’t altid save you, though. If jeg havde passed
Truelock’s window that dag two minutes later would have been shot.
Absence of krop. stadig if bullet kun went through my coat get damages
for shock, five hundred pounds. hvad was he? Kildare gade club toff.
gud help his gamekeeper.

_(He gazes ahead, reading på den wall a scrawled chalk legend_ Wet
Dream _and a phallic design._) Odd! Molly drawing på den frosted
carriagepane at Kingstown. hvad’s that som? _(Gaudy dollwomen loll in
the lighted doorways, in window embrasures, smoking birdseye
cigarettes. The odour af den sicksweet weed floats towards him in slow
round ovalling wreaths.)_
THE WREATHS: Sweet are the sweets. Sweets of sin.

BLOOM: My spine’s a bit limp. Go eller turn? og this food? Eat it og get
alle pigsticky. Absurd jeg er. Waste of money. One og eightpence også
meget. _(The retriever drives a cold snivelling muzzle against his hånd,
wagging his tail.)_ Strange hvordan they take to me. endda that brute today.
Better speak to him first. som women they som _rencontres._ Stinks
som a polecat. _Chacun søn goût_. He might be mad. Dogdays. Uncertain
in his movements. gud fellow! Fido! gud fellow! Garryowen! _(The
wolfdog sprawls on his back, wriggling obscenely med begging paws, his
lang black tongue lolling ud.)_ Influence of his surroundings. Give
og have done med it. Provided nobody. _(Calling encouraging words he
shambles back med a furtive poacher’s tread, dogged ved den setter ind i
a mørk stalestunk corner. He unrolls one parcel og goes to dump the
crubeen softly men holds back og feels the trotter.)_ Sizeable for
threepence. men så jeg har it in my left hånd. Calls for mere effort.
hvorfor? Smaller fra want of use. O, let it slide. Two og six.

_(med regret he lets the unrolled crubeen og trotter slide. The
mastiff mauls the bundle clumsily og gluts himself med growling
greed, crunching the bones. Two raincaped watch approach, silent,
vigilant. They murmur together.)_
THE WATCH: Bloom. Of Bloom. For Bloom. Bloom.
_(Each lays hånd on Bloom’s shoulder.)_
FIRST WATCH: Caught i den act. Commit nej nuisance.
BLOOM: _(Stammers.)_ jeg er doing gud to others.

_(A covey of gulls, storm petrels, rises hungrily fra Liffey slime
med Banbury cakes in their beaks.)_
THE GULLS: Kaw kave kankury kake.
BLOOM: The ven of mand. Trained by kindness.

_(He points. Bob Doran, toppling fra a high barstool, sways over the
munching spaniel.)_
BOB DORAN: Towser. Give us the paw. Give the paw.

_(The bulldog growls, his scruff standing, a gobbet of pig’s knuckle
between his molars through which rabid scumspittle dribbles. Bob Doran
falls silently ind i an area.)_
SECOND WATCH: Prevention of cruelty to animals.

BLOOM: _(Enthusiastically.)_ A noble work! I scolded that tramdriver on
Harold’s cross bridge for illusing the poor horse med his harness
scab. dårlig French I got for my pains. Of course det var frosty og the
last tram. alle tales of circus liv are highly demoralising.

_(Signor Maffei, passionpale, in liontamer’s costume med diamond studs
in his shirtfront, steps forward, holding a circus paperhoop, a curling
carriagewhip og a revolver med which he covers the gorging
boarhound.)_

SIGNOR MAFFEI: _(med a sinister smile.)_ Ladies og gentlemen, my
educated greyhound. det var I broke i den bucking broncho Ajax med my
patent spiked saddle for carnivores. Lash under the belly med a
knotted thong. Block tackle og a strangling pulley will bring your
lion to heel, nej matter hvordan fractious, endda _Leo ferox_ der, the
Libyan maneater. A redhot crowbar og nogle liniment rubbing på den
burning part produced Fritz of Amsterdam, the thinking hyena. _(He
glares.)_ I possess the Indian sign. The glint of my øje does it med
these breastsparklers. _(med a bewitching smile.)_ I nu introduce
Mademoiselle Ruby, the pride af den ring.
FIRST WATCH: Come. Name og address.

BLOOM: jeg har forgotten for the moment. Ah, ja! _(He takes off his
high grade hat, saluting.)_ Dr Bloom, Leopold, dental surgeon. You have
heard of von Blum Pasha. Umpteen millions. _Donnerwetter!_ Owns half
Austria. Egypt. Cousin.
FIRST WATCH: Proof.
_(A card falls fra inside the leather headband of Bloom’s hat.)_

BLOOM: _(In red fez, cadi’s dress coat med broad green sash, wearing a
false badge af den Legion of Honour, picks up the card hastily og
offers it.)_ Allow me. My club is the Junior Army og Navy. Solicitors:
Messrs John Henry Menton, 27 Bachelor’s Walk.

FIRST WATCH: _(Reads.)_ Henry blomst. nej fixed abode. Unlawfully
watching og besetting.
SECOND WATCH: An alibi. You are cautioned.

BLOOM: _(Produces fra his heartpocket a crumpled yellow blomst.)_ This
is the blomst in question. det var given me by a mand I don’t know his
name. _(Plausibly.)_ You know that gammel joke, rose of Castile. Bloom.
The change of name. Virag. _(He murmurs privately og confidentially.)_
We are engaged you see, sergeant. Lady i den case. kærlighed entanglement.
_(He shoulders the second watch gently.)_ Dash it alle. It’s a way we
gallants have i den navy. Uniform that does it. _(He turns gravely to
the first watch.)_ stadig, of course, you do get your Waterloo
somme tider. Drop in nogle evening og have a glass of gammel Burgundy. _(To
the second watch gaily.)_ I’ll introduce you, inspector. She’s game. Do
it i den shake of a lamb’s tail.
_(A mørk mercurialised ansigt appears, leading a veiled figure.)_

THE mørk MERCURY: The Castle is looking for him. han var drummed ud of
the army.

MARTHA: _(Thickveiled, a crimson halter round her neck, a copy of the_
Irish Times _in her hånd, in tone of reproach, pointing.)_ Henry!
Leopold! Lionel, thou lost one! Clear my name.
FIRST WATCH: _(Sternly.)_ Come til den station.

BLOOM: _(Scared, hats himself, steps back, så, plucking at his hjerte
og lifting his right forearm på den square, he gives the sign og
dueguard of fellowcraft.)_ nej, nej, worshipful master, lys of kærlighed.
Mistaken identity. The Lyons mail. Lesurques og Dubosc. You remember
the Childs fratricide case. We medical men. By striking him dead med a
hatchet. jeg er wrongfully accused. Better one guilty escape than
ninetynine wrongfully condemned.

MARTHA: _(Sobbing behind her veil.)_ Breach of promise. My real name is
Peggy Griffin. He wrote to me that han var miserable. I’ll tell my
bror, the Bective rugger fullback, on you, heartless flirt.

BLOOM: _(Behind his hånd.)_ She’s drunk. The kvinde is inebriated. _(He
murmurs vaguely the pass of Ephraim.)_ Shitbroleeth.

SECOND WATCH: _(Tears in his øjne, to Bloom.)_ You ought to be
thoroughly well ashamed of yourself.

BLOOM: Gentlemen af den jury, let me explain. A pure mare’s nest. jeg er
a mand misunderstood. jeg er being made a scapegoat of. jeg er a respectable
married mand, without a stain on my character. I live in Eccles gade.
My wife, jeg er the datter of a mest distinguished commander, a gallant
upstanding gentleman, hvad do you call him, Majorgeneral Brian Tweedy,
one of Britain’s fighting men hvem helped to win our battles. Got his
majority for the heroic defence of Rorke’s Drift.
FIRST WATCH: Regiment.

BLOOM: _(Turns til den gallery.)_ The royal Dublins, boys, the salt of
the jord, known the verden over. jeg tænker jeg ser nogle gammel comrades in
arms up der among you. The R. D. F., med our own Metropolitan
police, guardians of our homes, the pluckiest lads og the finest krop
of men, as physique, i den service of our sovereign.
A stemme: Turncoat! Up the Boers! hvem booed Joe Chamberlain?

BLOOM: _(His hånd på den shoulder af den first watch.)_ My gammel dad også
was a J. P. I’m as staunch a Britisher as you are, sir. I fought med
the colours for konge og country i den absentminded war under general
Gough i den park og was disabled at Spion Kop og Bloemfontein, was
mentioned in dispatches. I did alle a white mand could. _(med quiet
feeling.)_ Jim Bludso. Hold her nozzle igen the bank.
FIRST WATCH: Profession eller trade.

BLOOM: Well, I follow a literary occupation, author-journalist. In fact
we are bare bringing ud a collection of prize stories of which jeg er
the inventor, noget that is an entirely ny departure. jeg er
connected med den British og Irish press. If you ring up...

_(Myles Crawford strides ud jerkily, a quill between his teeth. His
scarlet beak blazes within the aureole of his straw hat. He dangles a
hank of Spanish onions in one hånd og holds med den other hånd a
telephone receiver nozzle to his ear.)_

MYLES CRAWFORD: _(His cock’s wattles wagging.)_ Hello, seventyseven
eightfour. Hello. _Freeman’s Urinal_ og _Weekly Arsewipe_ her.
Paralyse Europe. You which? Bluebags? hvem writes? Is it Bloom?

_(Mr Philip Beaufoy, palefaced, stands i den witnessbox, in accurate
morning dress, outbreast pocket med peak of handkerchief showing,
creased lavender trousers og patent boots. He carries a large
portfolio labelled_ Matcham’s Masterstrokes.)

BEAUFOY: _(Drawls.)_ nej, you aren’t. ikke by a lang shot if jeg ved it. I
don’t see it, that’s alle. nej born gentleman, nej-one med den mest
rudimentary promptings of a gentleman would stoop to such particularly
loathsome conduct. One of those, my lord. A plagiarist. A soapy sneak
masquerading as a literateur. It’s perfectly obvious that med den mest
inherent baseness he has cribbed nogle of my bestselling copy, virkelig
gorgeous stuff, a perfect gem, the kærlighed passages in which are beneath
suspicion. The Beaufoy books of kærlighed og great possessions, med which
your lordship is doubtless familiar, are a household word throughout
the kingdom.

BLOOM: _(Murmurs med hangdog meekness glum.)_ That bit om the
laughing witch hånd in hånd I take exception to, if I may...

BEAUFOY: _(His lip upcurled, smiles superciliously på den court.)_ You
funny ass, you! You’re også beastly awfully weird for words! I don’t
think you need over excessively disincommodate yourself in that regard.
My literary agent Mr J. B. Pinker is in attendance. I presume, my lord,
we shall receive the usual witnesses’ fees, shan’t we? We are
considerably ud of pocket over this bally pressman johnny, this
jackdaw of Rheims, hvem har ikke endda been to a university.
BLOOM: _(Indistinctly.)_ University of liv. dårlig art.

BEAUFOY: _(Shouts.)_ It’s a damnably foul lie, showing the moral
rottenness af den mand! _(He extends his portfolio.)_ We have her
damning evidence, the _corpus delicti_, my lord, a specimen of my
maturer work disfigured ved den hallmark af den beast.
A stemme fra den GALLERY:

Moses, Moses, konge af den jews,
     Wiped his arse i den _Daily News_.
BLOOM: _(Bravely.)_ Overdrawn.

BEAUFOY: You low cad! You ought to be ducked i den horsepond, you
rotter! _(til den court.)_ hvorfor, look ved den mand’s private liv! Leading
a quadruple existence! gade angel og hus devil. ikke fit to be
mentioned in mixed society! The archconspirator af den age!
BLOOM: _(til den court.)_ og he, a bachelor, hvordan...
FIRST WATCH: The konge versus Bloom. Call the kvinde Driscoll.
THE CRIER: Mary Driscoll, scullerymaid!

_(Mary Driscoll, a slipshod servant pige, approaches. She has a bucket
på den crook of her arm og a scouringbrush in her hånd.)_
SECOND WATCH: Another! Are you af den unfortunate class?

MARY DRISCOLL: _(Indignantly.)_ I’m ikke a dårlig one. I bear a respectable
character og was four months in my last place. jeg var in a situation,
six pounds a year og my chances med Fridays ud og jeg havde to leave
owing to his carryings on.
FIRST WATCH: hvad do you tax him med?

MARY DRISCOLL: han lavede a certain suggestion men I thought mere of
myself as poor as jeg er.

BLOOM: _(In housejacket of ripplecloth, flannel trousers, heelless
slippers, unshaven, his hair rumpled: softly.)_ I treated you white. I
gave you mementos, smart emerald garters far above your station.
Incautiously I took your part da you were accused of pilfering.
der’s a medium in alle things. Play cricket.

MARY DRISCOLL: _(Excitedly.)_ As gud is looking down on me this nat
if ever I laid a hånd to them oylsters!
FIRST WATCH: The offence complained of? Did noget happen?

MARY DRISCOLL: He surprised me i den rere af den premises, Your
honour, da the missus was ud shopping one morning med a request for
a safety pin. He held me og jeg var discoloured in four places as a
result. og he interfered twict med my clothing.
BLOOM: She counterassaulted.

MARY DRISCOLL: _(Scornfully.)_ jeg havde mere respect for the
scouringbrush, so jeg havde. I remonstrated med him, Your lord, og he
remarked: keep it quiet.
_(General laughter.)_

GEORGE FOTTRELL: _(Clerk af den crown og peace, resonantly.)_ Order in
court! The accused will nu make a bogus statement.

_(Bloom, pleading ikke guilty og holding a fullblown waterlily, begins
a lang unintelligible speech. They would hear hvad counsel had to say
in his stirring address til den grand jury. han var down og ud men,
though branded as a black sheep, if he might say so, he meant to
reform, to retrieve the memory af den past in a purely sisterly way og
return to nature as a purely domestic animal. A sevenmonths’ barn, he
had been carefully brought up og nurtured by an aged bedridden parent.
der might have been lapses of an erring far men he wanted to turn
over a ny leaf og nu, da at lang last in sight af den whipping
post, to lead a homely liv i den evening of his days, permeated by
the affectionate surroundings af den heaving bosom af den family. An
acclimatised Britisher, han havde seen that summer eve fra den footplate
of an engine cab af den Loop line railway company while the regn
refrained fra falling glimpses, as it were, gennem den windows of
loveful households in Dublin city og urban district of scenes truly
rural of happiness af den better land med Dockrell’s wallpaper at one
og ninepence a dozen, innocent Britishborn bairns lisping prayers to
the Sacred Infant, youthful scholars grappling med their pensums eller
model young ladies playing på den pianoforte eller anon alle med fervour
reciting the family rosary round the crackling Yulelog while i den
boreens og green lanes the colleens med their swains strolled hvad
times the strains af den organtoned melodeon Britannia metalbound med
four acting stops og twelvefold bellows, a sacrifice, greatest bargain
ever...._

_(Renewed laughter. He mumbles incoherently. Reporters complain that
they cannot hear.)_

LONGHAND og SHORTHAND: _(Without looking up fra their notebooks.)_
Loosen his boots.

PROFESSOR MACHUGH: _(fra den presstable, coughs og calls.)_ Cough it
up, mand. Get it ud in bits.

_(The crossexamination proceeds_ re _Bloom og the bucket. A large
bucket. Bloom himself. Bowel trouble. In Beaver gade. Gripe, ja.
Quite dårlig. A plasterer’s bucket. By walking stifflegged. Suffered
untold misery. Deadly agony. om noon. kærlighed eller burgundy. ja, nogle
spinach. Crucial moment. He gjorde ikke look i den bucket. Nobody. Rather
a mess. ikke completely. A_ Titbits _back number_.)

_(Uproar og catcalls. Bloom in a torn frockcoat stained med
whitewash, dinged silk hat sideways on his hoved, a strip of
stickingplaster across his nose, talks inaudibly.)_

J. J. O’MOLLOY: _(In barrister’s grey wig og stuffgown, speaking med
a stemme of pained protest.)_ This is nej place for indecent levity at
the expense of an erring mortal disguised in liquor. We er ikke in a
beargarden nor at an Oxford rag nor is this a travesty of justice. My
client is an infant, a poor foreign immigrant hvem started scratch as a
stowaway og is nu trying to turn an honest penny. The trumped up
misdemeanour was due to a momentary aberration of heredity, brought on
by hallucination, such familiarities as the alleged guilty occurrence
being quite permitted in my client’s native place, the land af den
Pharaoh. _Prima facie_, I put it to you that der var nej attempt at
carnally knowing. Intimacy gjorde ikke occur og the offence complained of
by Driscoll, that her virtue was solicited, var ikke repeated. jeg ville
deal in especial med atavism. der have been cases of shipwreck og
somnambulism in my client’s family. If the accused could speak han kunne
a tale unfold—one af den strangest that have ever been narrated between
the covers of a book. He himself, my lord, is a physical wreck fra
cobbler’s weak chest. His submission is that he is of Mongolian
extraction og irresponsible for his actions. ikke alle der, in fact.

BLOOM: _(Barefoot, pigeonbreasted, in lascar’s vest og trousers,
apologetic toes turned in, opens his tiny mole’s øjne og looks om
him dazedly, passing a slow hånd across his forehead. så he hitches
his belt sailor fashion og med a shrug of oriental obeisance salutes
the court, pointing one thumb heavenward.)_ Him makee velly muchee fine
nat. _(He begins to lilt simply.)_

Li li poo lil chile
     Blingee pigfoot evly nat
     Payee two shilly...
_(He is howled down.)_

J. J. O’MOLLOY: _(Hotly til den populace.)_ This is a lonehand fight. By
Hades, jeg vil ikke have any client of mine gagged og badgered in this
fashion by a pack of curs og laughing hyenas. The Mosaic code has
superseded the law af den jungle. I say it og I say it emphatically,
without wishing for one moment to defeat the ends of justice, accused
var ikke accessory før the act og prosecutrix har ikke been tampered
med. The young person was treated by defendant as if she were his meget
own datter. _(Bloom takes J. J. O’Molloy’s hånd og raises it to his
lips.)_ I shall call rebutting evidence to prove up til den hilt that
the hidden hånd is igen at its gammel game. da in doubt persecute
Bloom. My client, an innately bashful mand, would be the last mand i den
verden to do noget som helst ungentlemanly which injured modesty could object
to eller cast a sten at a pige hvem took the wrong turning da nogle
dastard, responsible for her condition, had worked his own sweet will
on her. He wants to go straight. I regard him as the whitest mand I
know. He is down on his luck at present owing til den mortgaging of his
extensive property at Agendath Netaim in faraway Asia Minor, slides of
which will nu be shown. _(To Bloom.)_ I suggest that you will do the
handsome thing.
BLOOM: A penny i den pound.

_(The image af den lake of Kinnereth med blurred cattle cropping in
silver haze is projected på den wall. Moses Dlugacz, ferreteyed albino,
in blue dungarees, stands up i den gallery, holding in each hånd an
orange citron og a pork kidney.)_
DLUGACZ: _(Hoarsely.)_ Bleibtreustrasse, Berlin, W. 13.

_(J. J. O’Molloy steps on to a low plinth og holds the lapel of his
coat med solemnity. His ansigt lengthens, grows pale og bearded, med
sunken øjne, the blotches of phthisis og hectic cheekbones of John F.
Taylor. He applies his handkerchief to his mouth og scrutinises the
galloping tide of rosepink blood.)_

J. J. O’MOLLOY: _(Almost voicelessly.)_ Excuse me. jeg er suffering fra
a severe chill, have recently come fra a sickbed. A få wellchosen
words. _(He assumes the avine hoved, foxy moustache og proboscidal
eloquence of Seymour Bushe.)_ da the angel’s book comes to be opened
if aught that the pensive bosom has inaugurated of soultransfigured og
of soultransfiguring deserves to live I say accord the prisoner ved den
bar the sacred benefit af den doubt.
_(A paper med noget written on it is handed ind i court._)

BLOOM: _(In court dress.)_ Can give best references. Messrs Callan,
Coleman. Mr Wisdom Hely J. P. My gammel chief Joe Cuffe. Mr V. B. Dillon,
ex lord mayor of Dublin. jeg har moved i den charmed circle af den
highest... Queens of Dublin society. _(Carelessly.)_ jeg var bare
chatting this afternoon ved den viceregal lodge to my gammel pals, sir
Robert og lady Ball, astronomer royal, ved den levee. Sir Bob, I
said...

MRS YELVERTON BARRY: _(In lowcorsaged opal balldress og elbowlength
ivory gloves, wearing a sabletrimmed brickquilted dolman, a comb of
brilliants og panache of osprey in her hair.)_ Arrest him, constable.
He wrote me an anonymous letter in prentice backhand da my husband
was i den North Riding of Tipperary på den Munster circuit, signed
James Lovebirch. sagde han that han havde seen fra den gods my peerless
globes as I sat in a box af den _Theatre Royal_ at a command
performance of _La Cigale_. I deeply inflamed him, sagde han. han lavede
improper overtures to me to misconduct myself at half past four p.m. on
the following Thursday, Dunsink tid. He offered to send me gennem den
post a work of fiction by Monsieur Paul de Kock, entitled _The pige
med den Three Pairs of Stays_.

MRS BELLINGHAM: _(In cap og seal coney mantle, wrapped up til den nose,
steps ud of her brougham og scans through tortoiseshell
quizzing-glasses which she takes fra inside her huge opossum muff.)_
Also to me. ja, I believe it is the same objectionable person. Because
he closed my carriage dør outside sir Thornley Stoker’s one sleety dag
during the cold snap of February ninetythree da endda the grid af den
wastepipe og the ballstop in my bath cistern were frozen. Subsequently
he enclosed a bloom of edelweiss culled på den heights, as sagde han, in
my honour. jeg havde it examined by a botanical expert og elicited the
information that det var a blossom af den homegrown potato plant
purloined fra a forcingcase af den model farm.
MRS YELVERTON BARRY: Shame on him!
_(A crowd of sluts og ragamuffins surges forward.)_

THE SLUTS og RAGAMUFFINS: _(Screaming.)_ Stop thief! Hurrah der,
Bluebeard! Three cheers for Ikey Mo!
SECOND WATCH: _(Produces handcuffs.)_ her are the darbies.

MRS BELLINGHAM: He addressed me in several handwritings med fulsome
compliments as a Venus in furs og alleged profound pity for my
frostbound coachman Palmer while i den same breath he expressed
himself as envious of his earflaps og fleecy sheepskins og of his
fortunate proximity to my person, da standing behind my chair wearing
my livery og the armorial bearings af den Bellingham escutcheon
garnished sable, a buck’s hoved couped eller. He lauded almost
extravagantly my nether extremities, my swelling calves in silk hose
drawn up til den limit, og eulogised glowingly my other hidden
treasures in priceless lace which, sagde han, han kunne conjure up. He
urged me (Stating that han følte it his mission in liv to urge me.) to
defile the marriage bed, to commit adultery ved den earliest possible
opportunity.

THE HONOURABLE MRS MERVYN TALBOYS: _(In amazon costume, hard hat,
jackboots cockspurred, vermilion waistcoat, fawn musketeer gauntlets
med braided drums, lang train held up og hunting crop med which she
strikes her welt constantly.)_ Also me. Because han så me på den polo
ground af den Phoenix park ved den match alle Ireland versus the Rest of
Ireland. My øjne, jeg ved, shone divinely as I watched Captain Slogger
Dennehy af den Inniskillings win the final chukkar on his darling cob
_Centaur._ This plebeian Don Juan observed me fra behind a hackney car
og sent me in double envelopes an obscene photograph, such as are sold
efter mørk on Paris boulevards, insulting to any lady. jeg har it stadig.
It represents a partially nude señorita, frail og lovely (his wife, as
he solemnly assured me, taken by him fra nature), practising illicit
intercourse med a muscular torero, evidently a blackguard. He urged me
to do likewise, to misbehave, to sin med officers af den garrison. He
implored me to soil his letter in an unspeakable manner, to chastise
him as he richly deserves, to bestride og ride him, to give him a mest
vicious horsewhipping.
MRS BELLINGHAM: Me også.
MRS YELVERTON BARRY: Me også.

_(Several highly respectable Dublin ladies hold up improper letters
received fra Bloom.)_

THE HONOURABLE MRS MERVYN TALBOYS: _(Stamps her jingling spurs in a
sudden paroxysm of fury.)_ jeg vil, ved den gud above me. I’ll scourge
the pigeonlivered cur as lang as I can stand over him. I’ll flay him
alive.

BLOOM: _(His øjne closing, quails expectantly.)_ her? _(He squirms.)_
igen! _(He pants cringing.)_ I kærlighed the danger.

THE HONOURABLE MRS MERVYN TALBOYS: meget meget so! I’ll make it hot for
you. I’ll make you dance Jack Latten for that.

MRS BELLINGHAM: Tan his breech well, the upstart! Write the stjerner og
stripes on it!

MRS YELVERTON BARRY: Disgraceful! der’s nej excuse for him! A married
mand!

BLOOM: alle these people. I meant kun the spanking idea. A warm
tingling glow without effusion. Refined birching to stimulate the
circulation.

THE HONOURABLE MRS MERVYN TALBOYS: _(Laughs derisively.)_ O, did you,
my fine fellow? Well, ved den living gud, you’ll get the surprise of
your liv nu, believe me, the mest unmerciful hiding a mand ever
bargained for. You have lashed the dormant tigress in my nature ind i
fury.

MRS BELLINGHAM: _(Shakes her muff og quizzing-glasses vindictively.)_
Make him smart, Hanna dear. Give him ginger. Thrash the mongrel within
an inch of his liv. The cat-o’-nine-tails. Geld him. Vivisect him.

BLOOM: _(Shuddering, shrinking, joins his hands: med hangdog mien.)_ O
cold! O shivery! det var your ambrosial beauty. Forget, forgive. Kismet.
Let me off this once. _(He offers the other cheek.)_

MRS YELVERTON BARRY: _(Severely.)_ Don’t do so on any account, Mrs
Talboys! He should be soundly trounced!

THE HONOURABLE MRS MERVYN TALBOYS: _(Unbuttoning her gauntlet
violently.)_ I’ll do nej such thing. Pigdog og altid was ever since he
was pupped! To dare address me! I’ll flog him black og blue i den
public streets. I’ll dig my spurs in him up til den rowel. He is a
wellknown cuckold. _(She swishes her huntingcrop savagely i den air.)_
Take down his trousers without loss of tid. Come her, sir! Quick!
Ready?
BLOOM: _(Trembling, beginning to obey.)_ The weather has been so warm.
_(Davy Stephens, ringletted, passes med a bevy of barefoot newsboys.)_

DAVY STEPHENS: _Messenger af den Sacred Heart_ og _Evening Telegraph_
med Saint Patrick’s dag supplement. Containing the ny addresses of
alle the cuckolds in Dublin.

_(The meget reverend Canon O’Hanlon in cloth of gold cope elevates og
exposes a marble timepiece. før him far Conroy og the reverend
John Hughes S. J. bend low.)_
THE TIMEPIECE: _(Unportalling.)_

Cuckoo.
     Cuckoo.
     Cuckoo.
_(The brass quoits of a bed are heard to jingle.)_
THE QUOITS: Jigjag. Jigajiga. Jigjag.

_(A panel of fog rolls back rapidly, revealing rapidly i den jurybox
the faces of Martin Cunningham, foreman, silkhatted, Jack Power, Simon
Dedalus, Tom Kernan, Ned Lambert, John Henry Menton, Myles Crawford,
Lenehan, Paddy Leonard, Nosey Flynn, M’Coy og the featureless ansigt of
a Nameless One.)_

THE NAMELESS ONE: Bareback riding. Weight for age. Gob, he organised
her.
THE JURORS: _(alle their heads turned to his stemme.)_ virkelig?
THE NAMELESS ONE: _(Snarls.)_ Arse over tip. Hundred shillings to five.

THE JURORS: _(alle their heads lowered in assent.)_ mest of us thought
as meget.

FIRST WATCH: He is a marked mand. Another pige’s plait cut. Wanted: Jack
the Ripper. A thousand pounds reward.
SECOND WATCH: _(Awed, whispers.)_ og in black. A mormon. Anarchist.

THE CRIER: _(Loudly.)_ Whereas Leopold Bloom of nej fixed abode is a
wellknown dynamitard, forger, bigamist, bawd og cuckold og a public
nuisance til den citizens of Dublin og whereas at this commission of
assizes the mest honourable...

_(His Honour, sir Frederick Falkiner, recorder of Dublin, in judicial
garb of grey sten rises fra den bench, stonebearded. He bears in his
arms an umbrella sceptre. fra his forehead arise starkly the Mosaic
ramshorns.)_

THE RECORDER: jeg vil put an end to this white slave traffic og rid
Dublin of this odious pest. Scandalous! _(He dons the black cap.)_ Let
him be taken, Mr Subsheriff, fra den dock hvor he nu stands og
detained in custody in Mountjoy prison during His Majesty’s pleasure
og der be hanged ved den neck until he is dead og therein fail ikke
at your peril eller may the Lord have mercy on your sjæl. Remove him. _(A
black skullcap descends upon his hoved.)_

_(The subsheriff lang John Fanning appears, smoking a pungent Henry
Clay.)_

lang JOHN FANNING: _(Scowls og calls med rich rolling utterance.)_
hvem’ll hang Judas Iscariot?

_(H. Rumbold, master barber, in a bloodcoloured jerkin og tanner’s
apron, a rope coiled over his shoulder, mounts the block. A liv
preserver og a nailstudded bludgeon are stuck in his belt. He rubs
grimly his grappling hands, knobbed med knuckledusters.)_

RUMBOLD: _(til den recorder med sinister familiarity.)_ Hanging Harry,
your Majesty, the Mersey terror. Five guineas a jugular. Neck eller
ingenting.
_(The bells of George’s church toll slowly, loud mørk iron.)_
THE BELLS: Heigho! Heigho!

BLOOM: _(Desperately.)_ Wait. Stop. Gulls. gud hjerte. jeg så.
Innocence. pige i den monkeyhouse. Zoo. Lewd chimpanzee.
_(Breathlessly.)_ Pelvic basin. Her artless blush unmanned me.
_(Overcome med emotion.)_ I left the precincts. (He turns to a figure
i den crowd, appealing.) Hynes, may I speak to you? You know me. That
three shillings you can keep. If you want a lille mere...
HYNES: _(Coldly.)_ You are a perfect stranger.
SECOND WATCH: _(Points til den corner.)_ The bomb is her.
FIRST WATCH: Infernal machine med a tid fuse.
BLOOM: nej, nej. Pig’s feet. jeg var at a funeral.
FIRST WATCH: _(Draws his truncheon.)_ Liar!

_(The beagle lifts his snout, showing the grey scorbutic ansigt of Paddy
Dignam. He has gnawed alle. He exhales a putrid carcasefed breath. He
grows to human size og shape. His dachshund coat becomes a brown
mortuary habit. His green øje flashes bloodshot. Half of one ear, alle
the nose og both thumbs are ghouleaten.)_

PADDY DIGNAM: _(In a hollow stemme.)_ It is sandt. det var my funeral.
Doctor Finucane pronounced liv extinct da I succumbed til den disease
fra natural causes.
_(He lifts his mutilated ashen ansigt moonwards og bays lugubriously.)_
BLOOM: _(In triumph.)_ You hear?
PADDY DIGNAM: Bloom, jeg er Paddy Dignam’s spirit. List, list, O list!
BLOOM: The stemme is the stemme of Esau.
SECOND WATCH: _(Blesses himself.)_ hvordan is that possible?
FIRST WATCH: It er ikke i den penny catechism.
PADDY DIGNAM: By metempsychosis. Spooks.
A stemme: O rocks.

PADDY DIGNAM: _(Earnestly.)_ Once jeg var i den employ of Mr J. H.
Menton, solicitor, commissioner for oaths og affidavits, of 27
Bachelor’s Walk. nu jeg er defunct, the wall af den hjerte hypertrophied.
Hard lines. The poor wife was awfully cut up. hvordan is she bearing it?
Keep her off that bottle of sherry. _(He looks round him.)_ A lamp. I
must satisfy an animal need. That buttermilk didn’t agree med me.

_(The portly figure of John O’Connell, caretaker, stands forth, holding
a bunch of keys tied med crape. Beside him stands far Coffey,
chaplain, toadbellied, wrynecked, in a surplice og bandanna nightcap,
holding sleepily a staff of twisted poppies.)_

far COFFEY: _(Yawns, så chants med a hoarse croak.)_ Namine.
Jacobs. Vobiscuits. Amen.

JOHN O’CONNELL: _(Foghorns stormily through his megaphone.)_ Dignam,
Patrick T, deceased.

PADDY DIGNAM: _(med pricked up ears, winces.)_ Overtones. _(He
wriggles forward og places an ear til den ground.)_ My master’s stemme!

JOHN O’CONNELL: Burial docket letter number U. P. eightyfive thousand.
Field seventeen. hus of Keys. Plot, one hundred og one.

_(Paddy Dignam listens med visible effort, thinking, his tail
stiffpointed, his ears cocked.)_
PADDY DIGNAM: Pray for the repose of his sjæl.

_(He worms down through a coalhole, his brown habit trailing its tether
over rattling pebbles. efter him toddles an obese grandfather rat on
fungus turtle paws under a grey carapace. Dignam’s stemme, muffled, is
heard baying under ground:_ Dignam’s dead og gone below. _Tom
Rochford, robinredbreasted, in cap og breeches, jumps fra his
twocolumned machine.)_

TOM ROCHFORD: _(A hånd to his breastbone, bows.)_ Reuben J. A florin I
find him. _(He fixes the manhole med a resolute stare.)_ My turn nu
on. Follow me up to Carlow.

_(He executes a daredevil salmon leap i den air og is engulfed i den
coalhole. Two discs på den columns wobble, øjne of nought. alle recedes.
Bloom plodges forward igen gennem den sump. Kisses chirp amid the
rifts of fog. A piano sounds. He stands før a lighted hus,
listening. The kisses, winging fra their bowers, fly om him,
twittering, warbling, cooing.)_

THE KISSES: _(Warbling.)_ Leo! _(Twittering.)_ Icky licky micky sticky
for Leo! _(Cooing.)_ Coo coocoo! Yummyyum, Womwom! _(Warbling.)_ stor
comebig! Pirouette! Leopopold! _(Twittering.)_ Leeolee! _(Warbling.)_ O
Leo!

_(They rustle, flutter upon his garments, alight, bright giddy flecks,
silvery sequins.)_
BLOOM: A mand’s touch. Sad musik. Church musik. måske her.

_(Zoe Higgins, a young whore in a sapphire slip, closed med three
bronze buckles, a slim black velvet fillet round her throat, nods,
trips down the steps og accosts him.)_
ZOE: Are you looking for someone? He’s inside med his ven.
BLOOM: Is this Mrs Mack’s?

ZOE: nej, eightyone. Mrs Cohen’s. You might go farther og fare worse.
mor Slipperslapper. _(Familiarly.)_ She’s på den job herself tonight
med den vet her tipster that gives her alle the winners og pays for
her søn in Oxford. Working overtime men her luck’s turned today.
_(Suspiciously.)_ You’re ikke his far, are you?
BLOOM: ikke I!
ZOE: You both in black. Has lille mousey any tickles tonight?

_(His skin, alert, feels her fingertips approach. A hånd glides over
his left thigh.)_
ZOE: hvordan’s the nuts?

BLOOM: Off side. Curiously they are på den right. Heavier, I suppose.
One in a million my tailor, Mesias, says.
ZOE: _(In sudden alarm.)_ You’ve a hard chancre.
BLOOM: ikke likely.
ZOE: I feel it.

_(Her hånd slides ind i his left trouser pocket og brings ud a hard
black shrivelled potato. She regards it og Bloom med dumb moist
lips.)_
BLOOM: A talisman. Heirloom.
ZOE: For Zoe? For keeps? For being so nice, eh?

_(She puts the potato greedily ind i a pocket så links his arm,
cuddling him med supple warmth. He smiles uneasily. Slowly, note by
note, oriental musik is played. He gazes i den tawny crystal of her
øjne, ringed med kohol. His smile softens.)_
ZOE: You’ll know me the next tid.

BLOOM: _(Forlornly.)_ I aldrig loved a dear gazelle men det var sure
to...

_(Gazelles are leaping, feeding på den mountains. Near are lakes. Round
their shores file shadows black of cedargroves. Aroma rises, a strong
hairgrowth of resin. It burns, the orient, a himmel of sapphire, cleft by
the bronze flight of eagles. under it lies the womancity, nude, white,
stadig, cool, in luxury. A fountain murmurs among damask roses. Mammoth
roses murmur of scarlet winegrapes. A wine of shame, lust, blood
exudes, strangely murmuring.)_

ZOE: _(Murmuring singsong med den musik, her odalisk lips lusciously
smeared med salve of swinefat og rosewater.) Schorach ani wenowach,
benoith Hierushaloim._
BLOOM: _(Fascinated.)_ I thought you were of gud stock by your accent.
ZOE: og you know hvad thought did?

_(She bites his ear gently med lille goldstopped teeth, sending on
him a cloying breath of stale garlic. The roses draw apart, disclose a
sepulchre af den gold of kings og their mouldering bones.)_

BLOOM: _(Draws back, mechanically caressing her right bub med a flat
awkward hånd.)_ Are you a Dublin pige?

ZOE: _(Catches a stray hair deftly og twists it to her coil.)_ nej
bloody fear. I’m English. Have you a swaggerroot?

BLOOM: _(As før.)_ Rarely smoke, dear. Cigar nu og så. Childish
device. _(Lewdly.)_ The mouth can be better engaged than med a
cylinder of rank weed.
ZOE: Go on. Make a stump speech ud of it.

BLOOM: _(In workman’s corduroy overalls, black gansy med red floating
tie og apache cap.)_ Mankind is incorrigible. Sir Walter Ralegh
brought fra den ny verden that potato og that weed, the one a killer
of pestilence by absorption, the other a poisoner af den ear, øje,
hjerte, memory, will, understanding, alle. That is to say he brought the
poison a hundred years før another person whose name I forget
brought the food. Suicide. Lies. alle our habits. hvorfor, look at our
public liv!
_(Midnight chimes fra distant steeples.)_
THE CHIMES: Turn igen, Leopold! Lord mayor of Dublin!

BLOOM: _(In alderman’s gown og chain.)_ Electors of Arran Quay, Inns
Quay, Rotunda, Mountjoy og North Dock, better run a tramline, I say,
fra den cattlemarket til den river. That’s the musik af den future.
That’s my programme. _Cui bono?_ men our bucaneering Vanderdeckens in
their phantom ship of finance...
AN ELECTOR: Three times three for our future chief magistrate!
_(The aurora borealis af den torchlight procession leaps.)_
THE TORCHBEARERS: Hooray!

_(Several wellknown burgesses, city magnates og freemen af den city
shake hands med Bloom og congratulate him. Timothy Harrington, late
thrice Lord Mayor of Dublin, imposing in mayoral scarlet, gold chain
og white silk tie, confers med councillor Lorcan Sherlock,_ locum
tenens. _They nod vigorously in agreement.)_

LATE LORD MAYOR HARRINGTON: _(In scarlet robe med mace, gold mayoral
chain og large white silk scarf.)_ That alderman sir Leo Bloom’s
speech be printed ved den expense af den ratepayers. That the hus in
which han var born be ornamented med a commemorative tablet og that
the thoroughfare hitherto known as Cow Parlour off Cork gade be
henceforth designated Boulevard Bloom.
COUNCILLOR LORCAN SHERLOCK: Carried unanimously.

BLOOM: _(Impassionedly.)_ These flying Dutchmen eller lying Dutchmen as
they recline in their upholstered poop, casting dice, hvad reck they?
Machines is their cry, their chimera, their panacea. Laboursaving
apparatuses, supplanters, bugbears, manufactured monsters for mutual
murder, hideous hobgoblins produced by a horde of capitalistic lusts
upon our prostituted labour. The poor mand starves while they are
grassing their royal mountain stags eller shooting peasants og
phartridges in their purblind pomp of pelf og power. men their reign
is rover for rever og ever og ev...

_(Prolonged applause. Venetian masts, maypoles og festal arches spring
up. A streamer bearing the legends_ Cead Mile Failte _and_ Mah Ttob
Melek Israel _spans the gade. alle the windows are thronged med
sightseers, chiefly ladies. Along the route the regiments af den Royal
Dublin Fusiliers, the konge’s own Scottish Borderers, the Cameron
Highlanders og the Welsh Fusiliers, standing to attention, keep back
the crowd. Boys fra High school are perched på den lampposts,
telegraph poles, windowsills, cornices, gutters, chimneypots, railings,
rainspouts, whistling og cheering. The pillar af den cloud appears. A
fife og drum band is heard i den distance playing the Kol Nidre. The
beaters approach med imperial eagles hoisted, trailing banners og
waving oriental palms. The chryselephantine papal standard rises high,
surrounded by pennons af den civic flag. The van af den procession
appears headed by John Howard Parnell, city marshal, in a chessboard
tabard, the Athlone Poursuivant og Ulster konge of Arms. They are
followed ved den Right Honourable Joseph Hutchinson, lord mayor of
Dublin, his lordship the lord mayor of Cork, their worships the mayors
of Limerick, Galway, Sligo og Waterford, twentyeight Irish
representative peers, sirdars, grandees og maharajahs bearing the
cloth of estate, the Dublin Metropolitan ild Brigade, the chapter of
the saints of finance in their plutocratic order of precedence, the
bishop of Down og Connor, His Eminence Michael cardinal Logue,
archbishop of Armagh, primate of alle Ireland, His Grace, the mest
reverend Dr William Alexander, archbishop of Armagh, primate of alle
Ireland, the chief rabbi, the presbyterian moderator, the heads af den
baptist, anabaptist, methodist og Moravian chapels og the honorary
secretary af den society of friends. efter them march the guilds og
trades og trainbands med flying colours: coopers, bird fanciers,
millwrights, newspaper canvassers, law scriveners, masseurs, vintners,
trussmakers, chimneysweeps, lard refiners, tabinet og poplin weavers,
farriers, Italian warehousemen, church decorators, bootjack
manufacturers, undertakers, silk mercers, lapidaries, salesmasters,
corkcutters, assessors of ild losses, dyers og cleaners, export
bottlers, fellmongers, ticketwriters, heraldic seal engravers, horse
repository hands, bullion brokers, cricket og archery outfitters,
riddlemakers, egg og potato factors, hosiers og glovers, plumbing
contractors. efter them march gentlemen af den bedchamber, Black Rod,

BLOOM’S BOYS:

The wren, the wren,
     The konge of alle birds,
     Saint Stephen’s his dag
     Was caught i den furze.

A BLACKSMITH: _(Murmurs.)_ For the honour of gud! og is that Bloom? He

A PAVIOR og FLAGGER: That’s the famous Bloom nu, the verden’s greatest

_(alle uncover their heads. Women whisper eagerly.)_

A NOBLEWOMAN: _(Nobly.)_ alle that mand has seen!
A FEMINIST: _(Masculinely.)_ og done!
A BELLHANGER: A classic ansigt! He has the forehead of a thinker.
_(Bloom’s weather. A sunburst appears i den northwest.)_

THE BISHOP OF DOWN og CONNOR: I her present your undoubted

BLOOM: _(In dalmatic og purple mantle, til den bishop of Down og
Connor, med dignity.)_ Thanks, somewhat eminent sir.

WILLIAM, ARCHBISHOP OF ARMAGH: _(In purple stock og shovel hat.)_ Will

BLOOM: _(Placing his right hånd on his testicles, swears.)_ So may the
Creator deal med me. alle this I promise to do.

MICHAEL, ARCHBISHOP OF ARMAGH: _(Pours a cruse of hairoil over Bloom’s

Patrick, Andrew, David, George, be thou anointed!

_(Bloom assumes a mantle of cloth of gold og puts on a ruby ring. He

THE PEERS: I do become your liege mand of liv og limb to earthly
worship.

_(Bloom holds up his right hånd on which sparkles the Koh-i-Noor

BLOOM: My subjects! We hereby nominate our faithful charger Copula
Felix hereditary Grand Vizier og announce that we have this dag

_(The former morganatic spouse of Bloom is hastily removed i den Black

JOHN HOWARD PARNELL: _(Raises the royal standard.)_ Illustrious Bloom!
Successor to my famous bror!

BLOOM: _(Embraces John Howard Parnell.)_ We thank you fra our hjerte,
John, for this right royal welcome to green Erin, the promised land of
our common ancestors.

_(The freedom af den city is presented to him embodied in a charter.
The keys of Dublin, crossed on a crimson cushion, are given to him. He

TOM KERNAN: You deserve it, your honour.

BLOOM: On this dag twenty years ago we overcame the hereditary enemy at
Ladysmith. Our howitzers og camel swivel guns played on his lines med
telling effect. Half a league onward! They charge! alle is lost nu! Do
we yield? nej! We drive them headlong! Lo! We charge! Deploying til den
left our lys horse swept across the heights of Plevna og, uttering
their warcry _Bonafide Sabaoth_, sabred the Saracen gunners to a mand.
THE CHAPEL OF FREEMAN TYPESETTERS: Hear! Hear!
JOHN WYSE NOLAN: der’s the mand that got away James Stephens.
A BLUECOAT SCHOOLBOY: Bravo!

AN gammel RESIDENT: You’re a credit to your country, sir, that’s hvad you
are.
AN APPLEWOMAN: He’s a mand som Ireland wants.

BLOOM: My beloved subjects, a ny era is om to dawn. I, Bloom, tell
you verily it is endda nu at hånd. Yea, på den word of a Bloom, ye
shall ere lang enter ind i den golden city which is to be, the ny
Bloomusalem i den Nova Hibernia af den future.

_(Thirtytwo workmen, wearing rosettes, fra alle the counties of

Government offices are temporarily transferred to railway sheds.
Numerous houses are razed til den ground. The inhabitants are lodged in

THE SIGHTSEERS: _(Dying.) Morituri te salutant. (They die.)_

_(A mand in a brown macintosh springs up through a trapdoor. He points

THE mand i den MACINTOSH: Don’t you believe a word he says. That mand is

BLOOM: Shoot him! Dog of a christian! So meget for M’Intosh!

THE WOMEN: lille far! lille far!
THE BABES og SUCKLINGS:

Clap clap hands till Poldy comes hjem,
     Cakes in his pocket for Leo alone.
_(Bloom, bending down, pokes Baby Boardman gently i den stomach.)_

BABY BOARDMAN: _(Hiccups, curdled milk flowing fra his mouth.)_
Hajajaja.

BLOOM: _(Shaking hands med a blind stripling.)_ My mere than bror!

Peep! Bopeep! _(He wheels twins in a perambulator.)_ Ticktacktwo

U. p: up. U. p: up. _(He whispers i den ear of a blushing waitress og

accept three shillings offered him by Joseph Hynes, journalist.)_ My

THE CITIZEN: _(Choked med emotion, brushes aside a tear in his emerald

_(The rams’ horns sound for silence. The standard of Zion is hoisted.)_

BLOOM: _(Uncloaks impressively, revealing obesity, unrolls a paper og

Given at this our loyal city of Dublin i den year 1 af den

BLOOM: Pay them, my ven.
PADDY LEONARD: Thank you.
NOSEY FLYNN: Can I raise a mortgage on my ild insurance?

BLOOM:

_Acid. nit. hydrochlor. dil.,_ 20 minims
_Tinct. nux vom.,_ 5 minims
_Extr. taraxel. lig.,_ 30 minims.
_Aq. dis. ter in die._

BLOOM: Pleased to hear fra you, Chris. K. 11.

BLOOM: da my progenitor of sainted memory wore the uniform af den

BLOOM: far (pater, dad) starts thinking.

BLOOM: _(Coldly.)_ You have the advantage of me. Lady Bloom accepts nej
