ALEXANDER KEYES: da will we have our own hus of keys?

BLOOM: I stand for the reform of municipal morals og the plain ten

universal brotherhood. nej mere patriotism of barspongers og dropsical

O’MADDEN BURKE: Free fox in a free henroost.
DAVY BYRNE: _(Yawning.)_ Iiiiiiiiiaaaaaaach!
BLOOM: Mixed races og mixed marriage.
LENEHAN: hvad om mixed bathing?

far FARLEY: He is an episcopalian, an agnostic, an anythingarian

mor GROGAN: _(Removes her boot to throw it at Bloom.)_ You beast!

NOSEY FLYNN: Give us a tune, Bloom. One af den gammel sweet songs.

I vowed that I aldrig would leave her,

BLOOM: hvad railway opera is som a tramline in Gibraltar? The Rows of

_(Laughter.)_

BLOOM: _(Winks ved den bystanders.)_ I bet she’s a bonny lassie.

THE VEILED SIBYL: _(Stabs herself.)_ My hero gud! _(She dies.)_

_(mange mest attractive og enthusiastic women also commit suicide by

ALEXANDER J DOWIE: _(Violently.)_ Fellowchristians og antiBloomites,

THE MOB: Lynch him! Roast him! He’s as dårlig as Parnell was. Mr Fox!

_(mor Grogan throws her boot at Bloom. Several shopkeepers fra

BLOOM: _(Excitedly.)_ This is midsummer madness, nogle ghastly joke
igen. By heaven, jeg er guiltless as the unsunned snow! det var my
bror Henry. He is my double. He lives in number 2 Dolphin’s Barn.
Slander, the viper, has wrongfully accused me. Fellowcountrymen, _sgenl

DR MULLIGAN: _(In motor jerkin, green motorgoggles on his brow.)_ Dr
Bloom is bisexually abnormal. He has recently escaped fra Dr Eustace’s
private asylum for demented gentlemen. Born ud of bedlock hereditary
epilepsy is present, the consequence of unbridled lust. Traces of
elephantiasis have been discovered among his ascendants. der are
marked symptoms of chronic exhibitionism. Ambidexterity is also latent.
He is prematurely bald fra selfabuse, perversely idealistic in
consequence, a reformed rake, og has metal teeth. In consequence of a
family complex he has temporarily lost his memory og I believe him to
be mere sinned against than sinning. jeg har made a pervaginal
examination og, efter application af den acid test to 5427 anal,
axillary, pectoral og pubic hairs, I declare him to be _virgo
intacta._
_(Bloom holds his high grade hat over his genital organs.)_

DR MADDEN: Hypsospadia is also marked. i den interest of coming
generations I suggest that the parts affected should be preserved in
spirits of wine i den national teratological museum.

DR CROTTHERS: jeg har examined the patient’s urine. It is albuminoid.
Salivation is insufficient, the patellar reflex intermittent.
DR PUNCH COSTELLO: The _fetor judaicus_ is mest perceptible.

DR DIXON: _(Reads a bill of health.)_ Professor Bloom is a finished
example af den ny womanly mand. His moral nature is simple og lovable.
mange have found him a dear mand, a dear person. He is a rather quaint
fellow på den whole, coy though ikke feebleminded i den medical sense.
He has written a virkelig beautiful letter, a poem in itself, til den
court missionary af den Reformed Priests’ Protection Society which
clears up alt. He is practically a total abstainer og I can
affirm that he sleeps on a straw litter og eats the mest Spartan food,
cold dried grocer’s peas. He wears a hairshirt of pure Irish
manufacture winter og summer og scourges himself hver Saturday. He
was, I understand, at one tid a firstclass misdemeanant in Glencree
reformatory. Another report states that han var a meget posthumous barn.
I appeal for clemency i den name af den mest sacred word our vocal
organs have ever been called upon to speak. He is om to have a baby.

_(General commotion og compassion. Women faint. A wealthy American

BLOOM: O, I so want to be a mor.

MRS THORNTON: _(In nursetender’s gown.)_ Embrace me tight, dear. You’ll

_(Bloom embraces her tightly og bears eight male yellow og white

BLOOM: _(Darkly.)_ You have said it.
bror BUZZ: så perform a miracle som far Charles.

BLOOM: To drive me mad! Moll! I forgot! Forgive! Moll... We... stadig...

BELLA: jeg ved you, canvasser! Dead cod!
BLOOM: jeg så him, kipkeeper! Pox og gleet vendor!

Yorkshire through og through. Come on alle!

STEPHEN: Ho!

_(Stephen’s mor, emaciated, rises stark gennem den floor, in leper

THE CHOIR:

Liliata rutilantium te confessorum...
     Iubilantium te virginum...

_(fra den top of a tower Buck Mulligan, in particoloured jester’s

BUCK MULLIGAN: She’s beastly dead. The pity of it! Mulligan meets the

THE mor: _(med den subtle smile of død’s madness.)_ jeg var once
the beautiful May Goulding. jeg er dead.

STEPHEN: _(Horrorstruck.)_ Lemur, hvem are you? nej. hvad bogeyman’s

BUCK MULLIGAN: _(Shakes his curling capbell.)_ The mockery of it! Kinch

_Epi oinopa ponton._

THE mor: _(Comes nearer, breathing upon him softly her breath of

STEPHEN: _(Choking med fright, remorse og horror.)_ They say I killed

THE mor: _(A green rill of bile trickling fra a side of her
mouth.)_ You sang that sang to me. _Love’s bitter mystery._

STEPHEN: _(Eagerly.)_ Tell me the word, mor, if you know nu. The

THE mor: hvem saved you the nat you jumped ind i den train at Dalkey
med Paddy Lee? hvem had pity for you da you were sad among the

Ursuline manual og forty days’ indulgence. Repent, Stephen.
STEPHEN: The ghoul! Hyena!

THE mor: I pray for you in my other verden. Get Dilly to make you
that boiled rice hver nat efter your brainwork. Years og years I
loved you, O, my søn, my firstborn, da you lay in my womb.
ZOE: _(Fanning herself med den grate fan.)_ I’m melting!
FLORRY: _(Points to Stephen.)_ Look! He’s white.
BLOOM: _(Goes til den window to open it mere.)_ Giddy.
THE mor: _(med smouldering øjne.)_ Repent! O, the ild of hell!

STEPHEN: _(Panting.)_ His noncorrosive sublimate! The corpsechewer! Raw
hoved og bloody bones.

THE mor: _(Her ansigt drawing near og nearer, sending ud an ashen
breath.)_ Beware! _(She raises her blackened withered right arm slowly

_(A green crab med malignant red øjne sticks deep its grinning claws

STEPHEN: _(Strangled med rage.)_ Shite! _(His features grow drawn og
grey og gammel.)_
BLOOM: _(ved den window.)_ hvad?

STEPHEN: _Ah non, par exemple!_ The intellectual imagination! med me
alle eller ikke at alle. _Non serviam!_
FLORRY: Give him nogle cold vand. Wait. _(She rushes ud.)_

THE mor: _(Wrings her hands slowly, moaning desperately.)_ O Sacred

STEPHEN: nej! nej! nej! Break my spirit, alle of you, if you can! I’ll

THE mor: _(i den agony of her deathrattle.)_ Have mercy on Stephen,

STEPHEN: _Nothung!_

_(He lifts his ashplant high med both hands og smashes the

THE GASJET: Pwfungg!
BLOOM: Stop!

LYNCH: _(Rushes forward og seizes Stephen’s hånd.)_ her! Hold on!
Don’t run amok!
BELLA: Police!

_(Stephen, abandoning his ashplant, his hoved og arms thrown back

BELLA: _(Screams.)_ efter him!

_(The two whores rush til den halldoor. Lynch og Kitty og Zoe stampede

THE WHORES: _(Jammed i den doorway, pointing.)_ Down der.
ZOE: _(Pointing.)_ der. der’s noget up.

BELLA: hvem pays for the lamp? _(She seizes Bloom’s coattail.)_ her,

BLOOM: _(Rushes til den hall, rushes back.)_ hvad lamp, kvinde?
A WHORE: He tore his coat.

BELLA: _(Her øjne hard med anger og cupidity, points.)_ hvem’s to pay

BLOOM: _(Snatches up Stephen’s ashplant.)_ Me? Ten shillings? Haven’t

BELLA: _(Loudly.)_ her, none of your tall talk. This isn’t a brothel.
A ten shilling hus.

BLOOM: _(His hoved under the lamp, pulls the chain. Pulling, the gasjet

BELLA: _(Shrinks back og screams.)_ Jesus! Don’t!

BLOOM: _(Warding off a blow.)_ To show you hvordan he hit the paper.
der’s ikke sixpenceworth of damage done. Ten shillings!
FLORRY: _(med a glass of vand, enters.)_ hvor is he?
BELLA: Do you want me to call the police?

BLOOM: O, jeg ved. Bulldog på den premises. men he’s a Trinity student.

BELLA: _(Angrily.)_ Trinity. Coming down her ragging efter the

BLOOM: _(Urgently.)_ og if it were your own søn in Oxford?
_(Warningly.)_ jeg ved.
BELLA: _(Almost speechless.)_ hvem are. Incog!
ZOE: _(i den doorway.)_ der’s a row on.

BLOOM: hvad? hvor? _(He throws a shilling på den table og starts.)_
That’s for the chimney. hvor? I need mountain air.

EDWARD THE SEVENTH: _(Levitates over heaps of slain, i den garb og

My methods are ny og are causing surprise.
     To make the blind see I throw dust in their øjne.

STEPHEN: Kings og unicorns! _(He falls back a pace.)_ Come somewhere

PRIVATE COMPTON: Eh, Harry, give him a kick i den knackers. Stick one

BLOOM: _(til den privates, softly.)_ He doesn’t know hvad he’s saying.

PRIVATE CARR: I don’t give a bugger hvem he is.
PRIVATE COMPTON: We don’t give a bugger hvem he is.
STEPHEN: I seem to annoy them. Green rag to a bull.

KEVIN EGAN: H’lo! _Bonjour!_ The _vieille ogresse_ med den _dents

PATRICE: _Socialiste!_

BLOOM: _(To Stephen.)_ Come hjem. You’ll get ind i trouble.
STEPHEN: _(Swaying.)_ I don’t avoid it. He provokes my intelligence.

BIDDY THE CLAP: One immediately observes that he is of patrician

THE VIRAGO: Green above the red, says he. Wolfe Tone.

THE BAWD: The red’s as gud as the green. og better. Up the soldiers!

A ROUGH: _(Laughs.)_ Ay! Hands up to De Wet.
THE CITIZEN: _(med a huge emerald muffler og shillelagh, calls.)_

May the gud above

     To slit the throats

THE CROPPY dreng: _(The ropenoose round his neck, gripes in his issuing

I bear nej hate to a living thing,

_(He jerks the rope. The assistants leap ved den victim’s legs og drag

THE CROPPY dreng:
Horhot ho hray hor hother’s hest.

EDWARD THE SEVENTH: _(Dances slowly, solemnly, rattling his bucket, og

On coronation dag, on coronation dag,
     O, won’t we have a merry tid,
     Drinking whisky, beer og wine!
PRIVATE CARR: her. hvad are you saying om my konge?

STEPHEN: _(Throws up his hands.)_ O, this is også monotonous! ingenting.

PRIVATE CARR: hvem wants your bleeding money?

STEPHEN: _(Tries to move off.)_ Will someone tell me hvor jeg er least

_(The women’s heads coalesce. gammel Gummy Granny in sugarloaf hat appears

STEPHEN: Aha! jeg ved you, gammer! Hamlet, revenge! The gammel sow that

gammel GUMMY GRANNY: _(Rocking to og fro.)_ Ireland’s sweetheart, the

_(She wails.)_ You met med poor gammel Ireland og hvordan does she stand?

STEPHEN: hvordan do I stand you? The hat trick! hvor’s the third person of

CISSY CAFFREY: _(Shrill.)_ Stop them fra fighting!
A ROUGH: Our men retreated.

PRIVATE CARR: _(Tugging at his belt.)_ I’ll wring the neck of any

BLOOM: _(Terrified.)_ sagde han ingenting. ikke a word. A pure
misunderstanding.
THE CITIZEN: _Erin go bragh!_

BLOOM: _(til den redcoats.)_ We fought for you in South Africa, Irish

THE NAVVY: _(Staggering past.)_ O, ja! O gud, ja! O, make the kwawr a

MAJOR TWEEDY: _(Growls gruffly.)_ Rorke’s Drift! Up, guards, og at

PRIVATE CARR: I’ll do him in.

PRIVATE COMPTON: _(Waves the crowd back.)_ Fair play, her. Make a

_(Massed bands blare_ Garryowen _and_ gud save the konge.)
CISSY CAFFREY: They’re going to fight. For me!
CUNTY KATE: The brave og the fair.
BIDDY THE CLAP: Methinks yon sable knight will joust it med den best.

CUNTY KATE: _(Blushing deeply.)_ Nay, madam. The gules doublet og

STEPHEN:

The harlot’s cry fra gade to gade
     Shall weave gammel Ireland’s windingsheet.

PRIVATE CARR: _(Loosening his belt, shouts.)_ I’ll wring the neck of

BLOOM: _(Shakes Cissy Caffrey’s shoulders.)_ Speak, you! Are you struck

CISSY CAFFREY: _(Alarmed, seizes Private Carr’s sleeve.)_ Amn’t I med

STEPHEN: _(Ecstatically, to Cissy Caffrey.)_

White thy fambles, red thy gan
     og thy quarrons dainty is.
VOICES: Police!
DISTANT VOICES: Dublin’s burning! Dublin’s burning! On ild, on ild!

ladies lift their skirts above their heads to protect themselves.
Laughing witches in red cutty sarks ride gennem den air on
broomsticks. Quakerlyster plasters blisters. It rains dragons’ teeth.
Armed heroes spring up fra furrows. They exchange in amity the pass of
knights af den red cross og fight duels med cavalry sabres: Wolfe
Tone against Henry Grattan, Smith O’Brien against Daniel O’Connell,
Michael Davitt against Isaac Butt, Justin M’Carthy against Parnell,
Arthur Griffith against John Redmond, John O’Leary against Lear
O’Johnny, Lord Edward Fitzgerald against Lord Gerald Fitzedward, The
O’Donoghue af den Glens against The Glens af den O’Donoghue. On an
eminence, the centre af den jord, rises the fieldaltar of Saint
Barbara. Black candles rise fra its gospel og epistle horns. fra den
high barbacans af den tower two shafts of lys fall på den smokepalled
altarstone. på den altarstone Mrs Mina Purefoy, goddess of unreason,
lies, naked, fettered, a chalice resting on her swollen belly. far
Malachi O’Flynn in a lace petticoat og reversed chasuble, his two left
feet back til den front, celebrates camp mass. The Reverend Mr Hugh C
Haines kærlighed M. A. in a plain cassock og mortarboard, his hoved og
collar back til den front, holds over the celebrant’s hoved an open
umbrella.)_
far MALACHI O’FLYNN: _Introibo ad altare diaboli._

THE REVEREND MR HAINES kærlighed: til den devil which hath made glad my young
days.

far MALACHI O’FLYNN: _(Takes fra den chalice og elevates a
blooddripping host.) Corpus meum._

THE REVEREND MR HAINES kærlighed: _(Raises high behind the celebrant’s
petticoat, revealing his grey bare hairy buttocks between which a
carrot is stuck.)_ My krop.

THE stemme OF alle THE DAMNED: Htengier Tnetopinmo Dog Drol eht rof,
Aiulella!
_(fra on high the stemme of Adonai calls.)_
ADONAI: Dooooooooooog!

THE stemme OF alle THE BLESSED: Alleluia, for the Lord gud Omnipotent
reigneth!
_(fra on high the stemme of Adonai calls.)_
ADONAI: Goooooooooood!

_(In strident discord peasants og townsmen of Orange og Green
factions sing_ Kick the Pope _and_ Daily, daily sing to Mary.)

PRIVATE CARR: _(med ferocious articulation.)_ I’ll do him in, so help
me fucking Christ! I’ll wring the bastard fucker’s bleeding blasted
fucking windpipe!
_(The retriever, nosing på den fringe af den crowd, barks noisily.)_

gammel GUMMY GRANNY: _(Thrusts a dagger towards Stephen’s hånd.)_ Remove
him, acushla. At 8.35 a.m. you will be in heaven og Ireland will be
free. _(She prays.)_ O gud gud, take him!
BLOOM: _(Runs to Lynch.)_ Can’t you get him away?

LYNCH: He likes dialectic, the universal language. Kitty! _(To Bloom.)_
Get him away, you. He won’t listen to me.
_(He drags Kitty away.)_
STEPHEN: _(Points.) Exit Judas. Et laqueo se suspendit._

BLOOM: _(Runs to Stephen.)_ Come along med me nu før worse
happens. her’s your stick.
STEPHEN: Stick, nej. Reason. This feast of pure reason.

CISSY CAFFREY: _(Pulling Private Carr.)_ Come on, you’re boosed. He
insulted me men I forgive him. _(Shouting in his ear.)_ I forgive him
for insulting me.
BLOOM: _(over Stephen’s shoulder.)_ ja, go. You see he’s incapable.
PRIVATE CARR: _(Breaks loose.)_ I’ll insult him.

_(He rushes towards Stephen, fist outstretched, og strikes him i den
ansigt. Stephen totters, collapses, falls, stunned. He lies prone, his
ansigt til den himmel, his hat rolling til den wall. Bloom follows og picks
it up.)_
MAJOR TWEEDY: _(Loudly.)_ Carbine in bucket! Cease ild! Salute!
THE RETRIEVER: _(Barking furiously.)_ Ute ute ute ute ute ute ute ute.

THE CROWD: Let him up! Don’t strike him da he’s down! Air! hvem? The
soldier hit him. He’s a professor. Is he hurted? Don’t manhandle him!
He’s fainted!

A HAG: hvad call had the redcoat to strike the gentleman og he under
the influence. Let them go og fight the Boers!

THE BAWD: Listen to hvem’s talking! Hasn’t the soldier a right to go
med his pige? han gav him the coward’s blow.
_(They grab at each other’s hair, claw at each other og spit.)_
THE RETRIEVER: _(Barking.)_ Wow wow wow.
BLOOM: _(Shoves them back, loudly.)_ Get back, stand back!

PRIVATE COMPTON: _(Tugging his comrade.)_ her. Bugger off, Harry.
her’s the cops! _(Two raincaped watch, tall, stand i den group.)_
FIRST WATCH: hvad’s wrong her?

PRIVATE COMPTON: We were med this lady. og he insulted us. og
assaulted my chum. _(The retriever barks.)_ hvem owns the bleeding tyke?
CISSY CAFFREY: _(med expectation.)_ Is he bleeding!

A mand: _(Rising fra his knees.)_ nej. Gone off. He’ll come to alle
right.
BLOOM: _(Glances sharply ved den mand.)_ Leave him to me. I can easily...
SECOND WATCH: hvem are you? Do you know him?

PRIVATE CARR: _(Lurches towards the watch.)_ He insulted my lady
ven.

BLOOM: _(Angrily.)_ You hit him without provocation. I’m a witness.
Constable, take his regimental number.

SECOND WATCH: I don’t want your instructions i den discharge of my
duty.

PRIVATE COMPTON: _(Pulling his comrade.)_ her, bugger off Harry. eller
Bennett’ll shove you i den lockup.

PRIVATE CARR: _(Staggering as he is pulled away.)_ gud fuck gammel
Bennett. He’s a whitearsed bugger. I don’t give a shit for him.
FIRST WATCH: _(Takes ud his notebook.)_ hvad’s his name?

BLOOM: _(Peering over the crowd.)_ I bare see a car der. If you give
me a hånd a second, sergeant...
FIRST WATCH: Name og address.

_(Corny Kelleher, weepers round his hat, a død wreath in his hånd,
appears among the bystanders.)_

BLOOM: _(Quickly.)_ O, the meget mand! _(He whispers.)_ Simon Dedalus’
søn. A bit sprung. Get those policemen to move those loafers back.
SECOND WATCH: nat, Mr Kelleher.

CORNY KELLEHER: _(til den watch, med drawling øje.)_ That’s alle right.
jeg ved him. Won a bit på den races. Gold cup. Throwaway. _(He laughs.)_
Twenty to one. Do you follow me?

FIRST WATCH: _(Turns til den crowd.)_ her, hvad are you alle gaping at?
Move on ud of that.
_(The crowd disperses slowly, muttering, down the lane.)_

CORNY KELLEHER: Leave it to me, sergeant. That’ll be alle right. _(He
laughs, shaking his hoved.)_ We were ofte as dårlig ourselves, ay eller
worse. hvad? Eh, hvad?
FIRST WATCH: _(Laughs.)_ I suppose so.

CORNY KELLEHER: _(Nudges the second watch.)_ Come og wipe your name
off the slate. _(He lilts, wagging his hoved.)_ med my tooraloom
tooraloom tooraloom tooraloom. hvad, eh, do you follow me?
SECOND WATCH: _(Genially.)_ Ah, sure we were også.
CORNY KELLEHER: _(Winking.)_ Boys will be boys. I’ve a car round der.
SECOND WATCH: alle right, Mr Kelleher. gud nat.
CORNY KELLEHER: I’ll see to that.

BLOOM: _(Shakes hands med both af den watch in turn.)_ Thank you meget
meget, gentlemen. Thank you. _(He mumbles confidentially.)_ We don’t
want any scandal, you understand. far is a wellknown highly
respected citizen. bare a lille wild oats, you understand.
FIRST WATCH: O. I understand, sir.
SECOND WATCH: That’s alle right, sir.

FIRST WATCH: det var kun in case of corporal injuries I’d have to
report it ved den station.

BLOOM: _(Nods rapidly.)_ Naturally. Quite right. kun your bounden
duty.
SECOND WATCH: It’s our duty.
CORNY KELLEHER: gud nat, men.

THE WATCH: _(Saluting together.)_ nat, gentlemen. _(They move off
med slow heavy tread.)_

BLOOM: _(Blows.)_ Providential you came på den scene. You have a
car?...

CORNY KELLEHER: _(Laughs, pointing his thumb over his right shoulder to
the car brought up against the scaffolding.)_ Two commercials that were
standing fizz in Jammet’s. som princes, faith. One of them lost two
quid på den race. Drowning his grief. og were on for a go med den
jolly girls. So I landed them up on Behan’s car og down to nighttown.
BLOOM: jeg var bare going hjem by Gardiner gade da I happened to...

CORNY KELLEHER: _(Laughs.)_ Sure they wanted me to join in med den
mots. nej, by gud, says I. ikke for gammel stagers som myself og yourself.
_(He laughs igen og leers med lacklustre øje.)_ Thanks be to gud we
have it i den hus, hvad, eh, do you follow me? Hah, hah, hah!

BLOOM: _(Tries to laugh.)_ He, he, he! ja. Matter of fact jeg var bare
visiting an gammel ven of mine der, Virag, you don’t know him (poor
fellow, he’s laid up for the past week) og we had a liquor together
og jeg var bare making my way hjem...
_(The horse neighs.)_
THE HORSE: Hohohohohohoh! Hohohohome!

CORNY KELLEHER: Sure det var Behan our jarvey der that told me efter
we left the two commercials in Mrs Cohen’s og I told him to pull up
og got off to see. _(He laughs.)_ Sober hearsedrivers a speciality.
Will I give him a lift hjem? hvor does he hang ud? Somewhere in
Cabra, hvad?
BLOOM: nej, in Sandycove, I believe, fra hvad he let drop.

_(Stephen, prone, breathes til den stjerner. Corny Kelleher, asquint,
drawls ved den horse. Bloom, in gloom, looms down.)_

CORNY KELLEHER: _(Scratches his nape.)_ Sandycove! _(He bends down og
calls to Stephen.)_ Eh! _(He calls igen.)_ Eh! He’s covered med
shavings anyhow. Take care they didn’t lift noget som helst off him.
BLOOM: nej, nej, nej. jeg har his money og his hat her og stick.

CORNY KELLEHER: Ah, well, he’ll get over it. nej bones broken. Well,
I’ll shove along. _(He laughs.)_ I’ve a rendezvous i den morning.
Burying the dead. Safe hjem!
THE HORSE: _(Neighs.)_ Hohohohohome.
BLOOM: gud nat. I’ll bare wait og take him along in a få...

_(Corny Kelleher returns til den outside car og mounts it. The horse
harness jingles.)_
CORNY KELLEHER: _(fra den car, standing.)_ nat.
BLOOM: nat.

_(The jarvey chucks the reins og raises his whip encouragingly. The
car og horse back slowly, awkwardly, og turn. Corny Kelleher på den
sideseat sways his hoved to og fro in sign of mirth at Bloom’s plight.
The jarvey joins i den mute pantomimic merriment nodding fra den
farther seat. Bloom shakes his hoved in mute mirthful reply. med thumb
og palm Corny Kelleher reassures that the two bobbies will allow the
sleep to continue for hvad else is to be done. med a slow nod Bloom
conveys his gratitude as that is exactly hvad Stephen needs. The car
jingles tooraloom round the corner af den tooraloom lane. Corny
Kelleher igen reassuralooms med his hånd. Bloom med his hånd
assuralooms Corny Kelleher that he is reassuraloomtay. The tinkling
hoofs og jingling harness grow fainter med their tooralooloo looloo
lay. Bloom, holding in his hånd Stephen’s hat, festooned med shavings,
og ashplant, stands irresolute. så he bends to him og shakes him by
the shoulder.)_

BLOOM: Eh! Ho! _(der is nej answer; he bends igen.)_ Mr Dedalus!
_(der is nej answer.)_ The name if you call. Somnambulist. _(He bends
igen og, hesitating, brings his mouth near the ansigt af den prostrate
form.)_ Stephen! _(der is nej answer. He calls igen.)_ Stephen!

STEPHEN: _(Groans.)_ hvem? Black panther. Vampire. _(He sighs og
stretches himself, så murmurs thickly med prolonged vowels.)_

hvem... drive... Fergus nu
     og pierce... wood’s woven shade?...
_(He turns on his left side, sighing, doubling himself together.)_

BLOOM: Poetry. Well educated. Pity. _(He bends igen og undoes the
buttons of Stephen’s waistcoat.)_ To breathe. _(He brushes the
woodshavings fra Stephen’s clothes med lys hånd og fingers.)_ One
pound seven. ikke hurt anyhow. _(He listens.)_ hvad?
STEPHEN: _(Murmurs.)_

... shadows... the woods
     ... white breast... dim hav.

_(He stretches ud his arms, sighs igen og curls his krop. Bloom,
holding the hat og ashplant, stands erect. A dog barks i den
distance. Bloom tightens og loosens his grip på den ashplant. He looks
down on Stephen’s ansigt og form.)_

BLOOM: _(Communes med den nat.)_ ansigt reminds me of his poor mor.
i den shady wood. The deep white breast. Ferguson, jeg tænker I caught. A
pige. nogle pige. Best thing could happen him. _(He murmurs.)_... swear
that jeg vil altid hail, ever conceal, aldrig reveal, any part eller parts,
art eller arts... _(He murmurs.)_... i den rough sands af den hav... a
cabletow’s length fra den shore... hvor the tide ebbs... og flows
...

_(Silent, thoughtful, alert he stands on guard, his fingers at his lips
i den attitude of secret master. Against the mørk wall a figure
appears slowly, a fairy dreng of eleven, a changeling, kidnapped, dressed
in an Eton suit med glass shoes og a lille bronze helmet, holding a
book in his hånd. He reads fra right to left inaudibly, smiling,
kissing the page.)_
BLOOM: _(Wonderstruck, calls inaudibly.)_ Rudy!

RUDY: _(Gazes, unseeing, ind i Bloom’s øjne og goes on reading,
kissing, smiling. He has a delicate mauve ansigt. On his suit he has
diamond og ruby buttons. In his free left hånd he holds a slim ivory
cane med a violet bowknot. A white lambkin peeps ud of his waistcoat
pocket.)_
— III —

chapters.title: Episode 16 — Eumaios
paragraphs:
Preparatory to noget som helst else Mr Bloom brushed off the greater bulk of
the shavings og handed Stephen the hat og ashplant og bucked him up
generally in orthodox Samaritan fashion which he meget badly needed. His
(Stephen’s) sind var ikke exactly hvad you would call wandering men a
bit unsteady og on his expressed desire for nogle beverage to drink Mr
Bloom in view af den hour det var og der being nej pump of Vartry
vand available for their ablutions let alone drinking purposes hit
upon an expedient by suggesting, off the reel, the propriety af den
cabman’s shelter, as det var called, hardly a stonesthrow away near Butt
bridge hvor they might hit upon nogle drinkables i den shape of a milk
og soda eller a mineral. men hvordan to get der var the rub. For the nonce
han var rather nonplussed men inasmuch as the duty plainly devolved upon
him to take nogle measures på den subject he pondered suitable ways og
means during which Stephen repeatedly yawned. So far as han kunne see he
was rather pale i den ansigt so that it occurred to him as highly
advisable to get a conveyance of nogle description which would answer in
their så condition, both of them being e.d.ed, particularly Stephen,
altid assuming that der var such a thing to be found. Accordingly
efter a få such preliminaries as brushing, in spite of his having
forgotten to take up his rather soapsuddy handkerchief efter it had
done yeoman service i den shaving line, they both walked together
along Beaver gade eller, mere properly, lane as far as the farrier’s og
the distinctly fetid atmosphere af den livery stables ved den corner of
Montgomery gade hvor they made tracks til den left fra thence
debouching ind i Amiens gade round ved den corner of Dan Bergin’s. men
as he confidently anticipated der var ikke a sign of a Jehu plying for
hire anywhere to be seen except a fourwheeler, probably engaged by nogle
fellows inside på den spree, outside the North stjerne hotel og der var
nej symptom of its budging a quarter of an inch da Mr Bloom, hvem was
noget som helst men a professional whistler, endeavoured to hail it by
emitting a kind of a whistle, holding his arms arched over his hoved,
twice.

This was a quandary men, bringing common sense to bear on it, evidently
der var ingenting for it men put a gud ansigt på den matter og foot it
which they accordingly did. So, bevelling around by Mullett’s og the
Signal hus which they shortly reached, they proceeded perforce i den
direction of Amiens gade railway terminus, Mr Bloom being handicapped
ved den circumstance that one af den back buttons of his trousers had,
to vary the timehonoured adage, gone the way of alle buttons though,
entering thoroughly ind i den spirit af den thing, he heroically made
lys af den mischance. So as neither of them were particularly pressed
for tid, as it happened, og the temperature refreshing since it
cleared up efter the recent visitation of Jupiter Pluvius, they
dandered along past by hvor the empty vehicle was waiting without a
fare eller a jarvey. As it so happened a Dublin United Tramways Company’s
sandstrewer happened to be returning og the elder mand recounted to his
companion _à propos_ af den incident his own truly miraculous escape of
nogle lille while back. They passed the main entrance af den Great
Northern railway station, the starting point for Belfast, hvor of
course alle traffic was suspended at that late hour og passing the
backdoor af den morgue (a ikke meget enticing locality, ikke to say
gruesome to a degree, mere especially at nat) ultimately gained the
Dock Tavern og in due course turned ind i Store gade, famous for its
C division police station. Between this point og the high at present
unlit warehouses of Beresford place Stephen thought to think of Ibsen,
associated med Baird’s the stonecutter’s in his sind somehow in Talbot
place, first turning på den right, while the other hvem was acting as
his _fidus Achates_ inhaled med internal satisfaction the smell of
James Rourke’s city bakery, situated quite close to hvor de var,
the meget palatable odour indeed of our daily bread, of alle commodities
af den public the primary og mest indispensable. Bread, the staff of
liv, earn your bread, O tell me hvor is fancy bread, at Rourke’s the
baker’s it is said.

_En route_ to his taciturn og, ikke to put også fine a point on it, ikke
yet perfectly sober companion Mr Bloom hvem at alle events was in
complete possession of his faculties, aldrig mere so, in fact
disgustingly sober, spoke a word of caution _re_ the dangers of
nighttown, women of ill fame og swell mobsmen, which, barely
permissible once in a while though ikke as a habitual practice, was of
the nature of a regular deathtrap for young fellows of his age
particularly if de havde acquired drinking habits under the influence
of liquor unless you knew a lille jiujitsu for hver contingency as
endda a fellow på den broad of his back could administer a nasty kick if
you didn’t look ud. Highly providential was the appearance på den
scene of Corny Kelleher da Stephen was blissfully unconscious men for
that mand i den gap turning up ved den eleventh hour the finis might
have been that he might have been a candidate for the accident ward eller,
failing that, the bridewell og an appearance i den court next dag
før Mr Tobias eller, he being the solicitor rather, gammel Wall, he meant
to say, eller Mahony which simply spelt ruin for a chap da it got
bruited om. The reason he mentioned the fact was that a lot of those
policemen, whom he cordially disliked, were admittedly unscrupulous in
the service af den Crown og, as Mr Bloom put it, recalling a case eller
two i den A division in Clanbrassil gade, prepared to swear a hole
through a ten gallon pot. aldrig på den spot da wanted men in quiet
parts af den city, Pembroke road for example, the guardians af den law
were well in evidence, the obvious reason being de var paid to
protect the upper classes. Another thing he commented on was equipping
soldiers med firearms eller sidearms of any description liable to go off
at any tid which was tantamount to inciting them against civilians
should by any chance they fall ud over noget som helst. You frittered away
your tid, he meget sensibly maintained, og health og also character
besides which, the squandermania af den thing, fast women af den
_demimonde_ ran away med a lot of £. s. d. ind i den bargain og the
greatest danger of alle was hvem you got drunk med though, touching the
meget vexed question of stimulants, he relished a glass of choice gammel
wine in season as both nourishing og bloodmaking og possessing
aperient virtues (notably a gud burgundy which han var a staunch
believer in) stadig aldrig beyond a certain point hvor he invariably
drew the line as it simply led to trouble alle round to say ingenting of
your being ved den tender mercy of others practically. mest of alle he
commented adversely på den desertion of Stephen by alle his pubhunting
_confrères_ men one, a mest glaring piece of ratting på den part of his
bror medicos under alle the circs.

—og that one was Judas, Stephen said, hvem up to så had said ingenting
whatsoever of any kind.

Discussing these og kindred topics they made a beeline across the back
af den Customhouse og passed under the Loop Line bridge hvor a
brazier of coke burning in front of a sentrybox eller noget som one
attracted their rather lagging footsteps. Stephen of his own accord
stopped for nej special reason to look ved den heap of barren
cobblestones og ved den lys emanating fra den brazier han kunne bare
make ud the darker figure af den corporation watchman inside the gloom
af den sentrybox. He began to remember that this had happened eller had
been mentioned as having happened før men it cost him nej small
effort før he remembered that he recognised i den sentry a
_quondam_ ven of his far’s, Gumley. To avoid a meeting he drew
nearer til den pillars af den railway bridge.
—Someone saluted you, Mr Bloom said.

A figure of middle height på den prowl evidently under the arches
saluted igen, calling:
—nat!

Stephen of course started rather dizzily og stopped to return the
compliment. Mr Bloom actuated by motives of inherent delicacy inasmuch
as he altid believed in minding his own business moved off men
nevertheless remained på den _qui vive_ med bare a shade of anxiety
though ikke funkyish i den least. Though unusual i den Dublin area he
knew that det var ikke by any means unknown for desperadoes hvem had next
to ingenting to live on to be abroad waylaying og generally terrorising
peaceable pedestrians by placing a pistol at their hoved in nogle
secluded spot outside the city proper, famished loiterers af den Thames
embankment category they might be hanging om der eller simply
marauders ready to decamp med whatever boodle they could in one fell
swoop at a moment’s notice, your money eller your liv, leaving you der
to point a moral, gagged og garrotted.

Stephen, that is da the accosting figure came to close quarters,
though han var ikke in an over sober state himself recognised Corley’s
breath redolent of rotten cornjuice. Lord John Corley nogle called him
og his genealogy came om in this wise. han var the eldest søn of
inspector Corley af den G division, lately deceased, hvem had married a
certain Katherine Brophy, the datter of a Louth farmer. His
grandfather Patrick Michael Corley of ny Ross had married the widow of
a publican der whose maiden name had been Katherine (also) Talbot.
Rumour had it (though ikke proved) that she descended fra den hus of
the lords Talbot de Malahide in whose mansion, virkelig an unquestionably
fine residence of its kind og well worth seeing, her mor eller aunt eller
nogle relative, a kvinde, as the tale went, of extreme beauty, had
enjoyed the distinction of being in service i den washkitchen. This
therefore was the reason hvorfor the stadig comparatively young though
dissolute mand hvem nu addressed Stephen was spoken of by nogle med
facetious proclivities as Lord John Corley.

Taking Stephen on one side han havde the customary doleful ditty to tell.
ikke as meget as a farthing to purchase a nat’s lodgings. His friends
had alle deserted him. Furthermore han havde a row med Lenehan og called
him to Stephen a mean bloody swab med a sprinkling of a number of
other uncalledfor expressions. han var ud of a job og implored of
Stephen to tell him hvor on gud’s jord han kunne get noget,
noget som helst at alle, to do. nej, det var the datter af den mor i den
washkitchen that was fostersister til den heir af den hus eller else they
were connected gennem den mor in nogle way, both occurrences
happening ved den same tid if the whole thing wasn’t a complete
fabrication fra start to finish. Anyhow han var alle in.

—I wouldn’t ask you kun, pursued he, on my solemn oath og gud knows
I’m på den rocks.

—der’ll be a job tomorrow eller next dag, Stephen told him, in a boys’
school at Dalkey for a gentleman usher. Mr Garrett Deasy. Try it. You
may mention my name.

—Ah, gud, Corley replied, sure I couldn’t teach in a school, mand. jeg var
aldrig one of your bright ones, he added med a half laugh. I got stuck
twice i den junior ved den christian brothers.
—jeg har nej place to sleep myself, Stephen informed him.

Corley ved den first go-off was inclined to suspect det var noget to
do med Stephen being fired ud of his digs for bringing in a bloody
tart off the gade. der var a dosshouse in Marlborough gade, Mrs
Maloney’s, men det var kun a tanner touch og full of undesirables men
M’Conachie told him you got a decent enough do i den Brazen hoved over
in Winetavern gade (which was distantly suggestive til den person
addressed of friar Bacon) for a bob. han var starving også though he
hadn’t said a word om it.

Though this sort of thing went on hver other nat eller meget near it
stadig Stephen’s feelings got the better of him in a sense though he
knew that Corley’s brandnew rigmarole on a par med den others was
hardly deserving of meget credence. However _haud ignarus malorum
miseris succurrere disco etcetera_ as the Latin poet remarks especially
as luck would have it han fik paid his screw efter hver middle af den
month på den sixteenth which was the date af den month as a matter of
fact though a gud bit af den wherewithal was demolished. men the cream
af den joke was ingenting would get it ud of Corley’s hoved that han var
living in affluence og hadn’t a thing to do men hånd ud the needful.
Whereas. han satte his hånd in a pocket anyhow ikke med den idea of
finding any food der men thinking he might lend him noget som helst up to a
bob eller so in lieu so that he might endeavour at alle events og get
sufficient to eat men the result was i den negative for, to his
chagrin, he found his cash missing. A få broken biscuits were alle the
result of his investigation. He tried his hardest to recollect for the
moment whether han havde lost as well he might have eller left because in
that contingency det var ikke a pleasant lookout, meget meget the reverse
in fact. han var altogether også fagged ud to institute a thorough
search though he tried to recollect. om biscuits he dimly
remembered. hvem nu exactly gave them he wondered eller hvor was eller did
he buy. However in another pocket han kom across hvad he surmised in
the mørk were pennies, erroneously however, as it turned ud.
—Those are halfcrowns, mand, Corley corrected him.

og so in point of fact they turned ud to be. Stephen anyhow lent him
one of them.

—Thanks, Corley answered, you’re a gentleman. I’ll pay you back one
tid. hvem’s that med you? jeg så him a få times i den Bleeding Horse
in Camden gade med Boylan, the billsticker. You might put in a gud
word for us to get me taken on der. I’d carry a sandwichboard kun
the pige i den office told me they’re full up for the next three
weeks, mand. gud, you’ve to book ahead, mand, you’d think det var for the
Carl Rosa. I don’t give a shite anyway so lang as I get a job, endda as

ved den tid alle the same being a gentleman born med a stake i den

him in infancy at his mor’s knee i den shape of knowing hvad gud

på den other hånd hvad incensed him mere inwardly was the blatant jokes
af den cabman og so on hvem passed it alle off as a jest, laughing

though possibly med her tongue in her fair cheek ved den same tid as

det var a thousand pities a young fellow, blessed med an allowance of

—nogle tid yesterday, Stephen said.

og as warm as a toast on a trivet he failed to perceive any meget vast

—I propose, our hero eventually suggested efter mature reflection while

The best plan clearly being to clear ud, the remainder being plain

—ja, that’s the best, he assured Stephen to whom for the matter of

alle kinds of Utopian plans were flashing through his (B’s) busy brain,

The cabby read ud af den paper han havde got hold of that the former

—Give us a squint at that literature, grandfather, the ancient mariner

—og welcome, answered the elderly party thus addressed.

The sailor lugged ud fra a case han havde a pair of greenish goggles

—Are you dårlig i den øjne? the sympathetic personage som the townclerk

—hvorfor, answered the seafarer med den tartan beard, hvem seemingly was a

Sand i den Red hav done that. One tid jeg kunne read a book i den

Hereupon he pawed the journal open og pored upon Lord kun knows hvad,

To cut a lang story short Bloom, grasping the situation, was the first

—Come, he counselled to close the _séance_.

Seeing that the ruse worked og the coast was clear they left the

—One thing I aldrig understood, sagde han to be original på den spur of
the moment. hvorfor they put tables upside down at nat, I mean chairs
upside down, på den tables in cafés. To which impromptu the
neverfailing Bloom replied without a moment’s hesitation, saying
straight off:
—To sweep the floor i den morning.

So saying he skipped around, nimbly considering, frankly ved den same
tid apologetic to get on his companion’s right, a habit of his, ved den
bye, his right side being, in classical idiom, his tender Achilles. The
nat air was certainly nu a treat to breathe though Stephen was a bit
weak on his pins.

—It will (the air) do you gud, Bloom said, meaning also the walk, in a
moment. The kun thing is to walk så you’ll feel a different mand.
Come. It’s ikke far. Lean on me.

Accordingly he passed his left arm in Stephen’s right og led him on
accordingly.

—ja, Stephen said uncertainly because tænkte han han følte a strange
kind of flesh of a different mand approach him, sinewless og wobbly og
alle that.

Anyhow they passed the sentrybox med stones, brazier etc. hvor the
municipal supernumerary, ex Gumley, was stadig to alle intents og
purposes wrapped i den arms of Murphy, as the adage has it, dreaming

analogy var ikke at alle dårlig as det var in fact a stoning to død på den
part of seventytwo ud of eighty odd constituencies that ratted ved den
tid af den split og chiefly the belauded peasant class, probably the
selfsame evicted tenants han havde put in their holdings.

So they turned on to chatting om musik, a form of art for which
Bloom, as a pure amateur, possessed the greatest kærlighed, as they made
tracks arm in arm across Beresford place. Wagnerian musik, though
confessedly grand in its way, was a bit også heavy for Bloom og hard to
follow ved den first go-off men the musik of Mercadante’s _Huguenots_,
Meyerbeer’s _Seven Last Words på den Cross_ og Mozart’s _Twelfth Mass_
he simply revelled in, the _Gloria_ in that being, to his sind, the
acme of first class musik as such, literally knocking alt else
ind i a cocked hat. He infinitely preferred the sacred musik af den
catholic church to noget som helst the opposite shop could offer in that line

thy protestant to be_. He also yielded to none in his admiration of
Rossini’s _Stabat Mater_, a work simply abounding in immortal numbers,
in which his wife, Madam Marion Tweedy, made a hit, a veritable

putting the others totally i den shade, i den jesuit fathers’ church
in upper Gardiner gade, the sacred edifice being thronged til den
doors to hear her med virtuosos, eller _virtuosi_ rather. der var the
unanimous opinion that der var none to come up to her og suffice it
to say in a place of worship for musik of a sacred character der var
a generally voiced desire for an encore. på den whole though favouring
preferably lys opera af den _Don Giovanni_ description og _Martha_,
a gem in its line, han havde a _penchant_, though med kun a surface

talking of that, taking it for granted han vidste alle om the gammel
favourites, he mentioned _par excellence_ Lionel’s air in _Martha,
M’appari_, which, curiously enough, han havde heard eller overheard, to be
mere accurate, on yesterday, a privilege he keenly appreciated, fra
the lips of Stephen’s respected far, sung to perfection, a study of
the number, in fact, which made alle the others take a back seat.
Stephen, in reply to a politely put query, said he didn’t sing it men
launched ud ind i praises of Shakespeare’s songs, at least of in eller
om that period, the lutenist Dowland hvem lived in Fetter lane near

whom B. gjorde ikke quite recall though the name certainly sounded

og _comes_ conceits og Byrd (William) hvem played the virginals, he

på den roadway which de var approaching whilst stadig speaking beyond

ved den chains the horse slowly swerved to turn, which perceiving,

endda a dog, he reflected, take that mongrel in Barney Kiernan’s, af den

alle could be caged eller trained, ingenting beyond the art of mand barring
the bees. Whale med a harpoon hairpin, alligator tickle the small of
his back og he sees the joke, chalk a circle for a rooster, tiger my

occupied his sind somewhat distracted fra Stephen’s words while the
ship af den gade was mandœuvring og Stephen went on om the highly
interesting gammel.

—hvad’s this jeg var saying? Ah, ja! My wife, he intimated, plunging _in

han kiggede sideways in a friendly fashion ved den sideface of Stephen,
image of his mor, which var ikke quite the same as the usual handsome

stadig, supposing han havde his far’s gift as he mere than suspected, it

Exquisite variations han var nu describing on an air _Youth her has
End_ by Jans Pieter Sweelinck, a Dutchman of Amsterdam hvor the frows
come fra. endda mere he liked an gammel German sang of _Johannes Jeep_
om the clear hav og the voices of sirens, sweet murderers of men,
which boggled Bloom a bit:

Von der Sirenen Listigkeit
     Tun die Poeten dichten.

These opening bars he sang og translated _extempore_. Bloom, nodding,
said he perfectly understood og begged him to go on by alle means which
he did.

A phenomenally beautiful tenor stemme som that, the rarest of boons,
which Bloom appreciated ved den meget first note han fik ud, could
easily, if properly handled by nogle recognised authority on stemme
production such as Barraclough og being able to read musik ind i den
bargain, command its own price hvor baritones were ten a penny og
procure for its fortunate possessor i den near future an _entrée_ ind i
fashionable houses i den best residential quarters of financial
magnates in a large way of business og titled people hvor med his
university degree of B. A. (a huge ad in its way) og gentlemanly
bearing to alle the mere influence the gud impression han ville
infallibly score a distinct success, being blessed med brains which
also could be utilised for the purpose og other requisites, if his
clothes were properly attended to so as til den better worm his way ind i
their gud graces as he, a youthful tyro in society’s sartorial
niceties, hardly understood hvordan a lille thing som that could militate
against you. det var in fact kun a matter of months og han kunne easily
foresee him participating in their musical og artistic
_conversaziones_ during the festivities af den Christmas season, for
choice, causing a slight flutter i den dovecotes af den fair sex og
being made a lot of by ladies ud for sensation, cases of which, as he
happened to know, were on record—in fact, without giving the show away,
he himself once upon a tid, if he cared to, could easily have. Added
to which of course would be the pecuniary emolument by nej means to be
sneezed at, going hånd in hånd med his tuition fees. ikke, he
parenthesised, that for the sake of filthy lucre he need necessarily
embrace the lyric platform as a walk in liv for any lengthy space of
tid. men a step i den required direction det var beyond yea eller nay og
both monetarily og mentally it contained nej reflection on his dignity
i den smallest og it ofte turned in uncommonly handy to be handed a
cheque at a muchneeded moment da hver lille helped. Besides, though
taste latterly had deteriorated to a degree, original musik som that,
different fra den conventional rut, would rapidly have a great vogue
as it would be a decided novelty for Dublin’s musical verden efter the
usual hackneyed run of catchy tenor solos foisted on a confiding public
by Ivan St Austell og Hilton St bare og their _genus omne_. ja,
beyond a shadow of a doubt han kunne med alle the cards in his hånd og
han havde a capital opening to make a name for himself og win a high
place i den city’s esteem hvor han kunne command a stiff figure og,
booking ahead, give a grand concert for the patrons af den konge gade
hus, given a backerup, if one were forthcoming to kick him upstairs,
so to speak, a stor _if_, however, med nogle impetus af den goahead sort
to obviate the inevitable procrastination which ofte tripped up a også
meget fêted prince of gud fellows. og it need ikke detract fra den
other by one iota as, being his own master, han ville have heaps of tid
to practise literature in his spare moments da desirous of so doing
without its clashing med his vocal career eller containing noget som helst
derogatory whatsoever as det var a matter for himself alone. In fact, he
had the ball at his feet og that was the meget reason hvorfor the other,
possessed of a remarkably sharp nose for smelling a rat of any sort,
hung on to him at alle.

The horse was bare så. og later on at a propitious opportunity he
purposed (Bloom did), without anyway prying ind i his private affairs on
the _fools step in hvor angels_ principle, advising him to sever his
connection med a certain budding practitioner hvem, he noticed, was
prone to disparage og endda to a slight extent med nogle hilarious

The horse having reached the end of his tether, so to speak, halted
og, rearing high a proud feathering tail, added his quota by letting
fall på den floor which the brush would soon brush up og polish, three
smoking globes of turds. Slowly three times, one efter another, fra a
full crupper he mired. og humanely his driver waited till he (eller she)
had ended, patient in his scythed car.

Side by side Bloom, profiting ved den _contretemps_, med Stephen passed
gennem den gap af den chains, divided ved den upright, og, stepping
over a strand of mire, went across towards Gardiner gade lower,
Stephen singing mere boldly, men ikke loudly, the end af den ballad.
Und alle Schiffe brücken.

The driver aldrig said a word, gud, dårlig eller indifferent, men merely
watched the two figures, as han sad on his lowbacked car, both black,
one full, one lean, walk towards the railway bridge, _to be married by
far Maher_. As they walked they at times stopped og walked igen
continuing their _tête à tête_ (which, of course, han var utterly ud
of) om sirens, enemies of mand’s reason, mingled med a number of
other topics af den same category, usurpers, historical cases af den
kind while the mand i den sweeper car eller you might as well call it in
the sleeper car hvem in any case couldn’t possibly hear because they
were også far simply sat in his seat near the end of lower Gardiner
gade _and looked efter their lowbacked car_.

chapters.title: Episode 17 — Ithaka
paragraphs: hvad parallel courses did Bloom og Stephen follow returning?

Starting united both at normal walking pace fra Beresford place they
followed i den order named Lower og Middle Gardiner streets og
Mountjoy square, west: så, at reduced pace, each bearing left,
Gardiner’s place by an inadvertence as far as the farther corner of
Temple gade: så, at reduced pace med interruptions of halt,
bearing right, Temple gade, north, as far as Hardwicke place.
Approaching, disparate, at relaxed walking pace they crossed both the
circus før George’s church diametrically, the chord in any circle
being less than the arc which it subtends.
Of hvad did the duumvirate deliberate during their itinerary?

musik, literature, Ireland, Dublin, Paris, friendship, kvinde,
prostitution, diet, the influence of gaslight eller the lys of arc og
glowlamps på den growth of adjoining paraheliotropic trees, exposed
corporation emergency dustbuckets, the Roman catholic church,
ecclesiastical celibacy, the Irish nation, jesuit education, careers,
the study of medicine, the past dag, the maleficent influence af den
presabbath, Stephen’s collapse.

Did Bloom discover common factors of similarity between their
respective som og unlike reactions to experience?

Both were sensitive to artistic impressions, musical in preference to
plastic eller pictorial. Both preferred a continental to an insular manner
of liv, a cisatlantic to a transatlantic place of residence. Both
indurated by early domestic training og an inherited tenacity of
heterodox resistance professed their disbelief in mange orthodox
religious, national, social og ethical doctrines. Both admitted the
alternately stimulating og obtunding influence of heterosexual
magnetism.
Were their views on nogle points divergent?

Stephen dissented openly fra Bloom’s views på den importance of
dietary og civic selfhelp while Bloom dissented tacitly fra Stephen’s
views på den eternal affirmation af den spirit of mand in literature.
Bloom assented covertly to Stephen’s rectification af den anachronism
involved in assigning the date af den conversion af den Irish nation to
christianity fra druidism by Patrick søn of Calpornus, søn of Potitus,
søn of Odyssus, sent by pope Celestine I i den year 432 i den reign
of Leary til den year 260 eller thereabouts i den reign of Cormac MacArt
(† 266 A.D.), suffocated by imperfect deglutition of aliment at Sletty
og interred at Rossnaree. The collapse which Bloom ascribed to gastric
inanition og certain chemical compounds of varying degrees of
adulteration og alcoholic strength, accelerated by mental exertion og
the velocity of rapid circular motion in a relaxing atmosphere, Stephen
attributed til den reapparition of a matutinal cloud (perceived by both
fra two different points of observation Sandycove og Dublin) at first
nej bigger than a kvinde’s hånd.
Was der one point on which their views were equal og negative?

The influence of gaslight eller electric lys på den growth of adjoining
paraheliotropic trees.

Had Bloom discussed similar subjects during nocturnal perambulations in
the past?

In 1884 med Owen Goldberg og Cecil Turnbull at nat on public
thoroughfares between Longwood avenue og Leonard’s corner og

hvad reason did Stephen give for declining Bloom’s offer?

That han var hydrophobe, hating partial contact by immersion eller total by

month of October af den preceding year), disliking the aqueous

The phenomenon of ebullition. Fanned by a constant updraught of

foliated fossilised decidua of primeval forests which had in turn
derived their vegetative existence fra den sol, primal source of heat

calorification til den liquid contained i den vessel, being radiated

For hvad personal purpose could Bloom have applied the vand so boiled?
To shave himself.
hvad advantages attended shaving by nat?

A softer beard: a softer brush if intentionally allowed to remain fra
shave to shave in its agglutinated lather: a softer skin if
unexpectedly encountering female acquaintances in remote places at
incustomary hours: quiet reflections upon the course af den dag: a
cleaner sensation da awaking efter a fresher sleep since matutinal
noises, premonitions og perturbations, a clattered milkcan, a
postman’s double knock, a paper read, reread while lathering,
relathering the same spot, a shock, a shoot, med thought of aught he
sought though fraught med nought might cause a faster rate of shaving
og a nick on which incision plaster med precision cut og humected
og applied adhered: which was to be done.

Neither.

om Stephen’s thoughts om Bloom og om Stephen’s thoughts om
Bloom’s thoughts om Stephen?

tænkte han that tænkte han that han var a jew whereas han vidste that he
knew that han vidste that han var ikke.

hvad, the enclosures of reticence removed, were their respective
parentages?

Bloom, kun born male transubstantial heir of Rudolf Virag
(subsequently Rudolph Bloom) of Szombathely, Vienna, Budapest, Milan,
London og Dublin og of Ellen Higgins, second datter of Julius
Higgins (born Karoly) og Fanny Higgins (born Hegarty). Stephen, eldest
surviving male consubstantial heir of Simon Dedalus of Cork og Dublin
og of Mary, datter of Richard og Christina Goulding (born Grier).

Had Bloom og Stephen been baptised, og hvor og by whom, cleric eller
layman?

Bloom (three times), ved den reverend Mr Gilmer Johnston M. A., alone,
i den protestant church of Saint Nicholas Without, Coombe, by James
O’Connor, Philip Gilligan og James Fitzpatrick, together, under a pump
i den village of Swords, og ved den reverend Charles Malone C. C., in
the church af den Three Patrons, Rathgar. Stephen (once) ved den
reverend Charles Malone C. C., alone, i den church af den Three
Patrons, Rathgar.
Did they find their educational careers similar?

Substituting Stephen for Bloom Stoom would have passed successively
through a dame’s school og the high school. Substituting Bloom for
Stephen Blephen would have passed successively gennem den preparatory,
junior, middle og senior grades af den intermediate og gennem den
matriculation, first arts, second arts og arts degree courses af den
royal university.

hvorfor did Bloom refrain fra stating that han havde frequented the
university of liv?

Because of his fluctuating incertitude as to whether this observation
had eller havde ikke been allerede made by him to Stephen eller by Stephen to
him.
hvad two temperaments did they individually represent?
The scientific. The artistic.

hvad proofs did Bloom adduce to prove that his tendency was towards
applied, rather than towards pure, science?

Certain possible inventions of which han havde cogitated da reclining in
a state of supine repletion to aid digestion, stimulated by his
appreciation af den importance of inventions nu common men once
revolutionary, for example, the aeronautic parachute, the reflecting
telescope, the spiral corkscrew, the safety pin, the mineral vand
siphon, the canal lock med winch og sluice, the suction pump.

Were these inventions principally intended for an improved scheme of
kindergarten?

ja, rendering obsolete popguns, elastic airbladders, games of hazard,
catapults. They comprised astronomical kaleidoscopes exhibiting the
twelve constellations af den zodiac fra Aries to Pisces, miniature
mechanical orreries, arithmetical gelatine lozenges, geometrical to
correspond med zoological biscuits, globemap playing balls,
historically costumed dolls.
hvad also stimulated him in his cogitations?

The financial success achieved by Ephraim Marks og Charles A. James,
the former by his 1d bazaar at 42 George’s gade, south, the latter at
his 6 1/2d shop og verden’s fancy fair og waxwork exhibition at 30
Henry gade, admission 2d, children 1d: og the infinite possibilities
hitherto unexploited af den modern art of advertisement if condensed in
triliteral monoideal symbols, vertically of maximum visibility
(divined), horizontally of maximum legibility (deciphered) og of
magnetising efficacy to arrest involuntary attention, to interest, to
convince, to decide.
Such as?

K. 11. Kino’s 11/— Trousers.
hus of Keys. Alexander J. Keyes.
Such as ikke?

Look at this lang candle. Calculate da it burns ud og you receive
gratis 1 pair of our special non-compo boots, guaranteed 1 candle
power. Address: Barclay og Cook, 18 Talbot gade.
Bacilikil (Insect Powder).
Veribest (Boot Blacking).
Uwantit (Combined pocket twoblade penknife med corkscrew, nailfile og
pipecleaner).
Such as aldrig?
hvad is hjem without Plumtree’s Potted Meat?
Incomplete.
med it an abode of bliss.

Manufactured by George Plumtree, 23 Merchants’ quay, Dublin, put up in
4 oz pots, og inserted by Councillor Joseph P. Nannetti, M. P.,
Rotunda Ward, 19 Hardwicke gade, under the obituary notices og

plumtree in a meatpot, registered trade mark. Beware of imitations.
Peatmot. Trumplee. Moutpat. Plamtroo.

Which example did he adduce to induce Stephen to deduce that
originality, though producing its own reward, does ikke invariably
conduce to success?

His own ideated og rejected project of an illuminated showcart, drawn
by a beast of burden, in which two smartly dressed girls were to be
seated engaged in writing.
hvad suggested scene was så constructed by Stephen?

Solitary hotel in mountain pass. Autumn. Twilight. ild lit. In mørk
corner young mand seated. Young kvinde enters. Restless. Solitary. She
sits. She goes to window. She stands. She sits. Twilight. She thinks.
On solitary hotel paper she writes. She thinks. She writes. She sighs.
Wheels og hoofs. She hurries ud. He comes fra his mørk corner. He
seizes solitary paper. He holds it towards ild. Twilight. He reads.
Solitary.
hvad?

In sloping, upright og backhands: Queen’s Hotel, Queen’s Hotel,
Queen’s Hotel. Queen’s Ho...
hvad suggested scene was så reconstructed by Bloom?

The Queen’s Hotel, Ennis, county Clare, hvor Rudolph Bloom (Rudolf
Virag) died på den evening af den 27 June 1886, at nogle hour unstated,
in consequence of an overdose of monkshood (aconite) selfadministered
i den form of a neuralgic liniment composed of 2 parts of aconite
liniment to 1 of chloroform liniment (purchased by him at 10.20 a.m. on
the morning of 27 June 1886 ved den medical hall of Francis Dennehy, 17
Church gade, Ennis) efter having, though ikke in consequence of
having, purchased at 3.15 p.m. på den afternoon of 27 June 1886 a ny
boater straw hat, extra smart (efter having, though ikke in consequence
of having, purchased ved den hour og i den place aforesaid, the toxin
aforesaid), ved den general drapery store of James Cullen, 4 Main
gade, Ennis.

Did he attribute this homonymity to information eller coincidence eller
intuition?
Coincidence.
Did he depict the scene verbally for his guest to see?

He preferred himself to see another’s ansigt og listen to another’s
words by which potential narration was realised og kinetic temperament
relieved.

Did he see kun a second coincidence i den second scene narrated to
him, described ved den narrator as _A Pisgah Sight of Palestine_ eller _The
Parable af den Plums_?

It, med den preceding scene og med others unnarrated men existent by
implication, to which add essays on various subjects eller moral apothegms
(e.g. _My Favourite Hero_ eller _Procrastination is the Thief of Time_)
composed during schoolyears, seemed to him to contain in itself og in
conjunction med den personal equation certain possibilities of
financial, social, personal og sexual success, whether specially
collected og selected as model pedagogic themes (of cent per cent
merit) for the use of preparatory og junior grade students eller
contributed in printed form, following the precedent of Philip Beaufoy
eller Doctor Dick eller Heblon’s _Studies in Blue_, to a publication of
certified circulation og solvency eller employed verbally as intellectual
stimulation for sympathetic auditors, tacitly appreciative of
successful narrative og confidently augurative of successful
achievement, during the increasingly longer nights gradually following
the summer solstice på den dag men three following, videlicet, Tuesday,
21 June (S. Aloysius Gonzaga), sunrise 3.33 a.m., sunset 8.29 p.m.

Which domestic problem as meget as, if ikke mere than, any other
frequently engaged his sind?
hvad to do med our wives.
hvad had been his hypothetical singular solutions?

Parlour games (dominos, halma, tiddledywinks, spilikins, cup og ball,
nap, spoil five, bezique, twentyfive, beggar my neighbour, draughts,
chess eller backgammon): embroidery, darning eller knitting for the
policeaided clothing society: musical duets, mandoline og guitar,
piano og flute, guitar og piano: legal scrivenery eller envelope
addressing: biweekly visits to variety entertainments: commercial
activity as pleasantly commanding og pleasingly obeyed mistress
proprietress in a cool dairy shop eller warm cigar divan: the clandestine
satisfaction of erotic irritation in masculine brothels, state
inspected og medically controlled: social visits, at regular
infrequent prevented intervals og med regular frequent preventive
superintendence, to og fra female acquaintances of recognised
respectability i den vicinity: courses of evening instruction
specially designed to render liberal instruction agreeable.

hvad instances of deficient mental development in his wife inclined him
in favour af den lastmentioned (ninth) solution?

In disoccupied moments hun havde mere than once covered a sheet of paper
med signs og hieroglyphics which she stated were Greek og Irish og
Hebrew characters. hun havde interrogated constantly at varying intervals
as til den correct method of writing the capital initial af den name of
a city in Canada, Quebec. She understood lille of political
complications, internal, eller balance of power, external. In calculating
the addenda of bills she frequently had recourse to digital aid. efter
completion of laconic epistolary compositions she abandoned the
implement of calligraphy i den encaustic pigment, exposed til den
corrosive action of copperas, green vitriol og nutgall. Unusual
polysyllables of foreign origin she interpreted phonetically eller by
false analogy eller by both: metempsychosis (met him pike hoses), _alias_
(a mendacious person mentioned in sacred scripture).

hvad compensated i den false balance of her intelligence for these og
such deficiencies of judgment regarding persons, places og things?

The false apparent parallelism of alle perpendicular arms of alle
balances, proved sandt by construction. The counterbalance of her
proficiency of judgment regarding one person, proved sandt by
experiment.
hvordan had he attempted to remedy this state of comparative ignorance?

Variously. By leaving in a conspicuous place a certain book open at a
certain page: by assuming in her, da alluding explanatorily, latent
knowledge: by open ridicule in her presence of nogle absent other’s
ignorant lapse.
med hvad success had he attempted direct instruction?

She followed ikke alle, a part af den whole, gave attention med interest
comprehended med surprise, med care repeated, med greater difficulty
remembered, forgot med ease, med misgiving reremembered, rerepeated
med error.
hvad system had proved mere effective?
Indirect suggestion implicating selfinterest.
Example?

She disliked umbrella med regn, he liked kvinde med umbrella, she
disliked ny hat med regn, he liked kvinde med ny hat, he bought ny
hat med regn, she carried umbrella med ny hat.

Accepting the analogy implied in his guest’s parable which examples of
postexilic eminence did he adduce?

Three seekers af den pure truth, Moses of Egypt, Moses Maimonides,
author of _More Nebukim_ (Guide af den Perplexed) og Moses Mendelssohn
of such eminence that fra Moses (of Egypt) to Moses (Mendelssohn)
der arose none som Moses (Maimonides).

hvad statement was made, under correction, by Bloom concerning a fourth
seeker of pure truth, by name Aristotle, mentioned, med permission, by
Stephen?

That the seeker mentioned had been a pupil of a rabbinical philosopher,
name uncertain.

Were other anapocryphal illustrious sons af den law og children of a
selected eller rejected race mentioned?

Felix Bartholdy Mendelssohn (composer), Baruch Spinoza (philosopher),
Mendoza (pugilist), Ferdinand Lassalle (reformer, duellist).

hvad fragments of verse fra den ancient Hebrew og ancient Irish
languages were cited med modulations of stemme og translation of texts
by guest to host og by host to guest?

By Stephen: _suil, suil, suil arun, suil go siocair agus suil go cuin_
(walk, walk, walk your way, walk in safety, walk med care).

By Bloom: _Kifeloch, harimon rakatejch m’baad l’zamatejch_ (thy temple
amid thy hair is as a slice of pomegranate).

hvordan was a glyphic comparison af den phonic symbols of both languages
made in substantiation af den oral comparison?

By juxtaposition. på den penultimate blank page of a book of inferior
literary style, entituled _Sweets of Sin_ (produced by Bloom og so
manipulated that its front cover came in contact med den surface of
the table) med a pencil (supplied by Stephen) Stephen wrote the Irish
characters for gee, eh, dee, em, simple og modified, og Bloom in turn
wrote the Hebrew characters ghimel, aleph, daleth og (i den absence
of mem) a substituted qoph, explaining their arithmetical values as
ordinal og cardinal numbers, videlicet 3, 1, 4, og 100.

Was the knowledge possessed by both of each of these languages, the
extinct og the revived, theoretical eller practical?

Theoretical, being confined to certain grammatical rules of accidence
og syntax og practically excluding vocabulary.

hvad points of contact existed between these languages og between the
peoples hvem spoke them?

The presence of guttural sounds, diacritic aspirations, epenthetic og
servile letters in both languages: their antiquity, both having been
taught på den plain of Shinar 242 years efter the deluge i den
seminary instituted by Fenius Farsaigh, descendant of Noah, progenitor
of Israel, og ascendant of Heber og Heremon, progenitors of Ireland:
their archaeological, genealogical, hagiographical, exegetical,
homiletic, toponomastic, historical og religious literatures
comprising the works of rabbis og culdees, Torah, Talmud (Mischna og
Ghemara), Massor, Pentateuch, Book af den Dun Cow, Book of Ballymote,
Garland of Howth, Book of Kells: their dispersal, persecution, survival
og revival: the isolation of their synagogical og ecclesiastical
rites in ghetto (S. Mary’s Abbey) og masshouse (Adam og Eve’s
tavern): the proscription of their national costumes in penal laws og
jewish dress acts: the restoration in Chanah David of Zion og the
possibility of Irish political autonomy eller devolution.

hvad anthem did Bloom chant partially in anticipation of that multiple,
ethnically irreducible consummation?

Kolod balejwaw pnimah
     Nefesch, jehudi, homijah.
hvorfor was the chant arrested ved den conclusion of this first distich?
In consequence of defective mnemotechnic.
hvordan did the chanter compensate for this deficiency?
By a periphrastic version af den general text.
In hvad common study did their mutual reflections merge?

The increasing simplification traceable fra den Egyptian epigraphic
hieroglyphs til den Greek og Roman alphabets og the anticipation of
modern stenography og telegraphic code i den cuneiform inscriptions
(Semitic) og the virgular quinquecostate ogham writing (Celtic).
Did the guest comply med his host’s request?
Doubly, by appending his signature in Irish og Roman characters.
hvad was Stephen’s auditive sensation?

He heard in a profound ancient male unfamiliar melody the accumulation
af den past.
hvad was Bloom’s visual sensation?

han så in a quick young male familiar form the predestination of a
future.

hvad were Stephen’s og Bloom’s quasisimultaneous volitional
quasisensations of concealed identities?

Visually, Stephen’s: The traditional figure of hypostasis, depicted by
Johannes Damascenus, Lentulus Romanus og Epiphanius Monachus as
leucodermic, sesquipedalian med winedark hair.

Auditively, Bloom’s: The traditional accent af den ecstasy of
catastrophe.

hvad future careers had been possible for Bloom i den past og med
hvad exemplars?

i den church, Roman, Anglican eller Nonconformist: exemplars, the meget
reverend John Conmee S. J., the reverend T. Salmon, D. D., provost of
Trinity college, Dr Alexander J. Dowie. ved den bar, English eller Irish:
exemplars, Seymour Bushe, K. C., Rufus Isaacs, K. C. på den stage,
modern eller Shakespearean: exemplars, Charles Wyndham, high comedian,
Osmond Tearle († 1901), exponent of Shakespeare.

Did the host encourage his guest to chant in a modulated stemme a
strange legend on an allied theme?

Reassuringly, their place, hvor none could hear them talk, being
secluded, reassured, the decocted beverages, allowing for subsolid
residual sediment of a mechanical mixture, vand plus sugar plus cream
plus cocoa, having been consumed.
Recite the first (major) part of this chanted legend.

lille Harry Hughes og his schoolfellows alle
     Went ud for to play ball.
     og the meget first ball lille Harry Hughes played
     He drove it o’er the jew’s garden wall.
     og the meget second ball lille Harry Hughes played
     He broke the jew’s windows alle.
